Lawmakers have also warned banks, port authorities and fuel distributors that handling the imports could expose them to civil or criminal liability, as well as future congressional investigations.

The Trump administration claims the exemption is lawful, and no court has ruled on the dispute.

“It’s clear there’s hesitancy here in bringing these barrels onshore just because of the implications of doing so,” Matt Smith, an analyst at Kpler, told AP.

Where will the diesel go now?

Probably not to the US, experts say.

The first two diverted tankers are heading towards Brazil and the Mediterranean, according to Kpler data, and the third tanker could follow.

“Because of regulatory [and] sanctions concerns, we may not see this cargo discharge on the US Atlantic coast,” Smith told AP.

Moscow, however, insists the deal is on track.

Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said “all the diesel will find its buyers.”

Putin’s special envoy, Kirill Dmitriev, went further, writing on X that the reports were “fake” and “tankers destined for the US continue on course.”

World.title: Qeshm island and Hormuz hit, as mediators try to prevent US-Iran escalation
World.content:
US strikes have continued on Iran after more ships in the Strait of Hormuz were attacked.

Tehran, Iran – The United States has bombed Iran after vessels were targeted in the Strait of Hormuz, as mediators continue to try to prevent large-scale fighting between the two countries.

Two projectiles hit Iran’s Qeshm on Friday night, the latest in a series of air strikes on the southern island over recent weeks targeting Iranian air defences and launchers. President Donald Trump called them “minor strikes”, amid increasing concerns of a potential escalation in the war between the countries.

Iran’s army said in the early hours of Saturday that it destroyed a US-made MQ-9 drone using an unnamed new system. The Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) separately claimed on Friday that its air defences intercepted an MQ-1, reportedly the 16th aircraft of this model to be destroyed since the start of the war.

At least 11 ships were attacked in and around the Strait of Hormuz over the week ending on November 6, according to the United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations (UKMTO), which said three of them sank. The Western military intelligence agency has recorded 88 projectile strikes since hostilities resumed in early July, although it has cautioned that most attacks are going unreported.

UKMTO’s weekly report also identified 170 outbound and 155 inbound transits in the Strait of Hormuz, approximately 65 percent below pre-conflict levels. Most of the vessels that travel with their transponders switched on are using the Iranian route to the north. But many ships are still attempting the southern route near Oman with their tracking systems offline to shuttle oil out of the waterway.



Iranian armed forces also claim that, in addition to being hit with missiles and drones, tankers and commercial vessels using “unauthorised” routes also run the risk of being hit by naval mines.

The Iranian military’s naval force said on Saturday that a tanker with its transponder turned off caught fire in the eastern area of the Strait of Hormuz after hitting a mine. Washington says the mines have been cleared.

No range limit on missiles

For years, the IRGC maintained that it was limiting the range of its ballistic missiles to about 2,000 kilometres (1,240 miles) to reassure European countries that they would not be targeted.

But with Trump threatening to resume extensive air strikes on Iran’s civilian infrastructure, commanders say nothing is off limits now.

“This limitation has been lifted for us,” IRGC spokesman Hossein Mohebbi told reporters during an event on Saturday, in reference to missile range constraints.

His comments came after Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei ordered an unrestrained military response to any future threats from Israel and the US. Iran’s aerospace division of the IRGC has prepared “surprising defence achievements” that will be deployed in action if another wave of major attacks starts, he added.

“The operational unveiling of these [advanced] achievements in case of new conflict will not only frustrate and fascinate enemies, but will further solidify Iran’s military authority on the global stage, make the resistance front happy, and fully neutralise aggressors’ calculations,” Mohebbi said.

The spokesman said the IRGC plans to unveil another underground “missile city” soon, and will deploy some combat systems to public spaces so the people can personally inspect them.

Mohebbi added that if the Islamic republic decides to alter its nuclear doctrine and build a bomb, the necessary preparations will be made.

On state television’s war-focused Be Vaght-e Iran (At Iran’s Time) programme over the weekend, presenters and analysts said Iranian armed forces had their fingers on the trigger and were especially eyeing any movement from Israel.

“Our military information about the strategic chokepoints of Israel is complete. If our water, electricity and natural gas is cut off, they will also be plunged into darkness and lack of water,” one analyst said. “This is not a bluff, but a serious warning.”

‘Pendulum swing between war and talks’

Over recent weeks, diplomatic efforts by mediators to avoid attacks that could damage the entire region have picked up, although with limited gains.



Iran’s Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said on Saturday that he held talks with 12 foreign ministers over the past 48 hours, including top diplomats from Oman, Qatar, Saudi Arabia and Pakistan.

He said he explained the “fundamental positions” of Tehran, including the seven demands to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, and stressed the need to form “regional security arrangements without the interference of superregional powers”.

Security chief Mohsen Rezaei reportedly emphasised the same conditions to Russian President Vladimir Putin during a visit to Moscow on Thursday, which was also aimed at delivering a message from Khamenei.

Developments between Iran and the US resemble a “constant pendulum swing between war and negotiations” that is increasingly leaning towards conflict, according to political analyst Mostafa Najafi, who is said to be close to Iran’s security chief.

“What is clear for now is that the movement of this pendulum will continue; a conflict whose ending is much more complicated and time-consuming than imagined,” he wrote on X. The historic defeat for Trump and the Republicans in US midterm elections this week may further complicate the picture, he added.

Trita Parsi, executive vice president of the Quincy Institute for Responsible Statecraft, said three factors increase the risk of war in the short term after the elections, unless negotiations lead to a breakthrough.

The political cost of high fuel prices, brought about largely due to the war on Iran, has already been paid, he said, and there won’t be another point on the political calendar soon for Trump to worry about this issue.

“On the one hand, the pressure to get a deal will dissipate,” he told Al Jazeera.

Pressure from pro-war hawks will also escalate significantly because they will be constrained in their efforts to step up the conflict after the Democrats take control of Congress in early January. The appointment of far-right, pro-Israel hawk Stephen Miller as chief of staff also hints that Trump might not be ready to wind down the war.

“Finally, there is a new psychological element to Trump’s mindset following this humiliation: Trump’s desire for vengeance. There has been a vindictive element to his calculations in the past weeks because of his anger over how Iran – in Trump’s mind – has ruined his presidency,” Parsi said.

World.title: Dozens killed as humanitarian crisis mounts in Yemen: What next for war?
World.content:
Government forces reclaim key territories in Taiz and Lahij but face setbacks under Houthi resistance in certain areas.

Share Dozens killed as humanitarian crisis mounts in Yemen: What next for war? on social media

Dozens were killed in Yemen on Friday when a missile struck a market in Taiz governorate, with each side of Yemen’s brutal war blaming the other for the attack.

It has been a month since Yemen’s internationally recognised government launched its “Dawn of Yemen” offensive on the Iran-aligned Houthi rebel group after it took swaths of territory along the country’s Red Sea coast.

As the fighting continues, the humanitarian crisis is only intensifying, with hundreds of thousands displaced so far.

Yemen’s Presidential Leadership Council has said the government will continue with its “irreversible” drive to dismantle Houthi military capacity and restore sovereignty, meaning the war may get worse before there is any resolution, observers say.

Here’s what we know.

What is Operation Dawn of Yemen?

The operation was launched by the head of the Presidential Leadership Council of Yemen’s internationally recognised government, Rashad al-Alimi, on October 5.

Its aim is to recapture areas under Houthi control and liberate the capital city of Sanaa, which has been under the rebels’ control since September 2014.

The operation has relied on air support from the Saudi-led coalition, as well as ground operations carried out by government military coalitions and units to weaken the Houthis’ military capabilities.

In the Red Sea corridor, breaking the Houthis’ maritime chokehold and securing the Bab al-Mandeb strait has been an essential goal after the group captured the strategic port city of Mocha (Mokha) in September.

How much territory have the government forces taken back?

After launching the operation, the government said its forces recaptured positions around Dhubab and Bab al-Mandeb the same day, though the extent of their gains could not be confirmed.



It also said they captured mountain positions in Haifan, western Taiz and around al-Waziiya.

By October 13, fighting spread to Marib, where the government forces claimed gains around the Maas camp and north of Harib.

It did, however, lose territory in Taiz governorate, which led to a Houthi siege that continues to suffocate the city as it reaches its first month.

On Friday, the government forces said they had recaptured many areas in the governorate, including al-Nidani village, Shaab al-Sarari, large parts of the Sanamat area and the Ribat al-Qarn area in Dhi al-Barh in Taiz governorate.

Government troops and coalition fighters also secured the Tavat Wathib and Habil al-Saram hills along the Al-Aqroud front.

They announced the execution of 1,211 operations against Houthi positions on the different battlefronts, as they confirmed control over new positions on the Tur al-Bahah front in the Lahij governorate.

However, government forces are far from being able to take back Yemen’s capital, Sanaa, Thomas Bonnie James, an assistant professor in politics and international relations at Aberdeen University in the United Kingdom, told Al Jazeera.

“[Defeat] won’t happen if it means taking back Sanaa and ending Houthi rule. Not any time soon,” he said. “The government’s forces look big on paper, but they are spread across too many fronts and use old equipment.

“Sanaa is surrounded by mountains, which makes it easy to defend. A much stronger Saudi-Emirati coalition tried from 2015 and never came close,” he explained.

What else has the government achieved since the operation began?

James told Al Jazeera that Dawn of Yemen’s aim is to apply pressure to, rather than achieve the total defeat of, the Houthis.

“Dawn of Yemen is better understood as a way to apply pressure than as a bid for total victory,” he said. “The aim is to make the war more costly for the Houthis and to give Saudi Arabia a stronger position before any peace deal.

“What happens in the next three months matters more than the slogans.”

The Yemeni Presidential Leadership Council announced on Thursday that the armed forces have carried out 40,761 military operations since the beginning of Dawn of Yemen.

The council also said the attacks resulted in the “neutralisation” of about 20,000 Houthi leaders and elements, and more than 5,000 vehicles.

Previous announcements from the military command said they conducted 17,000 targeting operations during their first weeks and daily figures ranging between 951 and 1,272 operations throughout the month.



Last month, the Yemeni government also said its forces were able to kill or wound 1,540 Houthis in 24 hours.

Last week, the government said 16,100 Houthi operatives and commanders had been killed or wounded since October 5.

The Houthis did say that the total number of attacks the group has been subjected to since the beginning of the escalation reached 3,930 raids and missiles up until early November.

Al Jazeera has not been able to verify these figures.

How are the Houthis striking back?

The Houthis, who are also known as Ansar Allah (Arabic for Supporters of God), have caused hundreds of casualties since the beginning of the escalation.

Yemen’s government forces have blamed the Houthis for an attack on the al-Hadara market on Friday in the Taiz governorate that killed and injured dozens, mostly civilians.

Government military spokesperson, Colonel Majed al-Nazili, said the “terrorist” Houthis hit the market with ballistic missiles, calling it a war crime.

The Iran-backed Houthis rejected the accusation and said Saudi Arabia, which backs the Yemeni government, was responsible for the attack.

After taking the capital and state institutions in 2014, the Houthis have had access to a large number of weapons that once belonged to the Yemeni military.

Analysts say with the external support from Iran and their reliance on international black markets, the Houthis’ military capabilities continued to advance.

Their increasingly long-range missile strikes have allowed them to reach many areas across Saudi Arabia and even Israel in June.

One of the Houthis’ latest deadly attacks killed at least 70 government security recruits in Shabwah.

How is this affecting people in Yemen?

As the government and the Houthis continue fighting, the humanitarian situation in Yemen is heading towards catastrophe.

More than 323,000 people have been displaced in Yemen since the escalation began in August, with Taiz governorate taking in most of them, the United Nations Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA) reported on Friday.

More than two in five of the internally displaced in Yemen are in Taiz, where the Houthi blockade continues to encircle the city, cutting off supplies to about 800,000 people.

The UN Human Rights Office has reported 281 civilian casualties since August, with 69 people killed and 212 injured. Children make up more than one-third of casualties.

In Taiz, Salah Ahmed Ghaleb al-Majidi, acting director of the governorate’s Siege Affairs Department, described the situation to Al Jazeera as “catastrophic”.

Essentials, including medical supplies, food, fuel and water, are unable to reach the governorate due to the Houthi blockade.

An Al Jazeera report found that the remaining diesel stocks in the city have dwindled and have less than 48 hours left to run.

Hospitals are warning that once they run out of fuel, departments and medical centres will have to shut down, including emergency services.

Taiz’s deputy governor for health affairs, Ilan Abdul Haw, told Al Jazeera that about 40 percent of hospitals have closed, while those still open are operating at 50 percent capacity due to the lack of fuel.

What next for this war?

James told Al Jazeera that as the winter approaches in Yemen, and the siege on Taiz tightens, conditions will only worsen for Yemenis caught in the conflict.



“The biggest worry is the people of Taiz. More than 800,000 of them have been cut off from aid since the Houthis surrounded the city in early October,” he said. “Winter is coming, aid money is short, and the city is under siege. That is what more fighting will mean for ordinary Yemenis.”

The war has also spread beyond Yemen, as the Houthis continue strikes on Saudi airports and oil sites.

“The Houthis are firing at Saudi almost every day. Saudi Arabia is now openly bombing inside Yemen again for the first time since 2022,” James said. “Both sides are hitting where it hurts most, and that is how wars get bigger”.

Other fighting in the region could also pull Yemen into a wider war, and vice versa, as the US-Israel war on Iran remains in a deadlock, James told Al Jazeera.

“Yemen is now tied to the wider conflict with Iran. If the US strikes Iran again, Iran will want to use the Houthis to put more pressure on Saudi Arabia,” he said.

World.title: Nepal’s fight to rebuild after flood disaster
World.content:
101 East reveals Nepal’s efforts to save lives and rebuild communities after a devastating natural disaster.

On the morning of August 26, 2026, a devastating flash flood of rock and ice thundered from a high Himalayan mountain through Nepal’s valleys, sweeping away homes, villages and bridges.

At least 1,400 people were killed and more than 5,000 people remain missing.

It was the latest in a series of natural disasters that have battered Nepal in recent years as climate change accelerates.

This programme follows the rescuers risking their lives to search for the missing and those providing aid and refuge for traumatised children and families.

101 East reveals Nepal’s efforts to save lives and rebuild communities after a deadly natural disaster.

World.title: Rains flood 70,000 displaced families’ tents in Gaza
World.content:
Initial losses are estimated at about $3m, according to Gaza’s Government Media Office.

About 70,000 tents sheltering displaced Palestinians have been flooded in the Gaza Strip within 12 hours of the first winter storm of the season, according to Gaza’s Government Media Office.

In a statement on Saturday, the office said initial losses were estimated at about $3m. Dozens of walls had collapsed and people had been injured, it said, while cracked buildings at risk of collapse posed a growing danger.

The office held Israel “fully responsible” for what it called a disaster caused by the continued closure of crossings and the blocking of shelter and reconstruction materials. It urged the international community and UN agencies to intervene immediately to protect the displaced.

Gaza’s civil defence agency said its crews received about 1,500 distress calls in just 10 hours after the rain began early on Saturday, with water levels in several shelter sites rising by 30-40cm (12-16 inches).

“What we feared has actually happened,” civil defence spokesman Mahmoud Basal told Al Jazeera. “A few shelter centres were completely flooded, and everyone inside them has now been forced out into the unknown.”

Basal said premature babies, the elderly and the sick were most at risk. “Those living in tents are at risk of death at any moment, and of illness at any moment,” he said.

The storm also brought down buildings damaged in Israel’s genocidal war on the enclave that began in October 2023.



The civil defence agency said rescuers had evacuated residents of a building in the central Nuseirat area that partially collapsed in the strong winds and rain. In northern Gaza, the wall of a separate building fell down due to heavy rainfall, injuring two people, according to the Palestinian news agency Wafa.

Footage from camps in Gaza City, Khan Younis and Deir el-Balah showed families wading through ankle-deep water, mattresses and blankets soaked, and children standing barefoot in pools of mud and sewage.

“Even houses can’t hold up against this rain, so how can open plastic sheeting?” said Al Jazeera’s Nour Khaled, reporting from a camp in Gaza City. She said more than 28,000 widows were among those facing the winter alone with their children.

In al-Mawasi, the coastal area where more than 900,000 displaced people are sheltering in southern Gaza, rain had been falling since 10pm (20:00 GMT) on Friday, Al Jazeera’s Rami Abu Taima reported from Khan Younis.

“People woke up to find hundreds, even thousands, of tents flooded across the Gaza Strip,” he said. He added that more than 125,000 families living along the coast were at particular risk of having their tents swept away by the sea.

Gaza’s emergency committee said more than one million displaced people face a harsh winter, and that the territory urgently needs about 200,000 tents along with heating supplies.

Raed al-Dahshan, director of civil defence in Gaza, told Al Jazeera that crews could do little once they reached flooded families. “Civil defence does not have a single tarpaulin or a single tent,” he said. “We deal only with saving lives, and that is not enough.”

Aid groups blame Israeli restrictions on the entry of shelter materials.

The storm also hit Gaza’s battered health system. Mohammed Abu Salmiya, director of al-Shifa Medical Complex in Gaza City, told Al Jazeera that the hospital’s emergency department flooded and was out of service for about four hours. He warned of a rise in gastrointestinal, respiratory and skin infections as sewage mixed with rainwater inside tents.

“We will see many deaths, in the dozens and perhaps the hundreds, among newborns who need warmth in these tents,” he said.

Reporting from Gaza City port, Al Jazeera’s Ghazi al-Aloul said thousands of families had pitched tents along the shoreline, where they face strong winds and rising tides. “These tents will flood first from the rain, and second from seawater,” he said.

Many of the tents were put up in the first year of displacement and are now in their fourth, patched and re-stitched by their owners. Under the ceasefire’s humanitarian protocol, they were supposed to be replaced with caravans, which Israel has not allowed into the territory.



One displaced man on the beach told Al Jazeera: “They pushed us west towards the sea. Why don’t they just throw us into the sea and be done with it?”

Mohammed Salha, director of the Palestinian NGO Network, told Al Jazeera that only 180 to 200 trucks were entering Gaza daily, far short of the 600 agreed under the humanitarian protocol of the “ceasefire”, and that only about 40 of those carried humanitarian aid.

“We don’t want to respond after the tents flood,” Salha said, adding that 50,000 tents had been waiting on the Egyptian side of the border. “We must respond before the disaster happens.”

He described international pressure on Israel to allow in more supplies as “timid”.

World.title: India beat New Zealand by four runs via DLS in rain-hit second ODI
World.content:
Put in to bat, New Zealand struggled to gain any momentum as ⁠India’s pace attack dismantled their batting lineup.

Share India beat New Zealand by four runs via DLS in rain-hit second ODI on social media

India’s seam bowlers thrived in helpful conditions for a second straight one-day international as they beat New Zealand by four runs on Saturday to take a 2-0 series lead.

New Zealand were unable to defend their total of 134, with wet conditions in Wellington having reduced game two to a maximum of 47 overs each and made batting conditions treacherous.

India were 113-7 off 26 overs when rain ended play, four runs ahead of the Duckworth-Lewis-Stern par score of 109.

KL Rahul was at the crease on 26 and Auqib Nabi on one, with the pair having done just enough to put the tourists in front.

They require one more win to wrap up the five-match series, heading into game three in Hamilton on Tuesday.

India won the rain-hit opener in Auckland on Wednesday by five wickets when the home side were skittled for 185.

They were never comfortable in their Wellington chase, rocked onto the back foot when New Zealand seamer Jacob Duffy (3-35) dismissed Indian captain Shubman Gill for a golden duck and Virat Kohli for seven.

Paceman Kyle Jamieson (3-35) made a key breakthrough by removing top-scorer Shreyas Iyer for 30, leaving the chase teetering at 86-5.

New Zealand were all out in 41 overs, led by a watchful 55 from Daryl Mitchell and 31 from captain Mitchell Santner.

No other home batsman scored more than 11, many of them undone by unpredictable bounce and tight Indian seam bowling.



Gurnoor Brar produced his best ODI figures of 4-30, making a key double-strike in the 20th over when he removed Tom Latham and Glenn Phillips cheaply to leave New Zealand 53-5.

Earlier, Auqib Nabi claimed his first two international wickets, taking openers Will Young and Tim Seifert to finish with 2-31.

World.title: With Stephen Miller pick, Trump readies for a battle
World.content:
In the aftermath of the Republican Party's sweeping defeat in Tuesday's midterm elections, Donald Trump said he would be willing to work with the newly ascendent Democrats in Congress.

On Friday, however, he elevated Stephen Miller, his bare-knuckled political operative and longtime adviser, to replace Susie Wiles as White House chief of staff.

Far from an olive branch to Congress, Miller's promotion could be a sign that the president is girding for political battle by installing a partisan firebrand in the top White House job.

"The mission now is more clear than ever: Fight with all of our soul to support our president and defend this magnificent republic," Miller posted on X, adding that he was "honored beyond words" to be Trump's pick for the job.

One of the most powerful positions in Washington, the chief of staff is gatekeeper to the president, agenda-setter in the White House and chief negotiator with Congress and other outside political interests.

"Stephen Miller's been with me since the beginning," Trump said in comments to reporters after announcing the move on his Truth Social website. "He gets it."

World.title: Paraguay's president impeached and under house arrest after bank collapse
World.content:
Paraguay's President Santiago PeÃ±a has been impeached and placed under house arrest after a bank collapse triggered a crisis that left more than half of the country's population without access to their accounts.

PeÃ±a was arrested on Friday minutes after lawmakers, including from his own party, unanimously voted to remove him from office following the collapse earlier this week of Ueno Bank, which has links to his private business interests.

He had offered to step down on Thursday. Rather than accept his resignation, senators impeached PeÃ±a and charged him with misconduct, meaning he has been stripped of the immunity usually granted to ex-presidents.

PeÃ±a, who until last year held shares in the company that owned the bank, has denied any wrongdoing.

The impeachment charges that led to PeÃ±a's removal alleged he had conflicts of interest, manipulated regulatory oversight, diverted pension funds, and participated in an institutional cover-up involving the central bank.

He is due to be questioned on Saturday over allegations of breach of trust, influence peddling, and misappropriation of funds, prosecutor Silvia Margarita Gonzalez Vester said.

PeÃ±a's deputy, Pedro Alliana, has been sworn in as the new interim president and promised not to "abandon" the millions of people affected by the scandal.

"Compatriots who are now going through a difficult time as a result of the financial collapse will be fully compensated," said Alliana, who will serve as president until 2028.

The demise of the digital bank left more than half of Paraguay's population without access to their savings after it was seized by Paraguay's central bank.

Long lines of people trying to withdraw money from Ueno branches snaked down the streets of the capital Asuncion on Tuesday and Wednesday.

An estimated three million depositors remain unable to access their savings and pensions, prompting public outrage particularly in the capital, AsunciÃ³n.

Protests erupted across the country in response, with thousands taking to the streets on Thursday to demand their money.

Earlier demonstrations featured clashes with the police, who used tear gas and water cannons on the crowd.

PeÃ±a's impeachment passed with 44 out of 45 senators voting in favour of it. One lawmaker was absent.

"It was never my intention to betray the trust you placed in me," PeÃ±a said in a video posted on X announcing his resignation, adding his priority was "the peace of mind of Paraguayans who entrusted their savings to our financial system".

Afterwards, senate president Basilio NÃºÃ±ez said PeÃ±a was found guilty of "dereliction of duty".

World.title: Ukraine's power network suffers further damage after fresh Russian strikes
World.content:
Overnight drone and ballistic missile attacks damaged Ukrainian energy infrastructure, President Volodymyr Zelenskyhas said, causing blackouts and disrupting water supplies.

Zelensky said 12 Ukrainian regions came under attack with the capital Kyiv hit hardest.

Nine people are reported to have been hurt across the country, including one child, in the wave of attacks that consisted of more than 30 ballistic missiles and over 170 drones.

The attacks come before Ukrainian and Russian delegations are due to take part in trilateral talks in Abu Dhabi next week.

Zelensky wrote on Telegram, external that Moscow was preparing for the talks by launching attacks on Ukraine's "critical infrastructure".

Temperatures are dropping in Ukraine, and parts of the country have had the first winter snow.

"The situation in the capital is difficult, with disruptions to electricity, water, and heating supplies. Residential buildings, the North Bridge, and a kindergarten have been damaged," Zelensky said.

"In the Kyiv region, there were strikes on substations that connect the Rivne and Khmelnytsky nuclear power plants to Kyiv and central Ukraine."

In his latest update, Kyiv's Mayor Vitali Klitschko said the city's water supply system is back to operating normally. He also said around 60% of the city's apartment buildings were connected to the heating system.

The energy minister, Denys Shmyhal, said there were power cuts in five regions but did not say how many homes were affected.

World.title: Pope in 'pretty good health' as he starts Latin America tour
World.content:
Pope Leo XIV has told reporters travelling with him to Latin America he is "in pretty good health", in his first comments on his condition since having surgery for lung cancer.

The Pope has arrived in Uruguay, the first stop of a 12-day tour which he is undertaking only three weeks after his operation.

The pontiff, 71, also said he was "very happy" to be able to make the trip which was thrown into doubt last month when doctors discovered a tumour during a routine scan.

The tour will cover Argentina and a much anticipated return to Peru, which the Vatican described as a "homecoming" as the Pope was based there for many years as a missionary, then a bishop.

"I must confess that, from the very first day, I never had any doubts; I was convinced that this journey had to go forward," the Pope told journalists on his plane to Uruguay.

"Thanks to the marvellous medical staff... I believe I am in quite good health," Pope Leo confirmed.

Last month's operation to remove a tumour was successful and his doctors say the cancer has not spread.

On Friday, he arrived in Monetevideo to a seafront lined with crowds shouting his name as his Popemobile passed.

In his first speech of the trip, the Pope said universal healthcare should be "accessible to everyone".

He told the crowd in Plaza Independencia the care he received made him think of the "many men and women who lack the means to obtain a timely diagnosis" or receive treatment.

He capped his day with a prayer at the Montevideo Cathedral.

Pope Leo will cover more than 20,000 miles on his sixth international tour.

On Sunday he will travel to Argentina, the homeland of his predecessor Pope Francis who did not return during his own papacy.

The Pope said his visit was about being near the people who were looking to the Church for a message of "hope".

World.title: AI stocks climb after trillions wiped from market values
World.content:
Shares in artificial intelligence and technology firms have recovered slightly from an enormous sell-off that wiped trillions of dollars off stock values.

The tech-heavy Nasdaq stock index closed in positive territory following a market rout that began in the US on Thursday before spilling over to Asian and European markets into Friday.

Investors had been selling off tech shares in part due to concerns the Democrat victory in the midterm elections would mean slower artificial intelligence development.

However the latest US employment figures added to a mixed picture for American markets on Friday morning, with an unexpectedly strong 165,000 jobs added to the economy in September.

On Thursday, businesses closely linked to artificial intelligence development took a hammering on stock markets, particularly chip and semiconductor makers.

But the Nasdaq Composite bounced back slightly on Friday, ending the day up 1.1%, partly reversing some of its 5.5% fall.

The S&P 500, which tracks the share prices of the largest publicly-traded US companies, closed up 0.3%, while the Dow Jones Industrial Average was flat through the day before ending slightly down 0.4%.

Companies that lost hundreds of billions in market value recovered some ground on Friday, including Nvidia, SpaceX and Tesla.

However, stock markets in Asia and Europe fared worse.

The Kospi in South Korea closed down 6% on Friday, with shares in chipmaker SK Hynix plunging more than 10%. European markets also fell, with the main indexes in Germany, France and Spain ending the day down.

In the UK, the FTSE 100, which tracks the largest companies on the London Stock Exchange, declined 1.01%.

In addition to the recent market volatility, UK traders were also digesting the latest Bank of England decision to raise interest rates and the signal that another rate rise could be on the cards to curb rising prices.

World.title: New wave of bomb threats hit European airlines
World.content:
While no link has been established between the threats against airlines and media outlets, the Irish government has warned it is a "likely coordinated campaign of disruption".

In a statement, it said: "Hoax threats such as these cause fear, distress and disruption to people going about their daily lives and activities; they achieve no positive purpose whatsoever. It is not known yet who is responsible for these threats, whether it is individuals or a centralised or co-ordinated effort.

Irish Prime Minister MicheÃ¡l Martin described the situation as "worrying" and added his government's first priority was the safety of the Irish public.

"Yesterday, there appeared to be coordinated efforts to disrupt air travel," he said.

Martin told RTÃ it was not yet known if the threats had come from individuals or if it was a "coordinated attack" but said they were being taken seriously.

Ireland is scheduled to host two high-profile European Union meetings in Dublin next week.

Broadcaster Sky confirmed it had received a security threat, hours after RTÃ had evacuated its building.

The broadcaster, which is owned by Comcast, said in a statement read by a presenter on its news channel that the broadcaster had "carried out a security assessment and reported the matter to the relevant authorities".

"The safety and security of our colleagues is our primary concern, and we are working closely with authorities to ensure our people and operations remain secure."

Friday's disruption comes after the Russian extremist group "Male State", named in this week's hoax bomb threats to Italian airports, denied any link to the false warnings.

Replying to the BBC Russian Service, an account on Telegram - one of several linked to the so-called "Male State" and its founder Vladislav Pozdnyakov - mocked any suggestion the group was involved in emailing the threats.

"What Male State? Where have you seen it? It hasn't existed for many years," the message on the channel reads. "If tomorrow they sign a [threat] letter, say, from Putin, will you then try to reach our president to ask your stupid question?"

World.title: Spain's rail authorities face European fraud probe after Urda rail disaster
World.content:
European Union prosecutors have begun investigating the possible misuse of EU funds meant for upgrading the Spanish railway line where a train crash killed 69 people last week.

Prosecutors backed by a special unit of Spain's Guardia Civil security force said they were conducting the inquiry at the offices of Adif rail infrastructure authority and rail safety agency AESF.

The 28 October accident on the Madrid-Seville high-speed line was one of the worst railway disasters in Europe this century.

It is the second EU fraud inquiry opened into Spain's railways this year, after 46 people were killed on the same line at Adamuz in January.

Last week, a train operated by state-owned operator Renfe ploughed into the back of a stationary train belonging to private Spanish company Iryo outside the village of Urda, around 130km (80 miles) south of Madrid.

The LZB communication system that monitors the position of trains had gone down, and the Renfe train had been given the all clear to start running at normal speed, even though the Iryo train ahead of it had been unable to restart.

The two accidents nine months apart on the same line have claimed 115 lives and dozens more injuries.

World.title: Kenyan doomsday cult leader given life sentence for murdering 191 people
World.content:
A Kenyan court has sentenced the leader of a doomsday cult, Paul Mackenzie, to 200 years in prison for murdering 191 people, all but one of them children.

Alongside 28 others, Mackenzie was found guilty of the murders for instructing members of his cult to starve their children to death so they could "meet Jesus".

Justice Diana Mochache said Mackenzie bore the "primary criminal culpability" for ordering his followers to fast to death, in one of the world's deadliest episodes of cult activity.

"The sentence is appropriate and just, to send an unmistakable message that such atrocities warrant the maximum penalties allowed by law," the judge added.

The self-styled pastor was arrested in 2023 after the discovery of more than 400 bodies in shallow graves in Shakahola forest near the Kenyan coast. The sprawling investigation into the cases shocked Kenya and drew international attention.

The court sentenced Mackenzie to 100 years in prison for homicide and another 100 years for offences related to starvation.

The sentences within each category will run concurrently, but the two sets will run consecutively, bringing his total prison term to 200 years.

Mackenzie also faces separate manslaughter and terrorism charges, which he denies.

Prosecutors had sought the death penalty, arguing that the scale and circumstances of the killings warranted the harshest punishment.

However, Justice Mochache declined to impose the death penalty, despite ruling that the case met the threshold for its consideration.

"Nevertheless, the court declines the invitation to impose the death penalty on any of the victims," she said, adding that capital punishment would eliminate any prospect of rehabilitation and disengagement. The death sentence has not been carried out in Kenya since 1987.

Mackenzie was tried alongside 28 accomplices, including guards who enforced his fasting orders and gravediggers who helped conceal the victims' bodies in mass graves.

They received varying prison sentences of up to 160 years.

Justice Mochache described the killings as "cold and calculated", saying the perpetrators had shown no remorse and had even declared their willingness to fast to death themselves.

Before the hearing began on Friday morning, Francis Wanje, who lost eight relatives including two grandchildren in Shakahola forest, told the BBC's Newsday programme that he was "hoping for... a sentence which will match his [Mackenzie's] deeds in the forest".

Mackenzie and the co-accused had asked for leniency from the court.

Before their conviction on 19 October, they had all pleaded not guilty and repeatedly insisted that nobody was forced to die.

World.title: PT Health Watch: Blood grouping alone cannot guarantee safe transfusion, experts warn
World.content:
Blood transfusion can save lives, particularly in emergencies involving severe blood loss, childbirth complications, surgery and serious illnesses.

However, when donated blood is not properly screened and tested for compatibility, a procedure intended to save a patient’s life can expose them to potentially fatal complications.

While determining a donor’s blood group is an essential first step, medical laboratory scientists say it is not enough to establish whether the blood is safe for a recipient.

Adedoye David and Olaiya Oluwatoba, who are medical laboratory scientists, explained to PT HEALTH WATCH that donated blood must undergo additional laboratory tests, including crossmatching and screening for transfusion-transmissible infections, before it is released for transfusion.

According to the scientists, blood grouping establishes a person’s ABO and Rhesus (Rh) blood types, but does not independently confirm compatibility between a donor and recipient.

They explained that crossmatching involves testing donor and recipient blood samples to identify possible reactions between antigens on red blood cells and antibodies in the recipient’s blood. Such reactions can cause the destruction of red blood cells, resulting in potentially serious transfusion reactions.

The scientists also cautioned against the assumption that blood group O is automatically safe for every recipient. Although group O red blood cells are commonly used in emergencies when a patient’s blood group is unknown, some group O whole-blood donations contain high levels of anti-A and anti-B antibodies that can cause haemolysis in recipients.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Beyond compatibility, another important aspect of blood safety is ensuring that donated blood does not carry infections that could be transmitted to patients.

Screening for infections

The scientists identified hepatitis B, hepatitis C, human immunodeficiency virus (HIV 1 and 2) and syphilis as infections that must be screened for before donated blood is released.

They explained that inadequate screening could turn hospitals and blood banks into channels for transmitting infections to patients who may already be vulnerable because of their medical conditions.

They highlighted enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA) as a preferred screening method but noted that infections can sometimes escape detection when donors are in the window period, during which an infection is present but may not yet be detectable by a particular test.

Although ELISA is an established screening method, it does not completely eliminate this risk. Nucleic acid testing (NAT), where available, can detect some infections earlier by identifying viral genetic material.

Risks of incompatible or unsafe blood

According to the scientists, one major consequence of transfusing incompatible blood is a haemolytic transfusion reaction, which occurs when the recipient’s immune system destroys transfused red blood cells.

They identified acute and delayed haemolytic transfusion reactions as possible complications. Acute reactions may present with sudden fever, chills, low blood pressure and haemoglobinuria, while delayed reactions can develop days or weeks after transfusion.

Infections such as hepatitis B, hepatitis C, HIV and syphilis may also be transmitted through inadequately screened blood.

Although these complications can occasionally occur despite routine screening, the scientists said strict adherence to laboratory procedures and quality-control measures remains essential to reducing the risks.

Maintaining standards in blood banks

On the standards guiding blood bank operations, the scientists referred to the International Organisation for Standardisation’s ISO 15189, which outlines quality and competence requirements for medical laboratories.

They also highlighted external quality assessment, through which laboratories’ testing performance is evaluated, sometimes with the support of reference laboratories.

Acknowledging that hospitals may experience blood shortages, the scientists maintained that scarcity should not justify abandoning essential safety procedures. They said emergency release of blood before completion of all compatibility tests must follow established protocols, with appropriate authorisation and documentation.

They further explained that medical laboratory scientists are responsible for determining blood groups, conducting compatibility tests, screening donations for infections, checking packed cell volume (PCV), monitoring expiry dates and maintaining records of blood bank activities.

The scientists urged blood donors and patients’ relatives to ask questions about blood bank procedures, including donor eligibility requirements, haemoglobin levels, health conditions and infection screening.

They said greater communication between laboratory professionals, donors and patients’ relatives would improve public understanding of blood safety and strengthen confidence in transfusion services.

World.title: Rwandan author Lisa Munezero to unveil personal growth book in Lagos
World.content:
Rwandan author, entrepreneur and cultural advocate Lisa Adeline Munezero is set to unveil her new book, “The Well of Knowing: 8 Lessons of Becoming” in Lagos State on 14 November.

In a statement sent to PREMIUM TIMES on Saturday, Ms Munezero said the book launch will take place at Four Points by Sheraton, Victoria Island.

She said guests will attend the event by invitation.

The book explores eight interconnected lessons on knowledge, personal growth, purposeful living and the choices that shape individual success.

According to the former Miss Rwanda contestant, the book centres on the idea that how people apply their knowledge determines the opportunities they create and the individuals they eventually become.

Ms Munezero encourages readers to rethink conventional ideas of success by examining how self-awareness, resilience, discipline and intentional actions influence the course of their lives.

She draws on her entrepreneurial journey, personal experiences and practical insights to explore these themes.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

“Eight lessons”

The author further explained that the book challenges readers to reflect on how they find their purpose, respond to setbacks, turn ideas into viable opportunities and use knowledge to create lasting social impact.

Through eight lessons, she explores themes such as self-awareness, accountability, resilience, entrepreneurship, continuous learning and the transfer of knowledge between generations.

Ms Munezero argued that academic qualifications, ambition, and access to opportunities do not automatically translate into fulfilment.

According to her, individuals must also show adaptability, make sound decisions, and take deliberate steps toward their goals.

“Addressing students, aspiring entrepreneurs, professionals and emerging leaders, the book presents personal development as an ongoing journey.

“It also explores mentorship, relationships and responsible leadership as ways in which individual growth can benefit communities and future generations”, said the cultural advocate and dancer.

She said she draws on her entrepreneurial experience, cultural engagement and personal reflections in her writing.

Although the book draws on African experiences, it explores universal themes of identity, ambition, adversity and opportunity.

Professional endorsements

The publication has attracted positive reviews from individuals with backgrounds in literature and professional practice.

Isi Agboaye, founder of Step Out Creatives Publications in the United Kingdom and a dramatist, praised the book for encouraging readers to identify their purpose and translate their aspirations into action.

He compared its underlying philosophy to Norman Vincent Peale’s The Power of Positive Thinking.

Meanwhile, Aderonke Adeyinka, a banking executive and author of Threads of Love and Duty, described the book as a worthwhile read for aspiring business owners and those pursuing personal development.

She noted its focus on building resilience and embracing continuous learning.

Kenyan literary journalist, blogger and podcaster James Murua also acknowledged the book’s treatment of mentorship, community connections and the preservation of knowledge through successive generations.

The gathering will allow guests to interact directly with the author and discuss the experiences and perspectives that informed the publication.

World.title: MTN partners Omoni Oboli to unveil seven Christmas films on YouTube
World.content:
MTN Nigeria has partnered with filmmaker and actress Omoni Oboli to unveil seven Christmas films, in a collaboration aimed at expanding access to Nigerian content and supporting the country’s creative industry through digital distribution.

The films, produced under Omoni Oboli TV, were unveiled at a Christmas Movie Mixer hosted by MTN Nigeria at its rooftop facility in Lagos.

The event brought together filmmakers, actors, content creators, and other entertainment industry stakeholders to celebrate Nigerian storytelling and the upcoming festive season.

The unveiling was accompanied by a fireside chat featuring Oboli and Barene Jankovich-Besan, a YouTube consultant and independent strategic adviser. The session was moderated by Sir Kenn.

Speaking at the event, Idowu Adesokan, General Manager, Consumer Segments at MTN Nigeria, said the partnership reflected the telecommunications company’s commitment to supporting the creative economy and creating opportunities for Nigerian talent.

Mr Adesokan said the collaboration with Omoni Oboli TV, alongside MTN’s strategic partnership with YouTube, was part of efforts to connect audiences with locally produced content while helping creators expand their reach.

“At MTN, we recognise that connectivity goes beyond access to the internet. It enables creativity, innovation and economic opportunity. We believe Nigeria’s creative industry has enormous potential to entertain, create jobs, build businesses and take our stories to the world,” he said.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Omoni highlights affordable access

Omoni said the partnership would make it easier for audiences to watch her productions, particularly through MTN’s YouTube data bundles, which she said reduce streaming costs.

The Edo-born actress explained that affordability matters to filmmakers because wider access to their productions can translate into increased viewership and revenue.

“With MTN bundles, you can watch a whole film with just a few hundred naira. That makes me happy because I can tell my audience that we have a movie out, and they don’t have to break the bank to watch it,” she said.

The filmmaker also linked the commercial success of online productions to the livelihoods of people working in the industry, including actors and other production professionals.

According to her, increased viewership and advertising revenue create opportunities for creators to invest in more productions and employ additional talent.

“The more people watch, the more money the creators make, and the more money the creators make, the more people we can empower. I can have more actors in my films. So, I’m also empowering other people,” she said.

Describing filmmaking as a serious business, Omoni said several people’s livelihoods depended on the success of productions, adding that her work carried responsibilities beyond personal achievement.

“It’s not a joke. It’s serious business. There are people here who, all they want in life is their bread and water. That’s how their rent is paid. That’s how their kids eat.

“For me, I take it as almost ministry. It’s not just, ‘Oh, this is just something I do.’ It’s very serious because many destinies are tied to mine. So I must win,” she said.

YouTube speaks on Nigerian films’ global reach

Also speaking during the fireside chat, Jankovich-Besan highlighted the emotional appeal of Nollywood productions as one of the factors behind their popularity among audiences.

She said themes such as love, betrayal, romance and success often encourage viewers to engage with characters and discuss the decisions made in films, extending their impact beyond entertainment.

She also pointed to the growing international audience for Nigerian films, noting that viewers outside Africa were increasingly engaging with content produced on the continent.

Ms Jankovich-Besan said she had encountered figures suggesting that “between 30 and 40 per cent of the viewership of some movies came from audiences outside Africa.”

She described the development as an important indication of the potential of Nigerian storytelling to reach international audiences.

On the partnership between MTN and YouTube, she explained that promotional campaigns deliberately incorporated content from creators’ YouTube channels to direct more viewers to their platforms.

The YouTube consultant said the approach included displaying creators’ channel names in promotional materials, allowing interested viewers to locate and subscribe to their channels.

“We want to make sure that the channel name is there so we can drive traffic to the creator channels on YouTube. Ultimately, success for us would be if those channels keep growing and have more subscribers,” she said.

Ms Jankovich-Besan also identified affordability and access to suitable devices as some of the challenges affecting digital adoption in Nigeria.

Responding to a question about growing YouTube viewership in the country, she said the platform’s recommendation algorithm was influenced by users’ viewing habits and the interests of people with similar viewing patterns.

She added that creators could also contribute to the growth of their platforms by consistently encouraging audiences to like their videos and subscribe to their channels.

Seven films embrace Christmas themes

Speaking about the inspiration behind the Christmas productions, Omoni said the films were designed around the values associated with the festive season, including family, love, forgiveness, togetherness and connection.

She described Christmas as a period when people take a break from the demands of the year, reconnect with loved ones and reflect on their relationships.

“It’s a time for family. It’s a time for togetherness. It’s time for sharing. It’s a time for caring. It’s a time that we remind ourselves that we’re human,” she said.

The 48-year-old actress also disclosed that producing seven films for the festive season would have been more difficult without MTN’s support.

She described herself as a Christmas movie enthusiast who watches films throughout the festive period and said the opportunity to produce seven titles was an expansion of that passion.

The productions include Seasoned With Love, Christmas on Budget, Memories on the Rooftop, Promise Me December, A Bride for the Season, Christmas Between Worlds and Short Sweet 2.

During the discussion, Omoni indicated that she was also looking forward to major cinema projects in 2027, suggesting that her relationship with MTN could extend to future productions.

World.title: Buhari promised me APC Presidential ticket, put it in writing, but failed to honour it – Amaechi
World.content:
Former Rivers State Governor Rotimi Amaechi has alleged that the late President Muhammadu Buhari promised in writing to endorse him ahead of the All Progressives Congress (APC) presidential primary in 2022 but failed to honour the commitment.

Mr Amaechi, who finished second behind Bola Tinubu at the primary, said he relied on the assurance rather than negotiate political deals that could have strengthened his chances of securing the party’s nomination.

Speaking on Mainland 98.3 FM’s The Situation Room programme on Friday, the former transportation minister described his decision to trust Mr Buhari as his first mistake in the contest.

“The first mistake that I made at that primary was that I listened to President Buhari,” he said.

“He said to me, ‘Don’t campaign. Don’t do anything. I will announce you as my candidate.'”

Asked whether Mr Buhari had personally given him the assurance, Mr Amaechi said the former president had put it in writing.

“When I write my book, I will put it out,” he said.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Mr Amaechi, who was Mr Buhari’s campaign director-general in the 2015 and 2023 presidential elections, did not display the document or disclose when the alleged commitment was made.

Amaechi alleges religious mobilisation for Tinubu

Mr Amaechi also accused Mr Tinubu of benefiting from appeals to religious identity during the contest.

He alleged that a delegation of Yoruba Muslims met governors in the North-west and urged them to support Mr Tinubu because of their shared faith.

According to him, the delegation argued that southern Muslims had supported northern Muslim candidates in previous elections and expected similar backing.

“Tinubu played on religion. I won’t play religious politics. I will never,” Mr Amaechi said.

He also referred to former Kaduna State Governor Nasir El-Rufai, who supported Mr Tinubu’s presidential ambition.

Mr Amaechi claimed that Mr El-Rufai had publicly linked his support for Mr Tinubu to religious considerations.

He did not identify the members of the alleged delegation or provide evidence of its discussions with the governors.

Mr Amaechi said he would not adopt a similar strategy by asking Catholic leaders to direct members of the church to support his presidential ambition.

“I wouldn’t want to go to the Catholic Church and say, please announce me, tell them that all Catholics must go out and vote Amaechi,” he said.

He argued that political campaigns built around religious identity could create divisions among Nigerians.

The 2022 APC primary

Mr Tinubu defeated 13 other aspirants at the APC presidential primary held in Abuja in June 2022.

He polled 1,271 votes, while Mr Amaechi came second with 316 votes. Then Vice-President Yemi Osinbajo finished third with 235 votes.

The primary followed weeks of uncertainty over whether Mr Buhari would openly endorse a successor.

Mr Amaechi, who served as transportation minister under Mr Buhari, resigned from the cabinet to contest the party’s presidential nomination.

Although he said the late president had advised him not to campaign, he undertook consultations with delegates and political stakeholders before the primary.

He did not explain in the interview how those consultations differed from the campaigning he said Mr Buhari had discouraged.

Mr Tinubu subsequently won the February 2023 presidential election and succeeded Mr Buhari in May of that year.

World.title: TenTrade offers partners up to $10 per lot in referral rebates
World.content:
TenTrade has revealed that its introducing broker programme allows partners to earn trading rebates of up to $10 per lot from clients they refer to the financial trading platform.

Francis Chukwu, Business Development Manager at TenTrade, disclosed this while speaking at the company’s One Community, One Future 2026 event in Ikeja, Lagos, on Saturday.

Mr Chukwu said individuals who register as introducing brokers and bring traders onto the platform could earn commissions based on the trading activities of their referrals.

“If I introduce him, he’s a trader, and he signs up with my link, once he starts trading, TenTrade will pay you up to $10 per lot size,” he said.

He explained that the programme also allows partners to benefit from referrals made by people within their own networks, creating multiple levels of earnings.

According to him, partners can continue earning rebates from referred traders for as long as those traders remain active on the platform.

“As long as they keep trading, you keep earning. It’s not something you just earn and stop,” he said.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Mr Chukwu added that partners could earn up to 15 per cent on funded accounts referred to TenTrade, in addition to the trading rebates.

He also said the programme provides for earnings across as many as five referral levels, allowing partners to receive rebates from trading activities within their extended referral networks.

Describing the partnership programme, Mr Chukwu said his own experience of earning in dollars began through referrals rather than trading.

“When I started making money in dollars, it wasn’t through just trading. It was through partnership because I advertised TenTrade. All I did was use my mouth, refer to them,” he said.

World.title: TenTrade considers Nigerian office expansion, unveils trading incentives
World.content:
TenTrade has expressed plans to establish a second office in Nigeria, potentially in Abuja, as the financial trading company seeks to expand its presence in the country.

The company’s Chief Revenue Officer, Andreas Andreou, disclosed this during its ‘One Community, One Future 2026’ event in Ikeja, Lagos, on Saturday.

Mr Andreou said the company was considering opening another office outside Lagos, adding that TenTrade already has a presence in Nigeria, Ghana, Kenya, South Africa, Vietnam, Pakistan, Bangladesh and India.

“I’m more than confident, so we seem to also open up a second office here in Nigeria. Obviously, not in Lagos, we’ll probably be looking in Abuja or something like that,” Mr Andreou said.

He also announced a 20 per cent discount on all funded accounts, including TenEdge and TenExpress accounts, for traders on the platform.

Speaking at the event, Wilfred Obasi, TenTrade’s Regional Director for Africa, encouraged traders to reinvest their earnings and grow their capital through compounding.

He said traders should build their capital over time, adding that the company offers different account types to accommodate traders with varying needs.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Also speaking, Kehinde Shogeke, TenTrade’s Sales Team Lead, outlined the company’s bonus account offerings, including a 30 per cent starter bonus and a trading boost bonus advertised at up to 200 per cent.

World.title: Nigeria’s external debt up 6.6% to $145bn in 2025 – World Bank
World.content:
Nigeria’s total external debt stock rose to $145.02 billion in 2025, representing a 6.6 per cent increase from the previous year, according to the World Bank.

The private non-guaranteed and short-term obligations accounted for more than half of the country’s external debt.

This is contained in the World Bank’s International Debt Report 2026 showing that Nigeria’s external debt increased from $83.21 billion in 2015 to $145.015 billion in 2025, a 74.3 per cent increase in 10 years.

Nigeria’s profile showed that public and publicly guaranteed debt accounted for $62.4 billion of the total, while private non-guaranteed debt stood at $54.476 billion. Short-term external debt accounted for another $28.139 billion.

This implies that Nigeria’s external debt exposure extends beyond direct government borrowing to include obligations contracted by private entities without public guarantees and short-term liabilities.

Debt transparency concerns

The World Bank report warned that rising debt stocks and debt-servicing obligations were putting pressure on developing economies, even as international capital markets reopened to some borrowers.

It said external debt across low- and middle-income countries increased by 5.5 per cent to a record $9.4 trillion in 2025, the largest annual increase in four years.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

According to the report, the return to international capital markets had been uneven, with the poorest and most vulnerable countries facing borrowing costs not seen since the late 1980s.

In the report’s foreword, Haishan Fu, the Chief Statistician of the World Bank Group, said that the total debt-service burden of low- and middle-income countries had increased for a fifth consecutive year in 2025.

She said the rising debt-service burden was reducing the resources available for infrastructure, jobs, education, healthcare and other development priorities.

“Against this backdrop, knowing how much countries owe, to whom, and on what terms has never been more important. Without reliable and reconciled information, governments cannot manage debt effectively, creditors cannot assess risks accurately, and debt restructurings can become more difficult,” Ms Fu said.

The bank’s chief statistician said transparency was a shared responsibility requiring borrowers to maintain comprehensive and timely debt records, creditors to disclose information about their obligations and international institutions to strengthen reporting standards and debt-management systems.

“The message of this year’s report is clear: access to finance is not enough. We must know the debt, understand its terms, and ensure that the financing developing economies receive strengthens rather than constrains their ability to grow, withstand shocks, and improve the lives of their people,” she said.

Nigeria debt breakdown

A breakdown of Nigeria’s $62.4 billion in public and publicly guaranteed external debt showed that multilateral creditors accounted for $31.365 billion, bilateral creditors $6.683 billion and private creditors $24.352 billion.

The World Bank’s International Development Association (IDA) accounted for $18.533 billion of the multilateral debt, while International Monetary Fund credit and Special Drawing Rights allocations stood at $5.516 billion.

Also, other multilateral creditors accounted for $7.315 billion.

China was Nigeria’s largest bilateral creditor, with $5.672 billion, followed by France with $774 million, while other bilateral creditors accounted for $237 million.

Debt ratios

The report also showed that Nigeria’s external debt-to-exports ratio stood at 212 per cent in 2025, while external debt as a share of Gross National Income was 51 per cent.

Debt service accounted for 19 per cent of exports and five per cent of GNI during the year.

On the terms of new borrowing, the report put the average maturity of Nigeria’s 2025 commitments from official creditors at 25 years, with a five-year grace period and an interest rate of 1.9 per cent.

However, new commitments from private creditors carried an average maturity of 12 years, an eight-year grace period and an interest rate of 9.6 per cent.

The report also highlighted Nigeria’s return to international capital markets, noting that the country, the third-largest issuer in Sub-Saharan Africa, raised $2.3 billion through a dual-tranche international bond issue in 2025.

One tranche had a 10-year maturity and an interest rate of 8.625 per cent, while the second had a 20-year maturity and an interest rate of 9.125 per cent.

It further disclosed that Nigeria entered into a $5 billion Total Return Swap transaction in 2026, with a three-year maturity and collateralisation of approximately 133 per cent, equivalent to about $6.7 billion in domestic securities.

World.title: Saapade Accident: Ogun Crime Watch urges Police to invite Nollywood actor over alleged falsehood
World.content:
Ogun Crime Watch has called on the Nigeria Police Force to invite Nollywood actor, Kunle Afod, for questioning over what it described as the deliberate circulation of misleading information and misrepresentation of events surrounding Friday’s road accident at Saapade on the Lagos-Ibadan Expressway.

The group said the timing of the actor’s video, in which he reportedly questioned the emergency response to the accident, raised serious concerns about his intentions and suggested an attempt to mislead the public about the intervention of the Ogun State Government’s emergency response team.

In a statement signed by its President, Comrade Olumide Martin, the group disclosed that the state emergency response team arrived at the accident scene at 12:28 p.m., while Afod reportedly published his video at 12:29 p.m., barely one minute after the team’s arrival.

Ogun Crime Watch said the timeline raised questions about the actor’s claims and the circumstances surrounding the production and publication of the video, particularly when emergency responders were already at the scene attending to the victims.

It alleged that the video appeared calculated to create a negative impression about the government’s response, undermine public confidence in the emergency management system and advance a political narrative favourable to opposition interests.

The group further alleged that the actor’s intervention bore the imprint of partisan political communication, adding that public safety and the welfare of accident victims should never be exploited for political advantage or personal gain.

It therefore urged the police to investigate the circumstances surrounding the video, establish the facts and determine whether any laws were breached in the process of circulating potentially misleading information.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

The group emphasised that its position was not an attempt to prevent freedom of expression or legitimate criticism of government but a demand for responsibility, accuracy and accountability, especially when public statements concern emergencies involving human lives.

The accident involved a Mazda bus conveying 18 passengers, which reportedly suffered a tyre burst before crashing into a concrete barrier around the Saapade axis of the Lagos-Ibadan Expressway. Thirteen passengers sustained injuries and were evacuated to hospitals for medical attention.

Ogun Crime Watch commiserated with the victims and their families, wishing those receiving medical attention a speedy recovery.

It also urged motorists to observe speed limits, avoid dangerous driving, maintain their vehicles properly and comply with Federal Road Safety Corps regulations to reduce the incidence of preventable road accidents.

The group called on public figures and social media influencers to exercise restraint and verify information before publishing reports, noting that irresponsible commentary during emergencies could create unnecessary panic, mislead the public and diminish confidence in the work of emergency responders.

World.title: Makinde: Tinubu’s poor planning plunged millions of Nigerians into hardship
World.content:
By Christopher Ameh, Bauchi

Oyo State Governor and presidential candidate of the Allied Peoples Movement (APM), Seyi Makinde, has blamed the economic hardship facing millions of Nigerians on what he described as inadequate planning by the President Bola Tinubu-led administration.

Makinde said major economic policy decisions introduced by the Federal Government were implemented without adequate plans and frameworks to cushion their effects on citizens, thereby worsening the economic difficulties faced by Nigerians.

The APM presidential candidate spoke on Friday during a live interview on the Bauchi Radio Corporation (BRC), while in Bauchi State to flag off his 2027 presidential campaign.

He argued that the immediate impact of the administration’s economic policies on Nigerians was a consequence of taking major decisions without adequate preparation and effective implementation strategies.

Makinde stressed that economic reforms must be supported by proper planning and clear implementation frameworks to ensure that ordinary citizens do not bear the brunt of government policies.

He said addressing the country’s economic challenges would require fundamental structural reforms and strong political will.

The Oyo governor also highlighted the APM’s Reset Nigeria Agenda, which he said was designed to address the country’s challenges through a documented policy framework and the party’s manifesto.

According to him, the agenda focuses on reforming critical sectors of the economy, promoting sustainable development and restoring true federalism that recognises and respects Nigeria’s diverse nationalities.

World.title: NDC to Tinubu: Obi-Kwankwaso ticket targets erosion of Nigeria’s wealth
World.content:
The National Democratic Congress (NDC) has said its presidential candidate, Peter Obi, and running mate, Rabiu Musa Kwankwaso, are committed to addressing what it described as the erosion of Nigeria’s commonwealth through excessive borrowing and alleged poor management of public resources.

The party made the position known in a statement by the Spokesperson of its National Presidential Campaign Council, Dr Chiogo Constance Ikokwu, in reaction to President Bola Tinubu’s criticism of Obi over the erosion menace in Anambra State.

The NDC said the mission of the Obi-Kwankwaso ticket went beyond tackling environmental erosion in Anambra to addressing the country’s fiscal challenges, including rising public debt, inadequate budgetary funding and the management of revenues accruing from the removal of petrol subsidy.

It questioned the benefits Nigerians had received from subsidy removal, particularly in view of the Federal Government’s continued borrowing, increased revenue generation and the country’s debt-service-to-revenue ratio.

The party also expressed concern over what it described as inadequate funding of critical public services, particularly healthcare and education, despite increased government revenues.

It said the Obi-Kwankwaso ticket would prioritise prudent management of public resources, accountability, productive investments and improvements in citizens’ welfare.

To support its argument, the NDC cited the financial records of Obi and Tinubu during their respective tenures as governors of Anambra and Lagos states.

According to the party, Obi left behind investments valued at the equivalent of $500 million, alongside local and foreign currency assets, including $156 million in dollar-denominated bonds, when he left office in 2014.

It also cited figures from the Debt Management Office, which it said put Lagos State’s external debt at approximately $190.43 million at the end of 2007, when Tinubu left office.

The NDC further criticised the pension law enacted during Tinubu’s administration in Lagos, which provided lifetime benefits for former governors and their deputies.

It listed the benefits as pensions equivalent to 100 per cent of the incumbent governor’s basic salary, houses in Lagos and Abuja, vehicles, furniture and utility allowances, entertainment allowances, free medical care and provisions for domestic staff.

The party contrasted the Lagos arrangement with Anambra, claiming that Obi did not establish a pension scheme for former governors during his tenure.

On environmental erosion, the NDC defended Obi’s record in Anambra, saying he helped attract and launch the World Bank-assisted Nigeria Erosion and Watershed Management Project (NEWMAP).

It also said his administration introduced drainage requirements for new state roads, ensuring that drainage systems were connected to safe discharge points, while undertaking local flood-control projects in communities including Adazi Nnukwu, Amawbia and Umuoji.

The party added that Obi regularly engaged the Federal Government on the need for ecological intervention funds and accountability in their utilisation.

Describing excessive borrowing without corresponding economic benefits as a threat to the country’s financial stability, the NDC cited historical examples of countries that had experienced economic difficulties associated with unsustainable debt and poor fiscal management.

It warned that Nigeria could face similar challenges if the trend was not addressed.

The party said its proposed economic approach would focus on responsible borrowing, accountability and investments capable of creating opportunities for Nigerians and improving the welfare of future generations.

World.title: Obienyem faults Tinubu over claim Obi ignored erosion in Anambra
World.content:
Valentine Obienyem, a media aide to former Anambra State Governor Peter Obi, has faulted President Bola Tinubu over his claim that Obi did nothing to tackle erosion during his tenure as governor.

Obienyem, in an opinion article sent to Vanguard on Saturday, described the allegation as unfair and contradicted by historical records, citing several erosion-control projects undertaken by the former governor and his role in securing regional and international support to address the problem.

The reaction followed Tinubu’s visit to Akwa Ibom State, where he reportedly promised to develop the state’s deep seaport and accused Obi of failing to address erosion in Anambra during his administration.

Obienyem linked the development to Obi’s recent remarks on the need to develop seaports across Nigeria’s coastal states, including the Calabar Port and Ibom Deep Seaport.

He recalled that Obi had advocated the development of multiple ports across the country’s littoral states, citing Egypt, with about 15 ports, and South Africa, with about eight, as examples of countries that had diversified their maritime infrastructure to promote balanced economic development.

On the erosion challenge in Anambra, Obienyem said the state had more than 1,000 active erosion sites, including the devastating Nanka-Agulu erosion complex, but maintained that Obi gave the problem considerable attention while in office.

He cited two incidents to illustrate the former governor’s personal involvement in emergency interventions.

According to him, Obi once arrived at Umuchiani, Ekwulobia, as early as 6 a.m. after receiving reports of advancing erosion threatening the Ekwulobia-Oko road and nearby buildings.

He said some residents had begun dismantling parts of their houses to salvage their belongings before Obi intervened and directed that work should commence immediately.

Obienyem said the erosion was subsequently arrested and stabilised, saving the road and protecting the threatened buildings from further destruction.

He also recalled a similar intervention along the Nkpor-Onitsha dual carriageway, around the Omagba axis, where Obi reportedly responded to a distress call and helped prevent an endangered building from being swallowed by erosion.

Beyond the emergency interventions, Obienyem said Obi, as Chairman of the South-East Governors’ Forum, advocated declaring the region an ecological disaster zone to attract urgent government attention and international assistance.

He credited the former governor’s advocacy with helping to advance the Nigeria Erosion and Watershed Management Project (NEWMAP), a World Bank-assisted programme designed to tackle erosion and watershed degradation.

To support the claim, he cited the remarks of former Minister of Environment, John Odey, who reportedly acknowledged Obi’s contribution during the project’s official launch in Abuja.

According to Obienyem, Odey recalled that Obi had almost single-handedly pushed for the initiative despite initial reservations among some of his colleagues.

He also cited the commendation by the World Bank’s then Country Director, Marie-Françoise Marie-Nelly, who praised Obi for being the first governor to pay the state’s N500 million counterpart contribution to the programme.

The project covered Anambra, Imo, Ebonyi, Enugu, Abia, Edo and Cross River states.

Obienyem further claimed that Obi had worked on nearly 40 erosion-control and storm-water management sites across Anambra State before leaving office, with most completed and work continuing on others.

Among the locations he listed were Umuchiana, Ekwulobia; Mbaukwu; Mbanabo-Umuogba/Bishop Uzodike Road, Nnewichi, Nnewi; Umunze-Uga; Umudiana, Adazi-Nnukwu; Nsugbe; and Utu/Osumenyi in Nnewi South.
