World.title: 'Cat' Matlala to testify before Madlanga Commission on Monday and Tuesday
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - Alleged crime boss Vusimuzi “Cat” Matlala is expected to appear before the Madlanga Commission on Monday and Tuesday.

Matlala, who remains behind bars facing several criminal charges, is expected to be questioned about government tenders and alleged criminal networks.

The Commission aims to conclude Phase Two of its inquiry this month before moving on to Phase Three.

The next phase will include the return of KwaZulu-Natal Police Commissioner Nhlanhla Mkhwanazi to the witness stand.

The inquiry will then compile its final report, which is due to President Cyril Ramaphosa by 25 January 2027.

World.title: IEC processes hundreds of objections ahead of election results announcement
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - The Electoral Commission says it is working to ensure credible local government election results.

IEC officials are processing hundreds of election-related objections, including the MK Party’s call for an audit of the eThekwini results.

Voter turnout currently stands at 45 percent, while the commission says it has experienced no technical glitches during the week.

The IEC is expected to announce the results on Sunday, once all objections have been considered.

"I know that our voter turnout numbers are sitting at 45 percent. This is a very good number in terms of, you know, the checks and balances, the controls to say where you stay; that's exactly where you need to vote," said the IEC's Vusi Vuma.

"So we did not have any glitches technically, and we are looking forward to tomorrow when the commission will be announcing the results. At this point, we are currently busy with objections.

"The objections closed yesterday; we received hundreds of them, and it's part and parcel of the process. We're going to process each and every one of them, and make sure that, you know, by the time we announce the results, everyone is happy."

World.title: France braces for protests as Yellow Vests urge 'mass disobedience'
World.content:
PARIS - French unions and student groups are set to take to the streets for another day of protests on Saturday, while the Yellow Vests movement plans a separate rally in central Paris despite a ban by authorities.

The demonstrations follow weeks of youth-led unrest and nationwide strikes that drew hundreds of thousands of workers protesting over the rising cost of living.

They come less than six months before voters elect a new head of state to replace centrist President Emmanuel Macron, with the far right leading in the opinion polls.

Student groups and trade unions have called for an authorised march in central Paris "against the high cost of living and in support of young people".

Yellow Vests activists, however, have refused to join, instead calling for a separate rally at Place de la Concorde, near the lower house of parliament and presidential palace, despite a ban by authorities.

Interior Minister Laurent Nunez said 70,000 police officers and security forces would be deployed across the country.

"If there are any rioters or looters... we'll be ready and waiting for them," he said.

The demonstrations have been largely peaceful, but there have at times been clashes with police or vandalism on their sidelines, including on October 17, when France saw its worst rioting in years.

On Thursday, hundreds of thousands of striking workers took to the streets across France in mostly orderly protests, although clashes between demonstrators and police broke out in several cities.

-'Mass disobedience'-

The Yellow Vests movement, which staged street protests eight years ago against Macron's government over planned fuel-tax hikes, has called for its banned rally to go ahead.

"We are calling for mass disobedience," said Benjamin Ball, a member of its coordinating committee.

Authorities are determined to prevent a repeat of the rioting and looting that marred the October 17 demonstrations, although the interior ministry said Thursday's protests had "generally gone well" despite 642 arrests.

The police response has faced criticism for being heavy-handed, with dozens of internal investigations launched into allegations of brutality against demonstrators.

Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu has said he will discuss wages and purchasing power with representatives of trade unions and employers' organisations on Monday.

"The only thing that will bring the protests to an end is a response to the demands that have been put forward for several weeks by workers, civil servants, young people and pensioners," an inter-union coalition said on Friday.

The unions are calling for an increase in the minimum wage, which has not received any discretionary boost since 2012, across-the-board wage raises, tax reforms and better learning conditions for young people.

With the European Union's second-largest economy under pressure to rein in debt, the government has limited scope to appease protesters.

World.title: Cyberattack shuts down internet fan fiction library
World.content:
LOS ANGELES - One of the world's most popular fan fiction libraries has been dark for over a week after a cyberattack forced it offline, leaving millions of fans without access to their favourite stories.

Since October 29, anyone trying to reach Archive of Our Own -- known to devotees as AO3 -- has been met with a message saying the site is down for maintenance.

"It's all over my social feed. People are in withdrawal," Johanna Sarriot, a writer and co-founder of pop-up romance bookstore Love Love Books in Los Angeles, told AFP.

Fan fiction refers to stories written by amateur authors using characters and worlds from already-existing books, films or TV shows.

Contributors rewrite endings, invent romances or give minor characters their own adventures, then share them online for free.

Once a niche hobby, it has become a launchpad for the publishing industry, generating breakout smashes like E.L. James's "Fifty Shades of Grey," which began as "Twilight" fan fiction, and Ali Hazelwood's bestseller "The Love Hypothesis," which sprang from the "Star Wars" universe.

Launched in 2008, AO3 has become the genre's main home, with more than 11 million registered users and nearly 18 million works stored on the platform.

In 2019, it won a Hugo Award for Best Related Work, one of science fiction's most prestigious prizes.

"We wanted to make sure that there was a place for fans to engage in non-commercial creativity in ways that wouldn't barrage them with ads, censor them to placate advertisers, sell their data, or do anything but provide a space for fandom," said Harvard Law School professor Rebecca Tushnet, who helped found the Organization for Transformative Works (OTW) which runs the site.

- 'AO3 is not gone' -

Romance fans have been among the hardest hit by the outage.

World.title: SACP maps out post-election strategy
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - The SACP says it will begin that process with an extended Politburo meeting on Monday.

The meeting will bring together national and provincial leadership to assess the outcome and map out the party's next steps.

General-Secretary Solly Mapaila says the party will also consult other formations within the left, through the established Council of the Left.

"We are certainly coordinating that session early next week so that they can reflect on what the masses have said about us as the forces of the left and therefore we can take it from there," he said.

World.title: IEC recognises need for more voter education
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - The IEC says voter education will be a key focus going forward.

The commission says it needs to do more to help the public identify fake information and understand electoral processes.

This comes amid a surge in misinformation and disinformation on social media.

"We need to improve one way or the other in terms of making sure that we start using even technology to make sure that people are able to even go back to material," said the IEC's Vusi Vuma.

"People are familiarised in terms of our electrical processes. And when I talk training, I'm not talking training for our staff, training for the general public. There's a lot of disinformation, misinformation."

World.title: ANC leads but loses ground in North West
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - The ANC remains in the lead in the North West, but its support has taken a significant knock.

The party is polling at just under 45 percent, down from more than 55 percent in the 2021 local government elections.

It's a setback for a party that has dominated the province for decades, with voters seemingly demanding more from their elected representatives.

With the counting process still underway, several municipalities are already facing the prospect of hung councils.

The ANC says its declining support is partly the result of former members who chose to contest the elections as independents or joined opposition parties.

The decline in ANC support could complicate the party's efforts to secure outright majorities across the province.

And political analysts say some municipalities could once again be forced into coalition arrangements.

For voters, however, the election was less about party loyalty and more about the issues affecting their daily lives.

Access to water, reliable electricity, decent roads and employment remain key concerns.

With the results still being finalised, the political negotiations could prove just as important as the votes themselves.

The challenge now is for political parties to find common ground and form stable administrations capable of delivering on residents' expectations.

World.title: ODM-UDA team begins fine-tuning joint manifesto ahead of 2027 elections
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

ODM-UDA manifesto joint committee met ODM deputy party leader Abdulswamad Nassir in Mombasa. [Omondi Onyango, Standard]

The ODM-UDA manifesto joint committee has started consultations with key political leaders and stakeholders to fine-tune a shared policy document to guide the broad-based government re-election campaign.

The team met ODM deputy party leader Abdulswamad Nassir as they raced against time to fine-tune the document ahead of the 2027 General election, which is 10 months away.

Nassir, who asked the team to come up with a good document, said they will also meet ODM deputy party Leader Simba Arati as they seek to consolidate the priorities of the two political parties.

Addressing the media in Mombasa after meeting the team, Nassir noted that the committee does not have a very big task in fine-tuning the document because both parties have similar aspirations in their documents.

Nassir explained that both manifestos recognised the need to remunerate Community Health Promoters (CHPs) and provide affordable housing, among other issues for the benefit of Kenyans.

He also identified special economic zones and social protection as other shared areas,

"I think drafting this manifesto will not be much work. It is just a matter of ironing out the issues to make sure everything is well," he said.

The governor said they expect the exercise to be completed by February next year.

“We are racing against time because we only have 10 months remaining before the General Election. The joint ODM-UDA manifesto drafting committee is racing against time to fine-tune a shared policy document to guide the broad-based government's re-election campaign,” said Nassir.

He explained that the team led by ODM representative Engineer Carey Orege and UDA's Dr Emmanuel Nzai are capable of consolidating the priorities of the two parties and coming up with a common manifesto ahead of the election.

The governor expressed confidence that the exercise will be smooth, saying ODM and UDA share common policy priorities in several key sectors.

Nassir reaffirmed ODM's commitment to the broad-based political arrangement and support for President William Ruto's re-election, urging the committee to produce a document that reflects the aspirations of Kenyans and enjoys the backing of all coalition partners.

He clarified that the committee was undertaking technical work to outline the broad-based government's development agenda and was not responsible for negotiating a pre-election coalition agreement.

The governor revealed that a separate team would be appointed by the respective party leaders to negotiate the coalition agreement in accordance with their party constitutions, with the proposals subsequently presented to the relevant party organs for endorsement.

The committee is expected to consult other deputy party leaders’ secretaries-general, governors, Members of Parliament and other stakeholders before completing its work.

World.title: Family identifies two security officers involved in Abshir Abdi abduction
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

LSK president Charles Kanjama leads members in a protest over the disappearance of lawyer Abshir Abdi. [Benard Orwongo Standard]

The family of Nairobi lawyer Abshir Ahmedsadak Abdi has identified two security officers alleged to have taken part in their kin's abduction, even as his colleagues threatened mass protests to push for his release.

The Law Society of Kenya (LSK) said the two names have been forwarded to the police to aid in investigations and demanded that the office of the Inspector General of Police, Douglas Kanja, speed up the probe into the abduction.

"One is named Siad and the other is Hussein, and we want them released for investigation, arrest, prosecution, conviction, sentencing and imprisonment," said LSK.

The revelation came during a demonstration led by (LSK outside the office of the Deputy Inspector General of Police and other towns yesterday .

Abshir was forcibly taken on November 1 along Muchai Road, his vehicle was pursued and intercepted by armed individuals in two vehicles before he was seized.

While state security agencies have denied holding him in custody, court filings and colleagues suggest his abduction may be connected to his professional work representing clients in high-profile cases involving senior police officers.

Furthermore, the LSK presented additional names of security personnel linked to the incident, demanding immediate legal action against Chief Inspector Vitalis Kibet, Inspector Kennedy Kimani Karanja, Siad Mohammed, Abdurahman of the Anti-Terrorism Police Unit (ATPU), and KDF officer Ali Hussein.

The leadership voiced their frustration over the state's inaction and the alarming pattern of extrajudicial actions targeting officers of the court. Representatives insisted that lawyers must be allowed to execute their duties without fear of intimidation, torture, or abduction.

"We demand that the officers involved be handed over, arrested, prosecuted, and convicted. We will stand in the courts, in the streets, and in the boardrooms until abductions come to an end," they said in a statement.

The LSK has issued a stern ultimatum to the police command, including the president, DIG Gilbert Masengeli, Inspector General Douglas Kanja, and senior commanders. If Abshir is not released safely and the identified suspects are not formally charged in court by Monday, the LSK warned it will initiate private prosecutions itself.

Furthermore, the society threatened to bring activities to a complete shutdown and demand the immediate resignation of Kanja, Masingeli and Minister for Security Kipchumba Murkomen, carrying their demonstrations to Parliament and State House if necessary.

As court proceedings continue under a habeas corpus application at the Milimani High Court, the legal fraternity remains resolute: the protest at Jogoo House is merely the beginning of an unyielding campaign for justice and the rule of law.

In Nakuru, lawyers protested within the Law Courts, calling for his production.

“It is shocking that one of our colleagues was picked and today we do not know where he is. Unless we voice our concern, there will be complete lawlessness in the country,” said LSK member Ekaterina Handa. “Our lives matter and silencing lawyers is silencing justice. we will not relent until we get justice.”

Rift Valley LSK Chair Wangari Mwangi said it was shocking that the alleged abduction was captured on CCTV.

She rubbished the narrative that the missing lawyer was involved in a crime syndicate, maintaining that he should have been arrested and charged in court. [Additional reporting by Daniel Chege]

World.title: Goon financiers should be cursed and sent to hell, Chief Justice Koome says
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Chief Justice Martha Koome said goonism falls under serious organised crimes that goes against the Rome Statute and humanity. [Phares Mutembei, Standard]

Chief Justice Martha Koome now says those mobilising and financing goons should be cursed and thrown to hell.

Koome on Thursday said goonism falls under organised serious crimes that go against the Rome Statute and humanity.

She spoke at Kieganguru, Maara constituency, where she presided over the opening of the Maara law courts.

While calling on police to focus more on arresting the mobilisers and financiers, Koome said a time has come for the country to plead with God to protect the country and rescue the youth who are being misused and misled into organised gangs and goonism.

“Nobody gives birth to a child to be called a goon. Those organisers will go to hell, we curse them,” Koome said, adding, “If they will not go to hell they will meet God's justice. These are our children, and we reclaim them in the name of our Lord Jesus.”

According to her, the last time she checked, people are charged at the International Criminal Court with Organised crime.

She maintained that the best solution to the current goonism that wreaked havoc, especially in political meetings, is to arrest the organisers.

Koome said the courts cannot hold arrested goons without bail, yet the constitution grants them the right to bail or bond.

“When we arrest small people with petty crimes of causing disorder, the law allows us to release them on bail and bond, but when you bring the organisers, we will charge them under the Serious Crimes Act,” she said.

Koome said currently, the judiciary has gazetted a serious crimes division at the High Court to support Magistrates handling the cases.

“Let us look at the root cause of goonism across the country and rehabilitate those involved by getting them gainful employment,” she said.

Her sentiments, however, differ from those of Interior Cabinet Secretary Kipchumba Murkomen, who on Wednesday told the National Assembly that the judiciary was the weakest link in the fight against the menace.

Tharaka Nithi Governor Muthomi Njuki, in his remarks, supported Koome’s view of arresting the planners.

Njuki, who doubles up as the Council of Governors Chairperson, said politicians have had their time and organising goons against their opponents should not be condoned.

Using the analogy of a dog, Njuki said ‘every barking dog has an owner ’, and it is time serious action was taken against such characters at whatever level they are.

The county boss said CoG will work closely with county security teams to arrest the fast-rising menace and report all cases.

Security agencies have been under scrutiny regarding goons, with calls for their arrest and prosecution.

Earlier on, Koome and DCI boss Mohammed Amin differed on how to handle the goons during a National Council for Administrative Justice meeting as with the DCI boss also accusing the Judiciary of laxity and granting minor bail to arrested goons.

But Koome maintained the issue must be addressed lest it becomes a thorn in the flesh ahead of the 2027 elections.

World.title: IEBC warns UDA SG Hassan Omar over remarks on deceased voters
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

UDA Secretary General Hassan Omar meets Village Elders and Mabalozi wa Nyumba Kumi from Jomvu Sub-County’ on September 10, 2026. [Nehemiah Okwemba, Standard]

The Independent Electoral and Boundaries Commission (IEBC) has issued a stern warning to Senator Hassan Omar after finding him in breach of the Electoral Code of Conduct over remarks he made at a political rally in Mombasa, cautioning that any repeat offence could attract tougher sanctions.

In a determination released on Wednesday, November 4, 2026, the Electoral Code of Conduct Enforcement Committee (ECCEC) found Omar guilty of breaching paragraphs 6(k)(i) and 6(l) of the Electoral Code of Conduct.

The committee consequently issued the senator with a formal and strict warning and severe caution, directing him to comply with the electoral regulations for the remainder of the applicable election period.

Omar was further instructed to refrain from language or conduct that could reasonably be understood as encouraging or normalising electoral malpractice or undermining public confidence in the integrity of the ballot.

The decision follows investigations into remarks the senator allegedly made during a public rally in Mombasa on September 11, 2026, which raised concerns over the possibility of encouraging electoral malpractice.

According to the commission, Omar was summoned to appear before the committee on October 21, 2026, to respond to the allegations. He honoured the summons and appeared in person, accompanied by his lawyer, where he was given an opportunity to explain his remarks and present his defence.

In reaching its determination, the committee considered the context in which the statements were made, Omar's explanation that his words were intended figuratively to encourage voter registration and participation, his subsequent clarification and the absence of evidence linking the remarks to an actual electoral incident.

However, the committee maintained that the language used could not be excused by the explanation offered.

It observed that the impugned words, considered in their original Kiswahili form and ordinary meaning, invoked the use of biometric identification details belonging to a deceased person to facilitate voting in that individual's name.

The committee consequently found the remarks inconsistent with the obligation under paragraph 6(l) of the Electoral Code to reassure voters about the integrity of the ballot.

The warning places Omar on clear notice that any recurrence of similar conduct could attract more severe sanctions under the Electoral Code of Conduct and applicable laws.

“The determination places Hon. Hassan Omar on clear and unequivocal notice that the warning issued by the Committee is intended to mark a firm boundary against any recurrence of similar conduct,” IEBC stated.

The commission further emphasised that political leaders and other electoral stakeholders have a constitutional right to campaign, criticise, debate, persuade and participate in political discourse.

However, it cautioned that political expression must be exercised responsibly, warning that statements perceived as advocating, encouraging or normalising electoral malpractice could undermine public confidence in the electoral process.

“As Kenya prepares for the 2027 General Election, the Commission calls upon all political leaders, candidates, political parties, supporters and other electoral stakeholders to exercise responsibility, restraint and vigilance in their public utterances and conduct,” the commission said.

The determination comes as political activities gradually intensify ahead of the 2027 General Election, with the electoral body seeking to strengthen compliance with regulations governing political campaigns and public conduct.

IEBC maintained that enforcement of the Electoral Code should not be interpreted as an attempt to suppress legitimate political competition or freedom of expression.

Instead, it said the measures were intended to safeguard democratic participation and ensure that every Kenyan could exercise their right to vote without intimidation, manipulation or interference.

The commission reiterated its commitment to protecting the sanctity of the ballot, assuring Kenyans that every vote must be protected and counted in accordance with the law.

It warned that it would continue enforcing electoral regulations firmly, fairly and without fear or favour, as preparations for the 2027 elections gather momentum.

World.title: Death rumours made me stronger, says ODM leader Oburu
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Speakers Moses Wetang’ula and Amason Kingi when they paid a visit to ODM leader Oburu Oginga at his Nairobi residence on November 4, 2026. [Speaker’s Press Unit]

ODM leader and Siaya Senator Oburu Oginga has said rumours about his death while he was admitted to hospital only strengthened his determination to overcome his illness.

Dr Oburu who is recovering after being discharged from hospital, assured his supporters that he was making remarkable improvement and would return to active politics soon.

Speaking at his Nairobi residence on Wednesday when Speakers Moses Wetang’ula and Amason Kingi paid him a visit, the ODM leader said the rumours only strengthened his resolve to come out of the hospital bed.

“Those who wrote me off while I was in hospital by declaring me dead only made me stronger and more determined to fight my sickness. Here I am, recovering and growing stronger by the day,” he said.

He said that his recovery was a testimony to God's protection, saying those who had spread the false reports had been put to shame.

Oburu admitted that the illness had slowed down him down but he was looking forward to returning to the political arena.

“The sickness slowed my political activities. Very soon, I will be back roaring in the best way I know how,” he said.

The senator thanked the National Assembly Speaker Wetang’ula, his Senate counterpart Kingi and other legislators for taking time to visit him following his discharge from hospital.

He said the visit had lifted his spirit and revealed that he missed participating in parliamentary debates and engaging in national political affairs.

“I have no words to explain my feelings after the Speakers of both Houses and fellow legislators created time to come and check on me,” he said.

“I miss being on the floor of the House debating and roaring in the political arena. I urge my supporters to pray for me and be patient because soon I will be back,” he added.

Despite his recent health challenges, Oburu kept his visitors entertained with his trademark humour while expressing confidence that he would soon resume his political duties.

The two Speakers condemned the spread of false information on social media, particularly rumours that the senator had died while undergoing treatment.

Wetang’ula said they were encouraged by the senator's recovery and wished him a full and speedy return to good health.

He, however, cautioned Oburu against rushing back into politics before fully recovering, urging him to give his health priority.

“Prioritise your health and avoid rushing back into political engagements before making a full recovery,” he said.

The National Assembly Speaker also praised the senator for his courage and determination in facing his health challenges.

Kingi said the Senate missed Dr Oburu's contribution to debates, parliamentary proceedings and national politics.

“As the Senate, we miss your contributions to proceedings and debates as well as your guidance in national politics. We pray that you get better and resume your political duties as soon as possible,” he said.

Those who accompanied the two Speakers included Senate Chief Whip David Wakoli, Senate Minority Leader Stewart Madzayo, Senators William Kisang and Daniel Maanzo.

Others were National Assembly Minority Whip Millie Odhiambo, Parliamentary Commissioner Mishi Mboko and MP Eve Obara.

World.title: Kenyans stranded after Saudi Arabia blocks entry over Ebola concerns
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Kenyan jobseekers arrive at JKIA on November 2, 2026, after being denied entry into Saudi Arabia over Ebola-related restrictions. [Stafford Ondego, Standard]

More than 300 Kenyans who travelled to Saudi Arabia in search of employment have been forced to return home after authorities blocked their entry over Ebola-related restrictions, leaving them stranded at the airport for two days.

The group, which departed Kenya on October 30, had travelled to the Gulf country on valid work visas but was denied entry upon arrival and subsequently repatriated, arriving back in the country on Monday.

The return follows a warning by Health Cabinet Secretary Aden Duale on Saturday, October 31, over restrictions imposed by Saudi Arabia on travellers from countries flagged over Ebola concerns.

Speaking to the media at Jomo Kenyatta International Airport (JKIA) on Monday, the affected workers recounted their ordeal, accusing authorities at the airport of subjecting them to harsh conditions as they waited to be repatriated.

“We were treated so harshly as though we had leprosy. We only took one meal per day and slept on the cold floors at the airport in Saudi Arabia,” said Kanyi Njau, one of the affected workers, claiming that some have even lost their luggage.

Beyond the difficult experience at the airport, the workers said their biggest concern was the financial loss incurred while preparing for the promised jobs.

Some said they had sold land, household belongings and other property, while others borrowed money to pay recruitment agents, process visas and secure travel documents in preparation for their departure.

Njau said the abrupt disruption had shattered the hopes of many who had invested heavily in securing employment abroad.

“Some of us sold things in our houses, even land. Some even took loans from shylocks just so that we could travel over there for the jobs, but now we are back with no hope,” she said.

Kenyan jobseekers arrive at JKIA on November 2, 2026, after being denied entry into Saudi Arabia over Ebola-related restrictions. [Stafford Ondego, Standard]

The workers are now appealing to the Kenyan Government to intervene and resolve the standoff with Saudi authorities before their visas expire, allowing them to return and take up the jobs they had secured.

Meanwhile, recruitment agencies have called on the Government to urgently clarify the restrictions, warning that uncertainty over a 21-day provision could disrupt the country's labour mobility programme.

Monika Mwema, the Secretary General of the Association of Skilled Migrant Agencies of Kenya (ASMAK), said recruiters had been caught off guard, with some workers already repatriated while others had confirmed tickets and were scheduled to travel.

“We are caught off guard. We have people who are coming back because they could not be allowed to enter Saudi Arabia, while others have confirmed tickets and are even supposed to leave tonight and tomorrow,” she said.

Mwema said the association was seeking clarification on what the 21-day provision meant for workers holding stamped Saudi work visas, including whether they would be required to undergo quarantine in Kenya or in a third country before being allowed into the Kingdom.

“Does it mean we have to quarantine our people here for the 21 days, then they are allowed to enter the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia? Or does it mean that we need to seek an alternative quarantine area where there is no case of Ebola?” she asked.

Kenyan jobseekers arrive at JKIA on November 2, 2026, after being denied entry into Saudi Arabia over Ebola-related restrictions. [Stafford Ondego, Standard]

She said recruiters were also concerned about the 90-day period within which migrant workers are required to travel after their visas are stamped, warning that delays could result in significant losses for agencies and prospective employees.

Mwema added that some workers had already undergone training and completed examinations in preparation for their deployment, while recruitment partners in Saudi Arabia were demanding to know when the workers would arrive.

“The losses are just too many. We have people who have already gone to school for training; others have done their examinations and are waiting to go. Our partners are calling us, asking when these people are coming, but we are all in the dark,” she said.

ASMAK is now seeking urgent engagement with the Kenyan Government and Saudi authorities to establish a clear way forward.

Mwema said the association was ready to engage the Government, including through a meeting with President William Ruto, to discuss the future of labour mobility between the two countries.

Saudi Arabia remains Kenya's biggest market for labour mobility, with recruiters warning that continued uncertainty could affect workers awaiting deployment and agencies with visas already processed.

World.title: Gachagua dismisses Uhuru reconciliation calls, says 'we are one team'
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

DCP leader Rigathi Gachagua received at PCEA Kamangu in Kikuyu constituency by former Kiambu governor James Nyoro on November 1, 2026. [George Njunge, Standard]

Former Deputy President Rigathi Gachagua has dismissed calls for mediation between him and former President Uhuru Kenyatta, insisting that the two leaders remain in contact and have no differences requiring reconciliation.

Gachagua said attempts by Mount Kenya elders to broker peace between them were unnecessary, maintaining that he and the former Head of State continue to communicate, meet and share meals despite perceptions of a political fallout.

He challenged elders calling for reconciliation to instead focus on uniting the Mount Kenya community, warning that internal divisions could weaken the region's political voice and influence.

“On unity, as a community we have to remain united. Our unity is strength. Nimeona some elders in the newspaper wakisema tunataka to reconcile Rigathi Gachagua and Uhuru Kenyatta. How do you reconcile two brothers, who love one another and work together?” he posed.

The former Deputy President maintained that he and Uhuru were still on the same team, dismissing claims that their relationship had deteriorated to a point requiring third-party intervention.

“President Uhuru Kenyatta and I are one team. We work together. Please elders don’t reconcile us because there is no need for reconciliation. We are working together. There is no work there, we are one. We talk the same language, we meet, talk, we agree,” he said.

Gachagua further urged Mount Kenya elders to resist attempts to divide the community along political lines and instead promote dialogue and cohesion among its leaders.

“Our unity is our strength as a community. Please help me to unite Mount Kenya elders and tell people not to accept to be divided,” he added.

His remarks come amid growing calls by sections of Mount Kenya elders for reconciliation among influential political figures from the region following political differences that have emerged since the 2022 General Election.

Uhuru, who served as Kenya's fourth president from 2013 to 2022, remains an influential political figure in the region, while Gachagua has continued to position himself as a key voice in Mount Kenya politics.

World.title: Sifuna rallies opposition leaders to unite against Ruto in 2027
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Linda Mwananchi leader Edwin Sifuna adresses a rally at Ukunda in Kwale County on 31st October, 2026. [Omondi Onyango, Standard]

Nairobi Senator Edwin Sifuna’s Linda Mwananchi movement took its grassroots mobilisation tour to Kwale County, a day after unveiling its secretariat and leadership, with leaders urging the opposition to unite behind one candidate to face President William Ruto in 2027.

The unveiling had been marred by disagreement, with Wiper leader Kalonzo Musyoka jeered. Addressing a rally at Masai Grounds in Ukunda town, Sifuna said Kenyans were yearning for a single, strong opposition candidate and asked other leaders not to let them down.

“To send Ruto home, we need a strong team and a strong presidential candidate. I will ask other leaders to listen to the voices of the people politely because this is the voice of God,” he said.

The team made stopovers in Samburu, Kinango, Kwale town and Kombani during the day-long tour. Unlike earlier rallies in Mombasa, the Kwale events drew modest crowds, amid claims that local organisers had failed to mobilise supporters.

The mobilisation tour covered Samburu Town, Kinango Town, Kombani Junction, Lunga Lunga Town, and culminated in a major public rally at the Ukunda Showground.

The movement officially opened its new Kwale County office as part of a push to build county-level structures ahead of the 2027 General Election.

Addressing supporters in the rain, Sifuna declared that he will continue to build consensus among the opposition to ensure that they are united to send Ruto home in 2027. he said that divisions of the opposition leaders will guarantee Ruto a second term.

He warned against schemes to elbow local leaders out of the front lines, stressing that Kwale residents and local aspirants must drive the agenda on regional issues like water shortages and mineral exploitation. The Kwale tour marks the first public rallies after weeks without a large-scale county mobilisation exercise.

It has previously held gatherings in Mombasa and Taita Taveta as part of its plan to reach all 47 counties. The tour took place the same day the Orange Democratic Movement (ODM) was holding a rally at Jacaranda Grounds in Nairobi's Embakasi East constituency.

Embakasi East MP Babu Owino urged Sifuna, Musyoka, DCP leader Rigathi Gachagua and Jubilee leader Fred Matiang’i to agree on one presidential candidate, warning that time was running out.

“We are urging all opposition leaders to sit down and talk. We only have nine months to the General Election, and you should agree on one presidential challenger to President Ruto,” he said. “Sifuna, Kalonzo, Gachagua and Matiang’i should come together now. United we stand, divided we fall.”

isii Senator Richard Onyonka said it was time for opposition leaders to lock themselves in a room and emerge with a single candidate to face Mr Ruto. The call was backed by Linda Mwananchi chairman Godfrey Osotsi and Secretary General Caroli Omondi.

Trans Nzoia Governor George Natembeya, however, said Sifuna was best placed to challenge the President and asked Mr Gachagua and Mr Musyoka to back him.

“I want to urge Gachagua and Kalonzo to back Sifuna for the opposition to secure an easy win against Ruto. I want to assure you that there will be no rigging of the election,” he said.

Meru Governor Kawira Mwangaza said Kenyans would reject Ruto at the ballot for failing to honour pledges, including those on women’s empowerment.

Sifuna accused the President of failing to protect the Constitution and the rights of Kenyans. “He has focused more on building houses and markets and failed to protect lives,” he said.

He also claimed the government had issued title deeds for smaller parcels than residents used to own, while land was stolen. He further alleged that the government was plotting to plunder mineral resources at Mrima Hill in Kwale and demanded that an agreement with American investors be made public.

World.title: Egyptian, Iranian FMs discuss regional developments, ongoing efforts to de-escalate tensions
World.content:
Minister of Foreign Affairs, International Cooperation and Egyptian Expatriates Badr Abdelatty held a telephone conversation with Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi to discuss the latest regional developments and ongoing efforts to de-escalate tensions in the region.

Foreign Ministry Spokesperson Nader Zaki said the two ministers exchanged views on recent regional developments and voiced concern over the prospect of renewed military confrontations and their potential repercussions for regional and international security and stability.

Abdelatty underscored the importance of prioritizing diplomatic solutions and demonstrating the necessary openness to advance a political settlement of the crisis.

He stressed the need for all parties to show flexibility and reach compromises that serve their respective interests, thereby preventing the region from descending into a new wave of escalation that could have serious political, economic, and humanitarian repercussions for the region and the world at large.

World.title: FM heads to Libya
World.content:
Minister of Foreign Affairs, International Cooperation and Egyptians Abroad Badr Abdelatty departed for Libya on Saturday, November 7, 2026.

The foreign minister is scheduled to hold a series of meetings with senior Libyan officials.

As part of the visit, Abdelatty will participate in the proceedings of the 22nd Ordinary Session of the Executive Council of the Community of Sahel-Saharan States (CEN-SAD), hosted by Tripoli, to discuss ways to strengthen cooperation among member states and advance efforts to activate the organization’s mechanisms.

World.title: Qatar issues statement following reports of failed negotiations between the US and Iran
World.content:
A statement by the International Media Office of Qatar said that Prime Minister and Minister of Foreign Affairs Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman bin Jassim al-Thani confirmed that the US and Iran are continuing efforts to reach an agreement.

“Reports circulating online claiming that His Excellency the Prime Minister and Minister of Foreign Affairs stated that the United States and Iran had failed to reach an agreement are false and misleading,” the statement said.

The statement added that “His Excellency’s remarks have been deliberately distorted by those who benefit from continued war and instability in our region. Many of these claims are being spread by fake accounts trying to undermine diplomatic efforts and push for further escalation. This is deeply irresponsible.”

Bloomberg previously reported, citing the Qatari Prime Minister and Minister of Foreign Affairs, that the US and Iran had failed to reach a “comprehensive agreement,” according to the Hebrew-language newspaper Yedioth Ahronoth.

An official from the US Central Command (CENTCOM) told Al Jazeera that the command would issue an announcement regarding Iran at 8:30 am Saturday (Washington time), though he declined to disclose the nature of the announcement.

Meanwhile, the Iranian news agency Tasnim reported that two missiles had struck Qeshm Island, located in the Arabian Gulf; no official information has yet been released regarding the extent of any potential damage.

World.title: Planning Minister: Luxor has unique comparative advantages, promising economic prospects
World.content:
Minister of Planning and Economic Development Ahmed Rostom said Luxor is one of Upper Egypt’s promising governorates, with unique comparative advantages underpinned by its diverse economic activities, particularly tourism and agriculture.

Rostom made the remarks during a field visit to Luxor, pursuant to presidential directives to monitor development projects that directly affect citizens’ lives across the country. He was received by Luxor Governor Abdel Mottaleb Emara.

The visit falls within the Ministry of Planning and Economic Development’s efforts to monitor implementation of the economic and social development plan, in line with directives from Prime Minister Mostafa Madbouly to ensure that development projects are implemented according to schedule, Rostom said.

He added that the visit aims to support state efforts to improve living standards and ensure that public investments contribute directly to the development of various sectors.

The minister said the visit includes inspections of a number of ongoing development and vital projects across the governorate, particularly in the infrastructure, drinking water and sanitation, education, and healthcare sectors, with the aim of advancing comprehensive development and improving the quality of life for Luxor residents.

It will also provide an opportunity to assess project completion rates on the ground, identify potential challenges, and address the governorate’s needs, reflecting the priority the state attaches to development projects in Upper Egypt, Rostom noted.

He also highlighted the integration of projects under Luxor’s economic and social development plan with the presidential Decent Life initiative, stressing the government’s commitment to completing the initiative’s first phase in full and preparing for the launch of its second phase.

The initiative represents a key pillar in upgrading infrastructure and public services in Egyptian villages and rural areas, he said.

The visit is part of a series of extensive field tours that the Minister of Planning and Economic Development has been conducting across various governorates this year.

Previous visits included Sharqiya, Monufia, and Beheira, as part of efforts to enhance monitoring of development projects under the national plan.

World.title: Egypt, Bahrain seek stronger trade and investment ties
World.content:
“Egypt and Bahrain are seeking to expand trade, increase investment and strengthen economic cooperation,” Finance Minister Ahmed Kouchouk said on Thursday November 5, 2026.

His remarks came during the third meeting of the Bahrain-Egypt Government Committee for Trade, Economic, Scientific and Technological Cooperation, held in Egypt’s New Capital and co-chaired by Kouchouk and Bahrain’s Minister of Finance and National Economy, Sheikh Salman bin Khalifa Al Khalifa.

Kouchouk said that both countries had opportunities to expand cooperation, particularly through private sector investment in manufacturing, exports and technology.

He called for increased Bahraini investment in Egypt’s productive, financial and technology sectors, alongside measures to facilitate trade and improve market access for businesses in both countries.

The Minister said Egypt and Bahrain would work to address investment obstacles and turn existing bilateral agreements into projects that support economic growth.

He also expressed Egypt’s interest in exchanging expertise with Bahrain on public financial management, spending efficiency and digital transformation.

For his part, Sheikh Salman bin Khalifa Al Khalifa called for closer economic cooperation and greater private sector participation in bilateral trade and investment.

He welcomed an agreement to organize the Bahrain-Egypt Business Forum regularly to encourage partnerships between companies in both countries.

The meeting also reviewed investment opportunities, joint projects and cooperation in trade, science and technology, with senior ministers and officials from both countries attending.

World.title: US issues warnings to its citizens in the Middle East
World.content:
The US has issued security warnings through its diplomatic missions in several Middle Eastern countries, including its embassy in Israel, on Saturday.

Yedioth Ahronoth reported that these warnings follow escalating threats from Houthi forces in Yemen, as well as intelligence regarding Iranian attempts to target high-ranking US officials in the region.

The warnings, which were also issued for Saudi Arabia, the United Arab Emirates, Qatar, Bahrain, and several other nations, urge US citizens to exercise the utmost caution.

They also advise individuals to be prepared for potential flight cancellations or the closure of airspace, as well as the possibility of a rapid escalation in the intensity of the conflict.

US planning to resume operations against Iran

American news reports indicated that the administration of US President Donald Trump was reviewing plans to resume military operations against Iran.

Axios, citing American officials, reported that Trump held a meeting on Thursday with his top national security advisors to discuss the Iran dossier.

The US President asserted that Iran would never possess a nuclear weapon, hinting that American decisions regarding how to deal with the country were imminent.

The report further quoted a US official as saying that US Central Command (CENTCOM) is finalizing preparations for the potential resumption of large-scale combat operations in Iran.

World.title: Egypt’s foreign currency reserves reach US$ 57.50 billion
World.content:
The Governor of the Central Bank of Egypt (CBE), Hassan Abdallah, announced that the country’s foreign currency reserves have climbed to an all-time high – reaching US$ 57.50 billion by the end of October.

He further noted that the banking sector’s net foreign assets have reached their highest level since 2011, coinciding with a decline in inflation rates.

The CBE Governor highlighted these indicators during his participation in the 49th annual conference of the Arab Union of Financial Markets Traders, emphasizing that the Egyptian economy has achieved positive results despite unprecedented global challenges.

Abdallah explained that the CBE continues to work toward maintaining financial stability and strengthening the resilience of the banking sector.

This is being pursued through an approach rooted in transparency and a monetary policy framework aimed at lowering inflation rates, alongside a commitment to a flexible exchange rate regime determined by market mechanisms.

He added that this approach is intended to enhance the economy’s capacity to absorb external shocks and withstand volatility, while building upon the gains achieved through the reforms implemented in 2024.

Technological innovations

The CBE Governor emphasized the importance of balancing the adoption of technological innovation with investment in human capital, in order to support the future of the banking sector.

He noted that CBE has leveraged artificial intelligence technology—through its “Data Science Center”—to enhance operational efficiency and advance economic analysis.

Furthermore, he called on establishing robust risk management frameworks, strengthening sound governance, and solidifying cybersecurity systems to mitigate risks that could threaten the stability of the financial system or impact markets.

Edited translation from Al-Masry Al-Youm

World.title: Drop in temperatures, rainy weather across Egypt on Saturday
World.content:
The Egyptian Meteorological Authority (EMA) expects temperatures to remain low across most regions on Saturday.

This will be accompanied by a chance of rain—varying in intensity—in parts of the north, along with active winds and disrupted maritime navigation along some Mediterranean coasts.

During the day, the weather will be moderate in most areas, and slightly hot in southern part of Upper Egypt.

At night and during the early morning, it will turn cool to cold across most regions.

Rainfall Map

Weather maps indicate a chance of moderate rainfall across parts of the North Coast governorates and the northern Lower Egypt.

The rainfall may occasionally be heavy and accompanied by thunderstorms, with a 30 percent probability – particularly in areas including El Alamein, Alexandria, the northern Delta, and North Sinai, occurring intermittently.

There is also a 30 percent chance of light rain across scattered areas of the southern Lower Egypt and the Suez Canal cities.

This may extend to parts of Greater Cairo, northern Upper Egypt, the Gulf of Suez, central and southern Sinai, and further south to the Halayeb and Shalateen regions.

Satellite imagery has detected intermittent wind activity across most regions, which is intensifying the perception of lower temperatures.

Furthermore, maritime navigation is being disrupted along parts of the Mediterranean coast—specifically in Matrouh, El Alamein, Alexandria, Beheira, Kafr el-Sheikh, Damietta, Port Said, and el-Arish.

Wind speeds in these areas will range between 40-50 kilometers per hour, with wave heights reaching two to 3.5 meters.

The EMA urged the public to take necessary precautions and measures and to stay updated through the latest bulletins issued by the authority.

Edited translation from Al-Masry Al-Youm

World.title: Law marker calls for cancer screening
World.content:
Lima Constituency Member of Parliament Kelvin Kunda has called on Zambians to prioritise regular cancer screening, warning that late detection continues to contribute to cancer-related deaths.

Mr Kunda has said that early detection remains critical in improving treatment outcomes urging members of the public not to wait until they experience symptoms before seeking screening services.

Speaking during the Rotary Club of Maluba’s Free Annual Cancer Screening event at Twikatane Mall in Barlastone Park in Lusaka today, Mr Kunda said cancer is a major health concern requiring collective efforts from Government, the private sector and communities.

He cited estimates from the International Agency for Research on Cancer indicating that approximately 16,600 Zambians are diagnosed with cancer annually, while nearly 9,800 die from the disease.

Mr Kunda mentioned that many people continue to lose their lives because cancer is detected at advanced stages when treatment is more difficult and costly.

“Not knowing does not protect you. Knowing does,” he said, urging people to overcome fear, stigma and misconceptions surrounding cancer screening,” he said.

He said early detection improves chances of successful treatment, reduces the financial burden on families and helps to prevent some cancers, particularly through screening for cervical cancer.

Mr Kunda has commended the Rotary Club of Maluba for sustaining its free cancer screening and awareness initiative for 22 years, noting that about 4,400 people have been educated on cancer prevention and have been screened through the programme.

He has called for more partnerships to expand access to screening services, particularly in underserved communities calling on churches, community health volunteers and other local groups to promote awareness.

Meanwhile, Rotary Club of Maluba President Chanja Makai said the club is targeting to screen 700 people during this year’s initiative.

Ms Makai said the annual programme has been running for 22 years, with prostate and breast cancer screening introduced alongside cervical cancer screening as the initiative expanded.

She said the services are being provided free of charge in partnership with health professionals from Kanyama Level One Hospital and CDH, with screening available for breast, cervical and prostate cancer.

“We are hoping to capture about 300 men and 400 women. So men will be testing for both prostate and breast cancer,” she said.

Ms Makai has encouraged members of the public to attend with their families, adding that screening is quick and can help detect cancer even among people who are not experiencing symptoms.

She said the club has also heard testimonies from cancer survivors who have lived cancer-free for several years after diagnosis and treatment, demonstrating the importance of early detection.

And Synergy Seeds Zambia Chief Executive Officer Brian Mhango said the company is proud to partner with the Rotary Club of Maluba and other stakeholders in making cancer screening services accessible to communities.

Mr Mhango said the initiative reflects the importance of promoting good health as a foundation for strong families, productive workplaces and thriving communities.

“Early detection saves lives, and screening is one of the most important steps we can take towards protecting our health,” he said.

He has urged members of the public not to wait until they feel unwell before taking their health seriously.

World.title: 2027 budget to be judged by results-Nkoma
World.content:
Government said the 2027 National Budget will be measured by results and not pronouncements.

Minister of Industry Noel Nkoma said the Budget will be judged by the businesses that grow the investments and materialise jobs among others.

He was speaking at the Zambia Institute of Chartered Accountants (ZICA) 2027 Post-Budget Analysis Dinner in Lusaka.

Mr Nkoma said the National Budget is the Government’s most powerful tool for driving national development, as it reflects Government’s priorities, aspirations and policy direction.

He said the 2027 Budget comes at a pivotal moment in Zambia’s economic transformation journey and has been crafted around the Grow Zambia Agenda.

He said the agenda seeks to stimulate economic expansion, support enterprise development, create jobs, increase productivity, attract investment and improve the quality of life for all citizens.

The Minister added that it was fitting for stakeholders to gather after the presentation of the Budget to analyse its provisions and understand its implications for the Grow Zambia Agenda.

He said the budget process is strengthened by stakeholder participation both before and after the Budget is presented.

“Before formulation, Government undertakes extensive consultations with business associations, professional bodies, civil society, academia and other key stakeholders to ensure the Budget reflects the realities of the economy and responds to the needs of citizens and industry,” he said

Mr Nkoma said discussions at forums such as the ZICA dinner help businesses understand emerging opportunities, enable investors to assess likely economic trends and allow stakeholders to align their plans with national development priorities.

He said such engagements strengthen collaboration between Government and the private sector, which remains a critical pillar of Zambia’s economic transformation agenda.

The Minister said the Government recognises that sustainable economic growth cannot be achieved through public sector interventions alone, but requires a vibrant and competitive private sector capable of investing, innovating, producing and creating employment.

He said the Budget therefore seeks to empower businesses, improve the operating environment and unlock opportunities for entrepreneurship and industrial development.

ZICA President Joseph Matimba, stated that the Budget comes at an important time as Zambia seeks to consolidate macroeconomic stability while accelerating growth, stimulating investment and addressing the challenges facing people.

He named the cost of living, unemployment, poverty, energy security and low productivity as critical areas requiring sustained attention.

“The National Budget must therefore be assessed not only in terms of fiscal allocations and policy measures, but also in terms of its ability to stimulate productive economic activity, support enterprise development and improve the livelihoods of ordinary Zambians,” Mr Matimba said.

He said the industrial sector has a particularly important role to play, noting that a stronger manufacturing base, increased local production and greater value addition are essential to creating jobs, reducing dependence on imports and strengthening Zambia’s competitiveness in regional and international markets.

Mr Matimba said the Budget must also be viewed within the Government’s Grow Zambia Agenda, which seeks to accelerate economic transformation and create inclusive growth through expanding production and investment in agriculture, mining, energy, manufacturing and tourism.

Meanwhile, ZICA Chief Executive Officer, Anthony Bwembya, said that the National Budget is more than a statement of Government’s revenue and expenditure priorities, but reflects national aspirations and provides a framework for stimulating investment, supporting industrial development, creating employment and improving livelihoods.

“Through sound financial management, transparency, accountability and professional advice, our members contribute to strengthening public financial management, supporting business growth and building confidence in our economy,” Mr Bwembya said.

World.title: Mundubile, Makebi Zulu Wait On Tuesday Ruling After 70 Days In Mukobeko
World.content:
Mundubile Bail Fate Rests On Tuesday Ruling As Tonse Condemns 70-Day Detention

The High Court will rule on Tuesday, 10 November, on whether Brian Mundubile and 17 others can proceed with their bid for constitutional bail. The State has asked the court to throw out the application on a technicality, arguing that it was filed in the wrong form. Opposition leaders are describing the prolonged detention as cruel and illegal.

A panel led by Mr Justice Mulenga reserved its ruling after hearing arguments in chambers on a preliminary issue raised by the State. Mr Mundubile is the losing presidential candidate of the National Reconciliation Party for Unity and Prosperity (NRPUP). He is joined in the application by his former running mate Makebi Zulu, Lusaka business executive Harry Findlay and 15 others. The group sued the State alleging gross violations of their constitutional rights. They then applied for constitutional bail, asking to be released either unconditionally or on reasonable conditions set by the court.

Attorney General Mulilo Kabesha, State Counsel, raised the preliminary issue. He urged the court to dismiss the bail application on the grounds that it had been wrongly commenced as a civil application instead of a criminal one. The State’s position is that the form of the filing goes to the heart of the court’s authority to hear the matter at all.

Acting Chief State Advocate Chibesa Mulonda developed that argument on behalf of the State. He submitted that the court could not grant constitutional bail when the application had been brought in civil rather than criminal format. He contended that, in those circumstances, the court had no jurisdiction to hear the application.

The defence pushed back hard. Lawyers for Mr Mundubile and the 17 others include three State Counsel: Bonaventure Mutale, Chifumu Banda and Sakwiba Sikota. They urged the court to reject the objection, sustain the application and hear it on its merits. The State maintained its position that the application should be dismissed for being irregularly filed.

The ruling leaves two possible paths. Mr Justice Mulenga said that if the preliminary issue did not succeed, the court would proceed straight to the substantive bail hearing on the same day. A ruling in the State’s favour would end the application in its current form and send the detainees’ lawyers back to refile.

Outside the courtroom, the opposition has escalated its language. Tonse-Pamodzi Alliance secretary general Muhabi Lungu said the continued incarceration of Mr Mundubile, Mr Zulu and the others at Mukobeko Maximum Prison for more than 70 days, without a plea before a High Court judge, was cruel. In a television interview, he said the detention was illegal because the country was not under a state of emergency.

“It’s not right and fair to charge Brian Mundubile, Makebi Zulu and 17 others and keep them in prison for 70 days without a plea before a judge. It’s not right; it’s illegal. We are not under a state of emergency. 70 days is not 48 hours, especially when the state says it has been probing this case for the last three years ahead of the arrest,” Mr Lungu said.

Mr Lungu accused the State of dragging its feet in the treason matter while the accused remained behind bars. He framed the choice facing prosecutors in stark terms: prove the case or free the accused.

“You can clearly see the State is dragging its feet in the treason matter while our leaders suffer. If you don’t have evidence, let them go, release them. If you have evidence, let the trial start and do it expeditiously so that the whole world sees what you accused them for,” he said.

The Tonse official went further and described the detention as an abuse of state power. In his view, it was aimed at punishing dissent rather than delivering justice. He said the opposition’s reading was that the Government wanted to demonstrate its power to punish.

“Our speculation is that government just wants to show that it can punish you, that abuse, that dictatorship, its cruelty, it’s not governance,” Mr Lungu said.

He tied the case to the final report of the European Union (EU) election observer mission, which he said confirmed that Zambia’s democratic space was shrinking. Mr Lungu said the mission was correct that the boundaries between the Electoral Commission of Zambia (ECZ) and the police had been unclear during the election. He cited uneven policing, misuse of public resources and questions over the independence of the electoral body. He added that former Botswana president Ian Khama and other outside observers had issued similar warnings.

“It’s wrong to jail people arbitrarily and then question why international observers say there’s shrinking democracy,” Mr Lungu said. “The police act selectively in Zambia under this government, one rule for those that support the government of the UPND, another that restricts those that have divergent views.”

The alliance is also demanding that the treason trial be opened to live coverage. Mr Lungu said past treason trials involving army generals, such as the late Christon Tembo, were covered openly. He said the present case should be held to the same standard.

“Here we are with a treason trial of civilians, namely Brian Mundubile; our leaders, including the media, are barred from covering the proceedings. Give us live coverage,” he said.

Access to the court itself has become a point of friction. Green Party leader Peter Sinkamba said blocking the Lusaka High Court premises had become a culture under the United Party for National Development (UPND) government whenever there was a case involving Mr Mundubile. Mr Sinkamba said he had gone to the court to file documents but met obstruction from police officers manning the premises during the bail hearing.

Tuesday’s ruling now carries weight well beyond the 18 applicants. If the court upholds the State’s objection, the detainees face further delay while the application is refiled. If it rejects the objection, the court will move straight to whether Mr Mundubile, Mr Zulu and the others should be released while their case proceeds. Either way, the decision will shape the course of the most closely watched prosecution of the post-election period

World.title: Here Is Who Pays More Under Zambia’s 2027 Budget Tax Measures
World.content:
High earners, small companies, mobile money users and mining shareholders face a heavier tax load from January 2027. Finance and National Planning Minister Dr Situmbeko Musokotwane has proposed a package of revenue measures expected to raise an extra K10.8 billion. The package raises Value Added Tax (VAT) to 16.5 per cent from 16 per cent and adds a new top Pay As You Earn (PAYE) rate of 39.5 per cent. It also lifts corporate income tax on lower-rated income, increases the mobile money levy across all bands and sharply raises duties on plastics.

Dr Musokotwane set out the measures when he presented the K284.8 billion 2027 National Budget to Parliament. He said the successful implementation of the Grow Zambia Agenda required strong, sustainable and predictable domestic revenue. The proposals, he said, would balance support for productive economic activity with the need for individuals and businesses to contribute fairly to national development. The measures would take effect on January 1, 2027.

The new PAYE band is aimed at the top of the income ladder. Individuals earning more than K37,000 a month will pay a top marginal rate of 39.5 per cent on the portion of income above that line. Dr Musokotwane moved to reassure most salaried workers that their payslips would not change under the measure.

“In simple terms, those earning K37,000 per month and below will continue to be taxed under the current regime and will therefore not be affected by this measure. Only the additional income above K37,000 per month will be taxed at 39.5 per cent,” Dr Musokotwane said.

Companies will also pay more. The corporate income tax rate will rise by five percentage points on income currently taxed at 20 per cent and below. VAT moves to 16.5 per cent, which the minister described as part of the Government’s commitment to strengthen domestic revenue mobilisation. Because VAT applies to most goods and services, it will touch nearly every household budget.

Mobile money users will reach deeper into their wallets. The minister proposed to increase the mobile money levy across all bands, so every transaction tier will cost more. For the millions of Zambians who send, receive and save money on their phones, this is likely to be the measure they feel most often.

The mining sector faces a new set of charges. Dr Musokotwane proposed to raise withholding tax on dividends paid by mining companies to 15 per cent from zero, and to introduce a five per cent export duty on zinc concentrates. Mining, mineral processing and exploration licence fees, area charges and related fees will also rise. He said this would align Zambia’s licensing regime with international good practice.

Plastics are the target of the steepest increases in the package. Customs duty on single-use plastics will double to 200 per cent from 100 per cent. An additional duty of K8 per bottle will be introduced on plastic bottles, and the extra duty on selected plastic articles will rise to 30 per cent from 15 per cent. The measures are framed as part of the Government’s environmental sustainability agenda.

A cluster of import duties is designed to shield local industry. Customs duty on imported ceramic tiles will rise to 40 per cent from 25 per cent. Selected imported aluminium bars, rods and profiles will attract a 20 per cent selected goods sales tax and 25 per cent customs duty. The selected goods sales tax on imported meat, including beef, sheep and goat meat, will rise to 30 per cent from 20 per cent.

Shoppers will also see the effect on cooking oil and packaging. Crude soya bean and sunflower oils will attract 15 per cent customs duty and a 10 per cent selected goods sales tax to encourage local production. The selected goods sales tax on imported cement packaging and woven bags will be harmonised at 30 per cent. The minister also proposed ending the customs duty exemption and VAT zero-rating on energy-saving appliances. Second-hand clothing and handbags will be excluded from the duty relief given to approved public benefit organisations.

The package is not all tightening. Dr Musokotwane proposed a 100 per cent customs duty suspension and a VAT exemption on imported raw materials used to manufacture sanitary products locally. Customs duty will also be suspended on safari vehicles, hospitality equipment and communications infrastructure. That relief supports the target of five million international tourist arrivals under President Hakainde Hichilema’s Grow Zambia Agenda.

Small-scale gold miners received a direct incentive to trade through official channels. The minister proposed to cut mineral royalty for artisanal and small-scale miners who sell to Government-approved aggregators to three per cent from six per cent. The measure is meant to pull a largely informal trade into the tax net. It sits alongside plans for a state gold trading agency to aggregate production.

Businesses that report losses year after year will face a narrower minimum alternative tax. Dr Musokotwane said the regime would apply only where a business recorded losses for three consecutive years.

“This will ensure that only businesses with a persistent pattern of loss declaration are brought into the alternative tax net while allowing businesses facing recurring downturns to recover and return to profitability,” Dr Musokotwane said.

The tax drive supports a budget that leans more heavily than ever on money raised at home. Domestic revenues of K233.7 billion will fund 82.1 per cent of spending, up from 58.7 per cent in 2021 and 76 per cent in 2024. Borrowing will account for K41.9 billion and grants from cooperating partners for K9.2 billion. The minister was blunt about the reasoning.

“There are no donors to pay, we must pay ourselves,” Dr Musokotwane said.

Debt remains a heavy claim on that revenue. The Treasury has set aside K67.6 billion for debt service in 2027, made up of K50.8 billion for domestic debt and K16.8 billion for external debt. Debt service sits within K90.5 billion, or 31.8 per cent of the budget, allocated to general public services.

Early reaction from economic and business voices was broadly positive. International Monetary Fund (IMF) Resident Representative for Zambia Dr Reginald Darius described the budget as growth-oriented and said revenue mobilisation would be critical to preserving fiscal stability and debt sustainability. Zambia Association of Manufacturers president Ashu Sagar said the increase in certain taxes was a move to support the social sector. Zambia Chamber of Commerce and Industry (ZACCI) chief executive officer Emmanuel Mumba said the incentives for manufacturing were a plus for local value addition.

To give effect to the measures, Dr Musokotwane proposed amendments to the Income Tax Act, the Customs and Excise Act and the Value Added Tax Act, among other laws. Parliament will now debate the proposals before they take effect in the new year.

World.title: E-government and decentralization key to improved service delivery
World.content:
Government has said deliberate investments in e-government and decentralization are driving public service transformation and anchoring the Grow Zambia agenda.

Speaking at the Association of Public Administration and Management conference, Secretary to the Cabinet Patrick Kangwa commended the Association for Public Administration of Zambia (APAZ) and partners for organizing the conference, saying it comes at a time when all institutions must align to the next phase of national development.

Mr Kangwa said the government has invested deliberately in e-government and service digitization, noting that citizens can now access several services online.

“Today, citizens can complete end-to-end processes for tax payments, road service licenses, land rates, and ground rent without unnecessary delays,” he said.

He cited the recent launch of the online passport application system by the Ministry of Home Affairs and Internal Security and the planned roll-out of the digital national registration card, saying, “they are the result of deliberate planning and execution aimed at making public services faster, transparent, and accessible.”

Mr Kangwa said the second major milestone is the implementation of the decentralization policy, stating that, Decentralization sits at the heart of President Hakainde Hichilema’s development agenda, adding that devolving functions, resources and decision-making to local authorities is empowering communities to manage their own development.

He said the targets set by government are not theoretical, pointing to the transformation of the former Rocky Gardens in Lusaka West into one of Africa’s biggest industrial parks by the Wonderful Group conglomerate, which is now producing packaging materials and fertilizer, including a new urea plant commissioned by the President on October 16, creating over 6,000 jobs and projected to bring in US$5 billion by 2029.

“You must make sure the private sector feels the facilitation and enabling role that we play as public administration,” he said.

He urged public service workers to embrace changes in systems and structures, break down silos, and build institutions that deliver consistently for citizens.

Ministry of Local Government and Rural Development permanent secretary for administration Gabriel Pollen said its partnership with the Association for Public Administration of Zambia (APAZ) was born out of the passion for duty demonstrated by the association’s leadership.

Dr Pollen said when the APAZ team visited his Ministry, he saw an opportunity to champion a partnership that would reflect the practicality of the public sector for the development of the country, and worked with the office of the Secretary to the Cabinet to ensure the conference took place.

“Seeing public administrators and public administration enthusiasts in one room gives me hope about the future that it holds,” he said.

Dr Pollen expressed concern over the low response from local authorities, who are the main stakeholders of the conference, but said the inaugural conference will give special momentum going forward, and encouraged staff in the Ministry of Local Government and all local authorities to affiliate with professional associations such as APAZ because regardless of backgrounds, all are public administrators.

Association of Public Administrators of Zambia (APAZ) president Mudonda Sikawala said the organisation is focusing on transforming into a professional association backed by an Act of Parliament to regulate thousands of practicing but unregulated administrators.

He said the association, formed by public administration enthusiasts in 2020, has grown to over 150 members across five provinces, adding that it needs the Secretary to Cabinet’s guidance and wisdom as its new patron to move to the next phase.

He said efforts are focused on transforming APAZ into a professional association backed by an act of parliament, in order to attain the same recognition already achieved by professions such as accountancy, lawyers and other professions.

Mr Sikawala assured the government of APAZ’s readiness to support the Grow Zambia agenda, recommending that the Ninth National Development Plan and the next five budget cycles be synced to the agenda for policy coherence and easy monitoring.

He announced that 14 individuals and organisations are being awarded this year, and thanked ZESCO and the Ministry of Local Government and Rural Development for their support ahead of a bigger event in June 2027.
