World.title: 2027 budget targets production, infrastructure growth
World.content:
Minister of Finance and National Planning Situmbeko Musokotwane has unveiled an ambitious production and infrastructure expansion programme under the 2027 national budget, targeting increased electricity generation, agricultural output, mining production and tourism arrivals as Government shifts its focus from economic stabilisation to accelerated growth.

Presenting the K284.8 billion 2027 Budget to Parliament themed ‘Grow Zambia: From Stabilisation to Unlocking Opportunities, Creating Jobs and Improving Livelihoods for All, Dr Musokotwane said Government plans to add more than 1,400 megawatts of electricity to the national grid in 2027, largely from non-hydropower sources.

He said Government would continue implementing cost-reflective electricity tariffs, strengthen Zesco’s operational and financial performance and expand investment in solar, thermal and other alternative energy sources.

The programme will also include transmission projects linking Zambia with Tanzania, Malawi and the Democratic Republic of Congo, while K391.3 million has been allocated to the Grid Resilience Programme to modernise electricity distribution infrastructure and improve power reliability.

Agriculture and livestock have been identified as major drivers of the growth agenda, accounting for five of its eight production targets.

These include producing 10 million tonnes of maize, three million tonnes of soya beans, one million tonnes each of wheat and sugar, and generating US$1 billion annually from beef exports.

To support the targets, Government has allocated K22.7 billion towards agriculture, fisheries and livestock interventions, including K9.1 billion for the Farmer Input Support Programme.

Dr Musokotwane announced plans to establish a Farm Block Development Agency to coordinate infrastructure development, attract private investment and promote productive utilisation of agricultural land.

He further said Government will also transition the Farmer Input Support Programme towards an agricultural loan scheme beginning in 2027, while expanding irrigation, mechanisation, access to affordable financing and out-grower arrangements.

In livestock, K100 million has been allocated for the establishment of beef compartments, alongside interventions in animal disease control, improved breeding, abattoir facilities and access to international markets.

Moreover, In the mining sector, Dr Musokotwane said the target would be supported by expansion programmes at major mines, including First Quantum Minerals, Barrick Lumwana, Konkola Copper Mines and Mopani Copper Mines, as well as the development of new projects such as Kitumba and KoBold.

The Minister has allocated K1.2 billion to mining-related activities, including K467.2 million for geological mapping and K450.7 million to support artisanal and small-scale miners.

Government will also establish a gold trading agency to formalise gold transactions and reduce mineral royalty from six percent to three percent for artisanal and small-scale miners selling through Government-approved aggregators.

Tourism is expected to benefit from measures aimed at increasing international arrivals to five million from 2.3 million recorded in 2025.

Dr Musokotwane said Government would work with the private sector to improve access to tourism destinations, strengthen destination marketing, diversify tourism products and attract international conferences, meetings and exhibitions.

The strategy will also involve packaging multiple tourism destinations into combined travel experiences, upgrading access roads and airports, and strengthening local supply chains for food, furniture, linen and crafts.

He noted that to encourage investment and reduce operating costs, Government has proposed suspending customs duty on safari vehicles, hospitality equipment and communications infrastructure used in tourism operations.

The Minister has allocated K1.4 billion to tourism programmes, with additional infrastructure investment expected to improve connectivity to major tourism destinations.

On infrastructure and aviation, Government plans to construct, upgrade and rehabilitate 787 kilometres of roads across the country in 2027, with priority projects including Kazungula-Sesheke, Kisasa-Mwinilunga and Chipata-Lundazi.

Construction of the Lobito railway line is expected to begin in the fourth quarter of 2027, while the rehabilitation of TAZARA will be accompanied by the development of a dry port at Kapiri Mposhi.

Government has allocated K18.1 billion towards road infrastructure and K2.4 billion for provincial airport development.

Mansa and Mfuwe airports are expected to be completed in 2027, while construction works at Nakonde will continue.

Construction of Choma Airport and upgrades at Chipata, Mongu and Solwezi airports are also expected to commence next year.

World.title: Musokotwane presents k284.8 billion 2027 budget
World.content:
Minister of Finance and National Planning Situmbeko Musokotwane has presented a proposed National Budget of 284.8 billion kwacha for the year 2027, equivalent to 28.4 percent of the Gross Domestic Product (GDP).

Dr Musokotwane says 2027 will be highly financed through domestic revenues of about K233.7 billion, representing 82.1 percent of the total budget.

Speaking when he presented the 2027 national budget in Parliament today, Dr Musokotwane added another source of financing will be borrowing from domestic and external sources amounting to K41.9 billion, representing 14.7 percent of the total budget.

Dr Musokotwane highlighted one of the government’s strategic focus since 2021 has been to strengthen fiscal sustainability through improved resource mobilisation and expenditure rationalisation.

Presenting the 2027 National budget expenditure, Dr Musokotwane revealed that about 90.5 billion kwachas will go towards general public services, 75.9 billion to economic affairs, while over K38.2 billion kwacha will be spent on education, a sector that has been given the highest allocation of the total budget at 13.4 percent.

Meanwhile, the health sector has been allocated K30.3 billion, representing 10.6 percent of the Budget on the health function.

To strengthen social protection and reduce vulnerability, Dr Musokotwane proposed an expenditure of K16.2 billion or 5.7 percent of the Budget, of which K10.4 billion will be spent on the Social Cash Transfer programme to support over 1.6 million beneficiary households up from 1.5 million in the 2026 Budget.

“The monthly transfer will be increased to K450 for eligible beneficiary households and K650 for households with eligible persons with disabilities. K5.2 billion will be spent on the public service pension funds to reduce waiting time from retirement to when the pension is paid,” he said.

As part of the government’s commitment to strengthen domestic revenues, Dr Musokotwane proposed adjustments in various taxation including the Value Added Tax rate that he proposed to adjust from 16 percent to 16.5.

The Minister also proposed to increase Corporate Income Tax rates by 5 percentage points on all income currently taxed at 20 percent and below.

“To rationalise the company tax regime which is currently characterised by preferential rates and arbitrage, I propose to increase Corporate Income Tax rates by 5 percentage points on all income currently taxed at 20 percent and below. This measure will ensure neutrality, fairness and alignment of the tax system,” he stated.

He also proposed to increase withholding tax on dividends paid by mining companies to 15 percent from zero percent, noting that this will align with tax treatment of dividends distributed by companies in other sectors.

Other tax adjustments by Dr Musokotwane was the proposal to introduce a top marginal rate of 39.5 percent PAYE tax for individuals earning above K37,000 per month.

He explained that those earning K37,000 per month and below will continue to be taxed under the current regime and will therefore not be affected by this measure.

Meanwhile, to lower capital costs and enhance Zambia’s competitiveness as a high value tourism destination, Dr Musokotwane proposed to suspend customs duty on safari vehicles, hospitality equipment and communications infrastructure.

The theme for the 2027 Budget is: Grow Zambia: From Stabilisation to Unlocking Opportunities, Creating Jobs and Improving Livelihoods for All.

The Budget presented provides a clear policy direction with specific interventions to achieve the Grow Zambia Agenda and will require concerted efforts from various stakeholders.

World.title: Engineers challenged to catalyze Grow Zambia Agenda
World.content:
Government has urged engineers to play a pivotal role in contributing to the achievement of the Grow Zambia Agenda through quality infrastructure development.

Ministry of Infrastructure and Urban Development Permanent Secretary

Albert Malama, said infrastructure remains a key driver of economic growth, and engineers are at the centre of delivering the projects that will transform the country.

Mr Malama said this when he officiated at the second annual public forum for the Association of Consulting Engineers of Zambia (ACEZ) on construction contracts held at Urban Hotel in Lusaka.

He said the government recognises the important role that professional bodies such as ACEZ play in supporting national development, and values their expertise and technical guidance in the infrastructure sector.

“Government recognises the important role that professional bodies such as the Association of Consulting Engineers of Zambia play in supporting national development, and values their expertise and technical guidance,” Mr Malama said.

He noted that the successful delivery of infrastructure requires collaboration, mutual understanding and clearly defined responsibilities among different stakeholders.

Mr Malama commended ACEZ for bringing together engineers, lawyers, quantity surveyors, architects, procurement specialists and contractors to discuss the distinctive nature of construction contracts.

He said challenges in the construction industry cannot be addressed by one profession in isolation, and the forum had created an opportunity for a more balanced and holistic discussion.

“A project can encounter serious challenges if the contractual arrangements are poorly understood or inadequately administered,” Mr Malama said.

He cited issues relating to risk allocation, payment obligations, variations, extensions of time, design responsibilities and dispute resolution as having significant implications on project delivery and quality.

Mr Malama urged engineers to appreciate the distinctive nature of construction contracts, as this will ensure projects are delivered on time, within budget and to the required quality key to achieving the Grow Zambia Agenda.

The forum was held under the ACEZ core values of transparency, accountability, dynamism, innovation, equity and sustainability.

Meanwhile ACEZ president Trephor Musonda appreciated government for the support shown to the association.

He said the association was encouraged to receive positive response from government to officiate the event.

World.title: Somalia: Court Says President Term Extension Unlawful
World.content:
Somalia's Supreme Court ruled on Thursday that the extension of the president's term by one year, which sparked violent clashes with the opposition, was "unlawful".

President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud's term ended in May, but his government declared a "transition period" that gave him an extra year in office to prepare for the first nationwide democratic elections, which are due in April and May 2027.

Mohamud has argued this was legal under amendments to the constitution passed by parliament in March, but that vote was boycotted by opposition parties and regional leaders.

On Thursday, the Supreme Court ruled that the amendments did not apply to his current term, and that he should have left office in May.



Mohamud announced late Wednesday that he was dismissing the chief justice, Bashe Yusuf Ahmed, and appointing a replacement.

There were unconfirmed reports that Ahmed was under arrest on Thursday.

The presidency's statement, posted on Facebook, did not reference the imminent decision on the constitution, saying only that the dismissal was due to "concerns... about the need for an efficient and fair judiciary".

The court rejected the dismissal in a separate statement, saying the move was designed "to obstruct the administration of justice in the constitutional case filed before the Supreme Court".

"The dismissal announced in the statement published on the Presidency's Facebook page is null and void," it added.

Around for 30 years now, Capcom's survival horror franchise has run unconstrained with the core concept that sets it apart from other zombie media: in its universe, the undead are the product of pharmaceutical experimentation, with various virus strains (the t-Virus being the most famous) mutating some of the infected into "superior", unstoppable beings.

The match, which served as the final preparatory test for both sides ahead of the 2026 World Amputee Football Federation (WAFF) World Cup in Mexico, got off to a lively start, with the visitors showing physicality and defensive solidity to contain Ghana's attacking threat.

Six minutes into the game, skipper Richard Arthur Opentil set up Fusieni Iddi, who shot weakly into the arms of goalkeeper Frances Fallah.

Three minutes later, Liberian skipper Matthew Joe tested Ghana goalkeeper Atsu Abor with a long-range effort, which the latter handled with ease.

World.title: Ghana: W Sports Int'l Donates Sports Equipment to Legon Presec
World.content:
W Sports International last Thursday donated sports kits to the Presbyterian Boys' Senior High School (PRESEC), Legon, under its sports sponsorship programme.

The items included jerseys, soccer uniforms, polo shirts and balls. The donation forms part of efforts to modernise sports in Ghana's second-cycle institutions and create opportunities for young talents to excel beyond the classroom.

PRESEC Legon is the first senior high school in the Greater Accra Region to benefit from the organisation's sports kit sponsorship programme.

The event was attended by the Minister of Sports and Recreation, Mr Kofi Adams; Dr Ernest Ofori Sarpong, Global President of Odadee and Board Chairman of PRESEC; the Headmaster of PRESEC, Mr David Odjija; members of the Odadee fraternity; teachers and students.



Presenting the items, the Chairman of W Sports International, Nana Bediako Brogya Sarpong, who is the Dompiahene of the Agogo Asante Akyem Traditional Area and a former student of Prempeh College, urged schools to look beyond traditional rivalries and support the collective development of Ghanaian students.

He acknowledged the rivalry between PRESEC Legon and Prempeh College during the National Maths and Science Quiz and sporting competitions but said such healthy competition should never become a barrier to recognising excellence or supporting one another.

Nana Sarpong explained that his decision to extend W Sports International's sponsorship to PRESEC was motivated by the school's outstanding record in academic and extracurricular activities, including its achievements in the National Science and Maths Quiz, robotics, soccer, hockey and basketball.

Mr Adams commended W Sports International and its Board Chairman, Nana Sarpong, for selecting PRESEC as the 21st beneficiary school nationwide.

He said the donation demonstrated a practical commitment to investing in the nurturing and development of young sporting talents.

Receiving the items on behalf of the school, Dr Ernest Ofori Sarpong expressed gratitude to Nana Sarpong and the W Sports International team, saying the intervention would strengthen the school's sporting activities.

He observed that although PRESEC had established itself as a centre of academic excellence, the sponsorship presented another opportunity for the school to demonstrate its strength in sports.

World.title: Ghana: Black Rock Belongs to Nungua - Mankralo
World.content:
The Office of the Nungua Mankralo has rebuffed claims by the Tema and Sanshie clans that the location of Angmu T3 (The Meridian Rock) falls under their authority.

According to the Mankralo, available records, court rulings and customary evidence all point to the fact that the site where the rock is located falls under the jurisdiction and authority of Nungua.

The claims follow a recent outburst by the Sanshie Clan of Tema that the Gborbu Wulomo had no right to perform customary rites around the rock because it falls directly under the authority of Tema.

Keep up with the latest headlines on WhatsApp | LinkedIn

However, at a press conference in Nungua on Tuesday, the Nungua Mankralo, ShwÉÉnÉtalÉ Têstê Nii Bortey Kofi Frankwa, said the Black Rock was among the 99 deities of Nungua Kple Spirituality.

He said the annual Djenten rite was an established Nungua tradition performed exclusively by the Gborbu Wulomo Shitse, the town's spiritual head, whose customary responsibilities included conducting important sacred rites for the community's deities.

The office cited Professor M.J. Field's 1937 publication, Religion and Medicine of the Ga People, which it said associated all 99 Nungua deities with the Nuumo Gorbu Temple, known locally as Koomli, in Nungua tradition.

It also relied on Field's Social Organisation of the Ga People, published in 1940 and widely cited, which identified the Gborbu Wulomo Shitse as the traditional timekeeper responsible for announcing the town's rites and festivals.

Further evidence, it said, came from Carl Christian Reindorf's 1895 publication, History of the Gold Coast and Asante, which identified Borkete Lawe as the priest of Angmu, supporting Nungua's account of its spiritual custodianship and ritual authority.

The statement also cited a Bureau of Ghana Languages publication and a book by Dr Joseph Nii Abakar Mensah as documentary records affirming the Gborbu Wulomo Shitse's association with Angmu and the annual Djenten rite.

It rejected claims that Angmu and Oshwe were the same deity, saying Angmu was known in Nungua Kple tradition as Sebrebedu, while Oshwe Yaado was a separate deity with distinct spiritual and customary responsibilities.

On the boundary dispute, the office cited an 1892 judgement by Chief Justice Hutchinson and a 1904 ruling by Crowther, which it said recognised Nungua's right of access to Angmu, historically described as the Black Rock in the sea.

Close 

It argued that the 1952 compulsory acquisition for Tema Township and Port altered administrative arrangements but did not extinguish traditional boundaries or customary rights, stressing that administrative jurisdiction did not establish traditional ownership.

The office further disputed claims that Professor Field placed the Tema-Nungua boundary at Asokplotsonaa, saying page 87 of her book contained no such statement and instead discussed Ataa Sakumo's historical connection with Nungua.

It also pointed to the 2016 Tema Port expansion, saying the Nungua Traditional Authority was consulted and its permission sought before work began, which it considered further recognition of Nungua's traditional interest in the area.

World.title: Ghana: Stanbic Bank Supports Weep Not Child Foundation
World.content:
The Internal Control Unit of Stanbic Bank Ghana has supported the Weep Not Child Foundation at Ahwerease-Darmang, near Nsawam, with equipment and financial assistance to improve the foundation's operations and support for children in its care.

The donation, led by the Head of Internal Control, Paa Kwesi Simpson, was made under the team's Employee Community Initiative, through which employees contribute to community development efforts.

The foundation received a grinding mill and accessories, a 508-litre freezer and GH¢5,000 in cash to support its immediate needs.



Mr Simpson said the initiative was driven by the team's desire to contribute to communities beyond its regular professional responsibilities.

He said while the Internal Control team's core mandate centred on risk management and controls, its members also recognised the importance of responding to social needs within communities.

"This initiative reflects our shared commitment to making a meaningful impact in the communities we serve and contributing positively beyond our 'risk and control' responsibilities," he said.

Mr Simpson explained that the team chose to support the foundation after considering some of the practical needs that could make a difference to its operations and the welfare of the children.

He said the items were intended to provide useful and lasting support rather than serve as a one-off gesture, adding that the team was pleased to contribute in an area where its assistance could be put to immediate use.

Receiving the donation, the Founder of the Weep Not Child Foundation, Nana Ama Benewaa I, expressed appreciation to the Stanbic Bank team for the support.

She said the donation had come at an important time for the foundation, which continued to cater for the needs of children under its care.

Nana Ama Benewaa noted that the grinding mill, freezer and cash support would help address some of the foundation's immediate requirements and ease aspects of its day-to-day operations.

"This support has come at a good time for us. The items will be put to good use and will help us respond to some of the needs of the children and the foundation," she said.

She thanked the Internal Control team for identifying the foundation as a beneficiary and taking steps to provide practical assistance.

She also encouraged the team to sustain its community-focused initiatives, saying continued support from individuals and organisations could help institutions such as the foundation provide better care for vulnerable children.

World.title: Ghana: AMA Gives Traders 48 Hours to Vacate Bus Stops
World.content:
The Accra Metropolitan Assembly (AMA) has given traders occupying unauthorised bus stops in the city 48 hours to vacate the areas or face enforcement action as part of efforts to restore order and ease traffic congestion.

The Assembly says the occupation of designated bus stops by traders undermines their intended purpose, obstructs the movement of vehicles and passengers, and creates unnecessary traffic congestion.

The Public Affairs Officer of the AMA, Mr Gilbert Nii Ankrah, said in an interview on Wednesday that the directive formed part of sustained efforts by the Assembly to enforce its by-laws and restore order in the city's central business district.

He said the decision was also informed by concerns raised by commercial drivers about the activities of traders at designated bus stops.

According to him, the concerns expressed by drivers had reinforced the Assembly's resolve to intensify enforcement and ensure that the facilities remained available for their intended use.

World.title: 9 mystery fingerprints from OJ Simpson murder case could hold new clues more than 30 years later

Nine fingerprints that went unidentified during the original OJ Simpson murder investigation could hold new clues more than 30 years later — and one filmmaker believes advances in forensic technology could help reveal who left them behind.

Ari Mark co-directed the Peacock docuseries "OJ's Accomplice," which reexamines the 1994 murders of Simpson's ex-wife, Nicole Brown Simpson, and her friend, Ron Goldman. The series explores the theory that the former NFL star may not have acted alone, focusing on convicted drug trafficker and Simpson associate Joey Ippolito, who reportedly had ties to organized crime.

Mark told Fox News Digital he wants investigators to consider reexamining nine fingerprints recovered from the crime scene that could not be matched to any known samples during the original investigation.

NICOLE BROWN SIMPSON TOLD FORMER LOVER SHE'D 'RATHER DIE' THAN RETURN TO O.J. SIMPSON BEFORE HER MURDER

"The fact that there's nine fingerprints sitting around that nobody wants to put through a system that's very updated and technologically not what it was before, that just seems unnecessary," Mark said. "Just do it."

"You can take latent prints and analyze those in a way that you couldn't before," Mark continued. "Also, remember, the systems over time are obviously collecting more data and more people. So, if you're looking for a match, you have a greater chance of getting one all these years later."

In 1995, the Los Angeles Times reported that none of the identifiable fingerprints investigators collected at the Bundy Drive condominium where Brown Simpson and Goldman were murdered matched Simpson. Fingerprint specialist Gilbert Aguilar, a defense witness, testified that police knew that Simpson's fingerprints did not match the identifiable prints recovered at the crime scene.

Under questioning by lead defense attorney Johnnie Cochran Jr., Aguilar testified that nine prints found at Bundy Drive could not be matched to any known sample. According to the Los Angeles Times, Simpson's lawyers argued that unknown attackers committed the murders and that detectives failed to adequately investigate that possibility because they quickly concluded Simpson had killed his ex-wife and her friend.

According to Aguilar's testimony, investigators compared the unidentified prints with those of Simpson, Brown Simpson and 58 friends, relatives and acquaintances, but found no matches. Aguilar also testified that investigators searched federal and state computerized fingerprint databases without finding a match.

Mark said his goal for the docuseries was "to raise enough questions that it gets a second look."

"I'm very careful about the call to action because there are victims' families involved here and you would want them to be supportive of that," Mark said. "That would be my first priority. Assuming it was something they were interested in, I think everyone deserves to know what actually happened, and if that involves a second person, third person or whatever it is, great."

Aguilar, who appears in the docuseries, raised the possibility that today's expanded fingerprint databases could produce a match.

"At the crime scene, there were nine identifiable prints that I never identified to whom they belong," Aguilar said in the documentary. "Back in 1994, you're running prints through AFIS (Automated Fingerprint Identification System). But first, it's checking everybody that's been arrested by the Los Angeles Police Department. Then it would be run through Sacramento. Then run through all the Western states."

"If somebody is arrested outside your database, like in New York or the state of Florida, you’re not going to get anything," Aguilar continued. "LAPD has all the prints and they could have them [tested again]. They may or may not. I don’t know. It’s up to them now."

It is unclear whether investigators have reexamined the nine unidentified fingerprints using modern forensic technology or updated fingerprint databases.

An LAPD spokesperson told Fox News Digital that the investigation remains open.

"I think it's impossible if you're in her position to speculate about theories, and I don't blame her for that," Mark said. "Everything about her felt like the little sister of somebody who's an unfortunate victim."

Simpson and Brown Simpson married in 1985. They had two children, Sydney and Justin, and divorced in 1992. Two years later, Brown Simpson and Goldman were found stabbed to death.

World.title: Jewish leaders in Michigan prepare to work with Abdul El-Sayed despite lingering concerns
World.content:
NEW You can now listen to Fox News articles!

Senator-elect Abdul El-Sayed's victory in Michigan has drawn mixed reactions from Jewish leaders and Jewish Democrats, with some expressing optimism and a willingness to work with him, while others say their concerns remain.

"We congratulate all the winners, and we will work with all the winners," Jewish Federation of Detroit CEO Steven Ingber told Fox News Digital. "The Jewish voice and Jewish vote is not monolithic, meaning, we have people who voted on every side of the aisle on all the races up and down the ballot. And the beauty of being a 501(c)(3) is we don't get to take an opinion and we just get to work with whoever then is elected."

The Jewish Federation is a 501(c)(3) tax-exempt nonprofit, meaning it cannot endorse political candidates or participate in political campaigns on behalf of or in opposition to candidates. Instead, it works with elected officials from across the political spectrum to support Jewish communities.

UNIVERSITY OF MICHIGAN STUDENTS RALLY BEHIND ABDUL EL-SAYED AFTER HIS SENATE WIN OVER MIKE ROGERS

For Ingber, the key is understanding that people have varying reactions to elections, something he said has happened before and will likely happen again.

"I think it's all about unity," he told Fox News Digital. "There'll be an election again in two years. There was an election two years ago. People were upset then, people were happy then. And I think that's the beauty of our system right now is — America will go on."

Throughout his campaign, El-Sayed faced criticism from Jewish leaders and voters who were concerned about his stance on Israel and ties to controversial figures. One remark in particular that struck many Jews the wrong way was El-Sayed's response to the March 2026 attack on Temple Israel in West Bloomfield, Mich.

According to the FBI, Ayman Mohamad Ghazali drove a truck containing commercial-grade fireworks and containers of flammable liquid into Temple Israel on March 12. Ghazali died from a self-inflicted gunshot wound during an exchange of gunfire with synagogue security personnel, investigators said. Following the attack, El-Sayed said, "Hurt people, hurt people," drawing criticism. He later apologized and told Fox News Digital that his comments "might have been misconstrued to be justifying something I did not intend to justify."

EL-SAYED’S HASAN PIKER PROBLEM FOLLOWS HIM TO DEM CONVENTION AS JEWISH VOTERS BREAK RANKS

Democratic strategist Julian Epstein told Fox News Digital that Democrats have been inconsistent when opposing bigotry, particularly when Jews are the targets.

"If you believe in civil rights, right? If you believe [in] pluralism, if you believe in dignity for all, if you're against bigotry, then you don't do it for one group, but not for another, or accept it for another or capitulate on it for others. Because then you really don't believe in the civil rights. You just believe in group preferences at that point," Epstein said.

Epstein predicted that El-Sayed's victory could mean a broader shift among Jewish voters, who have long been a reliable Democratic base.

"I think there's no question that Jewish voters are going to start leaving the Democratic Party," Epstein told Fox News Digital. "They should. I mean, why would you stick with a party that openly tolerates hate directed at you?"

The American Jewish Committee's Detroit chapter (AJC Detroit) acknowledged the historic significance of El-Sayed's election as the first Muslim elected to the U.S. Senate but expressed concern about his public statements.

ABDUL EL-SAYED DELIVERS MAJOR BLOW TO GOP IN MICHIGAN AFTER BRUISING SENATE RACE

"We recognize the historic significance of Dr. El-Sayed becoming the first Muslim elected to the U.S. Senate, a milestone that reflects the promise of American democracy. As a Jewish organization, we understand the profound importance of seeing one’s community represented in government," AJC Detroit's statement read. "Unfortunately, this historic moment has been tarnished by the Senator-elect’s continued anti-Israel rhetoric that alienates countless Jewish Michiganders and other supporters of the State of Israel, and endangers American Jews."

"As a U.S. Senator, El-Sayed will have the responsibility to represent all Michiganders. The Senator-elect proclaimed that America is 'big enough for all of us' but his obsessive hostility toward Israel yet again in his victory speech told many Jewish Michiganders and countless others who support Israel that they are not included," AJC Detroit added.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE OF MEDIA AND CULTURE

Despite the concerns expressed by some Jewish leaders, Ingber urged community leaders to continue calling out antisemitism regardless of which party is responsible.

"We have antisemitism coming at us from both sides, from the far-left, from the far-right. Neither is better, neither is worse," he told Fox News Digital. "Antisemitism isn't a Jewish problem, it's an American problem."

He said Jewish Americans should not retreat from public Jewish life because of rising antisemitism or political divisions.

"Antisemitism and people who don’t want us to succeed in life are not going to stop us from being who we are," Ingber said.

CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

The El-Sayed campaign did not immediately respond to Fox News Digital's request for comment.

Fox News Digital's Paul Steinhauser and Peter D'Abrosca contributed to this report.

World.title: Republican state lawmakers reported Omar to the IRS in 2019
World.content:
NEW You can now listen to Fox News articles!

EXCLUSIVE: A group of Minnesota Republican state lawmakers asked the IRS in August 2019 to "conduct a detailed reexamination" of tax filings by Rep. Ilhan Omar, D-Minn., based on a report from a state board suggesting she filed joint tax returns in 2014 and 2015 with a man she was not legally married to, according to a letter obtained by Fox News Digital.

The letter was sent after the Minnesota Campaign Finance and Public Disclosure Board issued a report on June 6, 2019, indicating that Omar had filed joint tax returns in 2014 and 2015 with Ahmed Hirsi, despite being legally married to another man, Ahmed Nur Said Elmi, at the time.

The joint tax returns came up during the Minnesota Campaign Finance and Public Disclosure Board’s examination of a $1,500 expense associated with Omar’s campaign committee. The board was investigating whether the expenditure was a legitimate campaign-related expense or whether campaign funds had been used to pay for services that benefited Omar personally. The payment was part of a larger $2,250 reimbursement to the Kjellberg Law Office for legal and other services.

ILHAN OMAR ISSUES STUNNING ADMISSION WHEN CONFRONTED WITH BROTHER MARRIAGE RUMORS

In response to the board’s questions, Omar’s campaign committee explained that the Kjellberg Law Office had retained the accounting firm Frederick & Rosen to obtain and review financial records as part of the campaign committee’s efforts to respond to allegations surrounding Omar’s marital history. According to the committee’s explanation, Frederick & Rosen prepared releases for Omar and Ahmed Hirsi to sign, so the firm could obtain copies of their filed joint federal income tax returns for 2014 and 2015 from the IRS.

The board concluded that the committee had not demonstrated that the $1,500 expense benefited the campaign and required Omar to reimburse the committee.

JD VANCE SAYS DOJ LOOKING INTO IF ILHAN OMAR COMMITTED IMMIGRATION FRAUD AMID BROTHER-MARRIAGE ALLEGATIONS

Omar married Hirsi in 2002 in their Muslim faith tradition and that they ended their relationship in that tradition in 2008, Newsweek reported. She then legally married Ahmed Nur Said Elmi in February 2009, according to public records, as reported by Newsweek.

According to divorce documents obtained by Fox News Digital, Omar legally divorced Elmi in December 2017.

Carla Kjellberg, a lawyer for Omar and her campaign committee, stated during the board proceedings that Frederick & Rosen’s services provided "some personal benefit to Rep. Omar," because "there was an issue with her tax returns that needed to be corrected regardless of her status as a candidate," according to the board’s report.

In a letter to then-IRS Commissioner Charles Rettig dated Aug. 6, 2019, the state lawmakers asked the IRS to undertake a review in light of the Minnesota Campaign Finance Board report.

"Due to recent developments, I believe probable cause exists for an investigation into Rep. Omar's tax filings," read the letter, signed by Minnesota state Reps. Steve Drazkowski, Linda Runbeck, Glenn Gruenhagen, Shane Mekeland, John Poston, Eric Lucero, Duane Quam, Tim Miller, Cal Bahr and Jeremy Munson.

Drazkowski told Fox News Digital that the IRS never responded to the request.

The IRS did not respond to Fox News Digital's request for comment. Fox News Digital could not confirm whether the IRS followed through with the lawmakers’ request.

Federal tax confidentiality rules generally restrict what the agency can disclose about individual taxpayers. The Minnesota Campaign Finance and Public Disclosure Board issued its findings on June 6, 2019, following two complaints filed by Drazkowski. Although the board required Omar to repay the $1,500 that her campaign had paid the Kjellberg Law Firm for Frederick & Rosen’s services related to the tax returns, it rejected the allegation that this money was payment for Omar’s personal divorce proceeding, in which Kjellberg also represented her.

The board also required Omar to repay campaign funds used for certain travel expenses, including trips to Boston, New York and Washington, D.C.

Following the board's 2019 findings, Omar said she was "glad" the process was complete and welcomed the board's determination regarding allegations that she had improperly used campaign funds for personal expenses. However, she did not address the portion of the board’s report concerning the joint tax returns she submitted with Hirsi.

Omar did not respond to Fox News Digital’s request for comment.

In a separate letter obtained by Fox News Digital, the Republican state lawmakers, led by Drazkowski, asked Cynthia Bauerly, then-commissioner of the Minnesota Department of Revenue, in August 2019 to review Omar's joint tax filings.

Drazkowski said neither Bauerly nor the Minnesota Department of Revenue responded to the lawmakers' request.

The Minnesota Department of Revenue did not respond to Fox News Digital's request for comment.

The letter from the lawmakers urging the state and federal tax reporting agencies to investigate Omar’s joint tax filings came two months after Drazkowski urged Rep. Angie Craig, D-Minn., to refer his concerns about Omar's tax filings to the House Ethics Committee.

As previously reported by Fox News Digital, Craig told Drazkowski in a letter that he could submit information himself to the Office of Congressional Ethics (OCE), which was renamed to the Office of Congressional Conduct in 2021.

The congressional ethics process allows members of the public and lawmakers to submit information concerning alleged misconduct, although the independent ethics office and the House Committee on Ethics have separate procedures.

CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

In late October, Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin said on Fox News that the federal investigation into Omar regarding potential immigration and marriage fraud had been referred to the Department of Justice (DOJ) as a "large case" that targets multiple individuals rather than just one person.

The DHS did not respond to Fox News Digital's request for comment on whether the investigation is looking into the 2014 and 2015 joint tax filings flagged by the state lawmakers in 2019.

World.title: Popular drinks linked to heart attacks, cardiac arrest in young adults, study finds
World.content:
NEW You can now listen to Fox News articles!

Energy drinks and stimulant-containing supplements have been linked to the risk of serious heart problems, including cardiac arrest and heart attacks, particularly among young adults.

That’s according to new research released by the American Heart Association, which will be presented at the AHA Scientific Sessions in Chicago, November 6–9, 2026.

A retrospective observational analysis looked at more than 28,000 reports submitted to the FDA of cardiovascular events, including cardiac arrest, myocardial infarction (heart attack), ventricular arrhythmias (abnormal rhythms), palpitations, tachycardia (rapid heart rate), chest pain and syncope (fainting).

EVEN OCCASIONAL MARIJUANA USE LINKED TO HIGHER STROKE RISK, STUDY FINDS

Cardiac arrest appeared in reports involving caffeine- and stimulant-containing products about 11 times as often as in reports involving products without those ingredients.

Heart attacks were reported about 4.5 times as often, while ventricular arrhythmias (abnormal heart rhythms) or palpitations were reported about four times as often, according to the AHA.

Elevated heart rate, chest pain and fainting were also increased among the group consuming those substances.

Approximately 45% of reported cardiovascular events associated with stimulant products involved adults ages 18 to 34.

"We don't know how many people consumed these drinks and didn't report symptoms or those who maybe had symptoms and didn’t report them."

The stimulants included in the study were caffeine, methylxanthines, guarana, yerba mate, synephrine, yohimbine and other compounds. They were consumed in products such as soft drinks, meal replacement shakes, protein bars, smoothies and vitamins.

Caffeine and heart risks

Colin Kane, M.D., pediatric cardiologist and service chief at Children's Health and professor at UT Southwestern Medical Center, said the findings build on earlier case reports about potential heart risks from high caffeine intake.

"We've known through case reports and anecdotal evidence that caffeine in high amounts can be potentially dangerous to people with underlying heart conditions and even those who have normal hearts," Kane, who was not involved in the study, told Fox News Digital.

WHY STACKING SUPPLEMENTS WITHOUT A BLOOD TEST FIRST CAN DO MORE HARM THAN GOOD

It is generally safe for adults to consume up to 400 mg of caffeine per day, which equates to up to five 8-ounce cups of regular black caffeinated coffee, according to a 2026 American Heart Association Scientific Statement on caffeine and cardiovascular disease.

"Some energy drinks have up to three times more caffeine per fluid ounce than brewed coffee, and some pre-workout supplements have more than 12 times as much," senior study author Dr. Pamela Benavidez, a cardiothoracic anesthesiologist at Fairfield Medical Center in Lancaster, Ohio, told Fox News Digital.

"This means one small serving can easily surpass the advised daily limit or more."

Benavidez also warned that these products often include other stimulants like synephrine, yohimbine and methylhexanamine.

"These can interact with caffeine in ways that are not fully understood, especially in young, healthy people," she said.

YOUR DAILY COFFEE HABIT MAY AFFECT YOUR BRAIN AND MOOD IN UNEXPECTED WAYS, STUDY FINDS

The researchers recommend that young people carefully monitor their consumption of caffeine and watch for heart-related symptoms, such as palpitations, chest pain or tightness, lightheadedness, fainting, or a racing or irregular heartbeat during or after use of these products.

"If you notice any of these symptoms, seek medical help right away," Benavidez advised. "If you have a known heart condition, a family history of sudden cardiac events, or take medications that are classified as stimulants or can affect your heart rate/rhythm, you should talk to your doctor before using these products at all."

Kane identified people with underlying heart conditions, particularly those with potentially dangerous heart rhythms and older adults with coronary artery disease, as groups needing particular awareness.

"And there's a whole group of people who may have an underlying heart condition that they're not diagnosed with yet," he added.

Study limitations

The findings are preliminary and have not yet been published as a full peer-reviewed manuscript.

As the study was observational, it could only show an association and could not prove that the products caused the cardiac events.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE HEALTH STORIES

"We don't know how many people consumed these drinks and didn't report symptoms or those who maybe had symptoms and didn’t report them," Kane said.

Also, as the FDA reports were voluntary, they may contain incomplete, inconsistent or selectively submitted data.

CLICK HERE TO 

It is possible that other factors, such as alcohol or drug use, strenuous exercise and undiagnosed heart conditions, may have contributed to the cardiovascular events.

"Anytime you're mixing stimulants and other substances or medications, it can certainly bring up a potential for harm," Kane said.

Industry response

The American Beverage Association, based in Washington, D.C., sent the below statement to Fox News Digital in response to the study.

"Energy drinks have been enjoyed by billions of people around the world for more than 30 years and are recognized as safe by government food safety agencies worldwide. The U.S. Food and Drug Administration, Health Canada, the European Food Safety Authority all relied on the highest quality science when they determined that a moderate daily intake of 400 milligrams of caffeine from all sources is safe for adults."

"Energy drinks have less caffeine than coffeehouse coffee and no regulatory agency has found that their other ingredients interact harmfully with caffeine," the statement concluded.

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

Andrea Wong, chief science officer of the Council for Responsible Nutrition in Washington, D.C., also reacted to the study’s findings.

"Because the analysis does not account for how many consumers actually used these products, whether they were overused or misused, or even the amount of caffeine (or other ingredients) per serving, it cannot determine the incidence of cardiovascular events or quantify the associated risk," she told Fox News Digital.

CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

"Importantly, the reported 11-fold difference in cardiac arrest reporting does not mean consumers are 11 times more likely to experience cardiac arrest."

World.title: Chainsaw robot looks terrifying but has a real job
World.content:
NEW You can now listen to Fox News articles!

If you saw a humanoid robot holding a chainsaw next to train tracks, you'd probably do a double take. I know I would. But that's exactly what's happening in Japan, where a towering chainsaw robot is cutting back branches that could interfere with passing trains. It's a little intimidating to watch, especially when you see how high this machine can reach. Still, there's a pretty good reason railway crews are putting it to work.

Japan's JR East railway company is using the chainsaw robot to handle dangerous maintenance jobs that would normally require workers to operate heavy cutting equipment high above the ground. The robot does the physical work while a person controls its movements from a safer location. I find that reassuring, especially when a chainsaw is involved. So how does this unusual machine actually work, and could it change the way dangerous maintenance jobs get done?

Missed CyberGuy LIVE? Watch the replay and discover five ways to travel smarter and save money.

Our free CyberGuy LIVE class, 5 Ways to Travel Smarter and Save Money, has ended, but you can still watch the full replay. Kurt "CyberGuy" Knutsson walks you through five practical ways to protect your phone and personal information, avoid common travel scams, find better deals, save money on bookings and use technology to make your travels easier and less stressful. No technical experience is needed.

Watch the free replay and downloadable checklist now at CyberGuyLive.com.

HUMANOID ROBOTS PERFORM LIVE SURGERY IN WORLD FIRST

How the chainsaw robot clears railway tracks

The robot has been put to work along JR East's Koumi Line in central Japan, where overgrown branches can create problems for passing trains. What's interesting is how the machine actually handles the cutting. One mechanical arm grips a branch while the other operates the chainsaw. The robot's upper body extends from a boom mounted on a specialized maintenance vehicle, allowing it to reach high above the tracks. That means workers can tackle branches that would normally require someone to operate cutting equipment at height.

The robot even has a name, ZIZAI ZX-3. Japanese manufacturer Nippon Signal announced its delivery to JR East earlier this year. The machine began full-scale maintenance work along the Koumi Line in October. And this technology already has some experience behind it. JR West started using a related robotic system in July 2024. What's especially appealing about this approach is that the machine takes on the dangerous physical work while a trained operator stays at a safer distance.

Who's actually controlling this chainsaw robot?

Now, before you start worrying about robots running around with chainsaws, the ZX-3 is actually controlled by a person. A trained operator guides the robot remotely, deciding where to position its arms and when to start cutting. That's important because working near railway tracks requires careful attention. One wrong move could damage equipment or put someone in danger. So while the robot handles the heavy lifting, a human still makes the decisions.

Nippon Signal designed the ZX-3 to make it easier for workers to control the robot's movements. Right now, its main job is cutting back trees and branches that grow too close to railway lines. However, the company hopes to give it additional tools so it can handle other maintenance work in the future. And here's what I find interesting. Workers still need the skills to do the job, but now they can operate the equipment from a safer location. That's a pretty big change when you're talking about working high above train tracks with a chainsaw.

Why railway companies are turning to robots

Keeping train tracks clear takes more work than you might realize. Branches can grow close enough to interfere with passing trains, and cutting them back sometimes means sending workers high above the tracks with heavy equipment. That brings some serious safety risks, especially when crews are working near electrical infrastructure. Japan is also dealing with a shortage of skilled workers, so JR East is looking for ways to make these jobs safer and less physically demanding.

That's where the chainsaw robot comes in. It can reach areas that would be difficult or dangerous for workers to access while the operator stays at a safer distance. JR East is also changing when some of this work gets done. Since 2022, the company has been moving certain maintenance jobs along the Koumi Line into daytime hours instead of having crews work overnight. That sometimes means temporarily canceling trains, which I'm sure passengers aren't thrilled about. But it also gives workers better conditions and more manageable schedules. And when you combine that with a robot that can handle dangerous cutting work, you can see why JR East is investing in this technology.

NEW AI BRAIN LETS ROBOTS MOVE LIKE HUMANS

Could AI eventually control a robot with a chainsaw?

Now this is where I start having a few more questions. JR East has been investing in artificial intelligence and robotics across its railway operations. The company is exploring ways to use AI for equipment inspections and other maintenance activities. Its broader technology plans include robots that can help inspect infrastructure. That raises an interesting possibility. Could a future version of this chainsaw robot identify an overgrown branch and cut it without someone guiding every movement?

It's certainly a direction robotics developers could explore. AI-powered image analysis could help identify vegetation that threatens railway operations. More advanced systems might eventually assist with some of the decisions an operator makes today. But there's an important difference between what might be possible and what JR East has actually announced.

The ZX-3 currently relies on human control, and JR East has not announced a timeline for making its chainsaw operation fully autonomous. Personally, I think that's worth emphasizing. Giving a robot greater independence sounds impressive until you consider what happens if it misidentifies an object or someone enters its working area. We recently covered how humanoid robots are getting new workplace safety systems. Those safeguards will become even more important as machines take on jobs involving powerful tools.

What this means to you

You may never see this particular chainsaw robot working near your local train station. However, the technology behind it could eventually change how infrastructure gets maintained closer to home. If you ride commuter trains, you already know how frustrating delays can be. Overgrown vegetation can contribute to service disruptions, and railway companies spend considerable time keeping tracks clear. Equipment that helps crews perform those jobs safely and efficiently could eventually benefit passengers. There are potential applications beyond railways, too. Utility companies regularly need to trim vegetation around power lines. Construction crews also handle dangerous work in areas that are difficult to reach. Remotely operated machines could help reduce some of those risks.

Of course, there's another side to this. As robots become more capable, companies will need workers who know how to operate and maintain them. That could create opportunities for new skills while changing the way traditional maintenance jobs are performed. And while robots can reduce certain dangers, they bring their own safety concerns. A machine handling a chainsaw still needs reliable controls and proper oversight. For now, the ZX-3 shows how robotics can help people perform hazardous work without placing them directly in the path of danger.

ONE OF THE WORLD'S HOTTEST INDUSTRIES IS SPARKING A BLUE-COLLAR JOBS BOOM

Kurt's key takeaways

I've seen plenty of humanoid robots doing backflips and showing off what they can do. But there's something different about watching one actually earn its keep. Seeing this robot handle a chainsaw high above the tracks makes me think about the risks workers face doing that job themselves. And if it can help keep railway workers out of dangerous situations, I am all for it. What I especially like is that there's still a person making the decisions. The operator brings the experience while the machine takes on the physically demanding work. That seems like a sensible way to introduce robotics into jobs where mistakes can have serious consequences. What I'll be watching is how quickly companies push these machines toward greater independence. AI is advancing, and I suspect we'll see more robots taking on jobs that once seemed impossible to automate. But when the tool in a robot's hand is a chainsaw, I want to know someone is paying very close attention.

World.title: California prosecutors slam Newsom's death row commutations, accuse governor of putting 'politics over people'
World.content:
NEW You can now listen to Fox News articles!

District attorneys and law enforcement unions across California have publicly condemned Gov. Gavin Newsom following his announcement to commute the sentences of 548 death row inmates, a decision one prosecutor called a slap in the face to victims' families.

Newsom’s sweeping order to commute the condemned inmates to life in prison without the possibility of parole has drawn intense criticism alongside praise from anti-death penalty advocates.

"I think it's all about politics, sadly. Politics is over people in this case, and that's a real sad state of affairs," San Luis Obispo County District Attorney Dan Dow told Fox News Digital.

ALABAMA GOVERNOR COMMUTES DEATH SENTENCE AS DOUBTS EMERGE ABOUT EVIDENCE IN MURDER CONVICTION

In an open letter detailing his decision, Newsom said California's capital punishment system is fundamentally at odds with the state's principles.

"After nearly 30 years in public office, I have come to understand the limits of what government can justly accomplish," Newsom wrote. "I take this action because I firmly believe that state-sanctioned killing is incompatible with California’s values, undermines the foundations of our legal system, and diminishes each of us."

POPE LEO DENOUNCES DEATH PENALTY AS 'INADMISSIBLE' AHEAD OF PENTAGON'S PLANNED LIVESTREAMED EXECUTION

Upon taking office in 2019, Newsom issued an executive moratorium on capital punishment. California has not carried out an execution since 2006.

The backlash to the governor's announcement was immediate.

FLORIDA PUTS 77-YEAR-OLD MAN TO DEATH FOR DEPUTY'S MURDER AS STATE CLOSES IN ON EXECUTION RECORD

"Justice will not have been served for these victims, dozens of them in San Diego County," said Lt. Jared Wilson, president of the San Diego Police Officers Association. "Their last memories were of these evil, evil men who took their lives. What Gavin Newsom has done is awful."

Wilson and other law enforcement officials strongly criticized the blanket clemency, citing cases like that of Jesse Michael Gomez, who was sentenced to death for the 2016 murder of San Diego police officer Jonathan "J.D." De Guzman.

"Californians have been asked on two separate ballot initiatives to abolish the death penalty, and both times they have chosen to keep it for the most serious crimes," said Los Angeles County District Attorney Nathan Hochman. "Until the law is changed, my office will continue to evaluate every death penalty-eligible case with the rigor, care, and restraint these decisions demand."

NEW YORK BILLS COULD ABOLISH LIFE WITHOUT PAROLE FOR SERIAL KILLERS AND COP KILLERS, CRITICS WARN

Orange County District Attorney Todd Spitzer called the commutations "mercy for the wolves … while inflicting the ultimate act of cruelty on the sheep," saying voters in California have upheld the death penalty in recent years.

Riverside County Sheriff Chad Bianco, who previously ran for governor, noted that 127 inmates on California’s death row were sentenced for crimes committed in his county.

"These sentences were not handed down without due process," he said. "They followed extensive investigations, lengthy trials, evidence presented in court, and decisions made by juries and judges.

"Yet, with one sweeping executive decision, the governor has chosen to override those outcomes, disregarding the voices of victims’ families, the work of prosecutors, and the pursuit of justice that took years to achieve."

Among the 548 inmates whose sentences were commuted are two men convicted in San Luis Obispo County: Michael Whisenhunt, 61, who was sentenced to death for the 1995 torture and murder of his girlfriend's 1-year-old daughter, Kesha Gurke; and Rex Krebs, 60, who was convicted in the brutal slayings of two female college students.

CHARLES MANSON CULT FOLLOWER BRUCE DAVIS, CONVICTED IN TWO 1969 KILLINGS, DIES BEHIND BARS AT 83

Dow noted that families of the victims were neither consulted nor notified prior to Newsom's public announcement.

"I was just sickened, frankly, for the crime victims in California who were slapped in the face by our governor," Dow said.

Addressing arguments from anti-death penalty groups who contend that capital punishment is inherently flawed and racially biased, Dow defended the current legal framework.

World.title: Cornell faculty senate votes no confidence in administration’s handling of sexual assault
World.content:
Members of the Cornell University faculty senate on Friday issued a vote of no confidence in the administration’s ability to manage the response to an alleged sexual assault at a fraternity house in 2024, according to the university.

The governing body took up the issue after a former student, known as Jane Doe, alleged she was sexually assaulted and forced to take drugs at the Chi Phi fraternity house from Oct. 19 to 20, 2024. The allegations, detailed in a lawsuit the woman filed in September, led to widespread criticism of the university and calls for reform from students and alumni.

The senate’s resolution states that the body “has no confidence in the ability of the central administration to effectively address the ongoing crisis of sexual assault at Cornell University.”

It does not recommend removals or suggest how to manage the controversy’s fallout. It passed by a vote of 75-50, with five abstentions and five members not voting, according to a copy of the results obtained by NBC News.

The vote will not directly affect leadership decisions at the institution, including whether President Michael Kotlikoff remains in his role. The board of trustees, which has the authority to replace him, can consider the finding in its decisions but suggested in a statement Friday that no immediate changes were expected.

“The Board of Trustees remains confident that President Kotlikoff and his administration are the right leaders to thoughtfully and comprehensively address the serious problem of sexual assault on our campus,” chair Anne Meinig Smalling said.

Smalling highlighted recent changes implemented by leadership.

“They have already taken several important steps to this end, including adding staff to the Cornell Office of Civil Rights, expanding in-person sexual assault prevention education, and hiring more victim advocates,” Smalling said. “The administration will continue to build on that progress with more initiatives to be launched in the weeks and months ahead.”

A demonstration by Cornell students in support of Jane Doe in Ithaca in October. Spencer Platt / Getty

Faculty senators who sponsored the resolution called the decision “a reckoning” for the university.

“It is a call for real, systemic change; not a slow-moving taskforce, weakly enforced ban on fraternity parties, or expensive [public relations] damage control, but meaningful, evidence-based steps to reduce the incidence of sexual assault on campus and provide significant support to and justice for survivors,” the sponsors wrote in a statement.

Jane Doe and her attorney have alleged that Cornell failed to support her through the reporting process and subsequent investigation.

“We are hopeful that this will be yet another step forward to educate and support the Cornell community by addressing the longstanding scourge of sexual assault on campus,” said Jane Doe’s attorney Thomas Giuffra.

Jane Doe accused seven members of the fraternity of participating in a sexual assault, which she told police began with a consensual threesome but resulted in unwanted sex and ketamine consumption.

All seven men accused in the incident deny the allegations. Two were expelled from the university after an internal civil rights proceeding, and others faced less severe punishments from the school.

Tompkins County District Attorney Matthew Van Houten said he declined to pursue a criminal case in November 2024 based on a six-page statement from Jane Doe.

New York Attorney General Letitia James was appointed by Gov. Kathy Hochul last month to investigate the matter and consider whether criminal charges are supported. Two of the defendants initiated court proceedings aimed at disqualifying James based on what they argue are biased statements of support for Jane Doe that James posted on social media.

On Thursday, several defendants joined an Article 78 proceeding in Sullivan County that was recently filed by lawyers for one of the fraternity brothers, Gillio Lopes. Diego Sarabia, Scott Kretzschmar, Scott Norris and Winston Lee, who are co-defendants in Jane Doe’s lawsuit, were added to the petition in support of Lopes’ request.

Two remaining defendants, Matthew Ingalls and Jonathan Newell, do not have representation in the civil case and did not respond to Lopes’ attorneys.

On Wednesday, James announced her appointment of a former federal prosecutor to direct the investigation. That attorney, Jacqueline Kelly, will lead a team under James to conduct an independent inquiry into the sexual assault allegations.

Lopes’ lawyers argued in court papers that unless James recuses herself, the appointment does not change their position on the existence of a conflict. James has said her office is fully capable of conducting a fact-based, unbiased review.

James has also said her comments were merely an expression of empathy for Jane Doe.

Lee’s attorney previously filed a separate motion in Tompkins County Supreme Court seeking to block James from any grand jury proceeding, arguing that she had exhibited bias. A decision is expected Nov. 13.

A Cornell University police vehicle outside Chi Phi fraternity in Ithaca in October. Heather Ainsworth for NBC News

At a virtual news conference after the faculty senate vote Friday, the proposal’s lead sponsor, Paul Ortiz, said the idea came “after hearing from scores of current students, alumni, staff and faculty that the Jane Doe case was the tip of the iceberg.”

“The bravery of the survivors of sexual assault at Cornell past and present who told us their stories proved that no administration or administrator at this university could have been unaware of the chronic crisis of sexual assault at Cornell,” said Ortiz, a labor history professor. “Not in the 1970s, not in the 2010s; most certainly not now.”

Ortiz said he and other faculty members are planning an oral history project to highlight stories of sexual assault survivors at Cornell.

The Cornell president last month fielded questions from professors and other university employees at a senate meeting. At that Oct. 14 session, Kotlikoff vowed to reassess Greek life at the university and examine preventive measures to reduce the number of reported sexual assaults on campus.

The president said additional resources were being added to support victims when they come forward. That includes assistance dealing with Cornell’s bureaucracy for students who make sexual assault complaints, Kotlikoff said.

Kotlikoff told the faculty members that he didn’t know until recently that Jane Doe dropped out of school after the incident.

Faculty senate members recently debated whether to postpone the vote until after the university’s outside review by former acting Attorney General Sally Yates, who was commissioned by the board of trustees to examine how the matter was handled.

A proposal to postpone the no-confidence decision failed to pass at the Senate’s Oct. 28 meeting.

World.title: Investors try to regain their footing after tech stocks tank
World.content:
Tech stocks in the U.S. steadied Friday after suffering one of their worst routs in years, as investors weighed the prospect of an AI investment slowdown resulting from Democratic midterm victories against the sector’s long-term growth potential.

The tech-focused Nasdaq 100 closed up 1.1% after plunging 6.3% on Thursday, its worst single-day performance since the Covid-19 pandemic.

The broader S&P 500 finished 0.3% higher, after tanking 4.4% Thursday, a drop that wiped out $2.8 trillion worth of wealth on paper.

A strong October jobs report Friday morning increased the odds that the Federal Reserve will raise interest rates at its next policy meeting in December. The prospect of higher borrowing costs helped to push stocks down from their highs earlier in the day.

Investors continue to digest the results of Tuesday’s midterm elections, in which a crop of Democratic candidates were elected to office who had pledged to rein in AI and data centers. They include Gov.-elect Gina Hinojosa of Texas, a state that is among the largest data center markets in the country.

The AI boom is responsible for an ever-increasing share of U.S. stock market gains and economic growth, so any threat to the narrative of demand-fueled growth can rattle investors.

“Markets are being punished according to their dependence on the U.S. AI infrastructure cycle,” Charu Chanana, chief investment strategist at Singapore-based SAXO Markets, told NBC News.

The incoming Democratic-controlled Congress could also tighten scrutiny of the AI industry, including its infrastructure projects, which could cause delays and additional costs.

This would add to existing worries investors already have about the long-term profitability of these investments.

Gov.-elect Gina Hinojosa of Texas has called for a pause in new data center developments. Texas is one of the nation's biggest data center markets. Mikala Compton / The Austin American-Statesman via Getty

Some analysts viewed Thursday’s dramatic sell-off as overblown — merely a sign of some froth coming off an overstretched market — rather than the end of the line for the AI investment boom.

Recent declines are “just speed bumps,” said economist and investor Ed Yardeni.

Rather than spelling doom for the sector, Yardeni said losses like this week’s could ultimately help keep the AI bubble from overheating.

Until it becomes clearer how much data center construction is truly threatened by newly elected lawmakers, volatility is likely to continue.

“This is a stock market that is trying to figure out the right valuations for the AI trade, which is grappling with a swift sentiment shift after the midterm elections,” said Alex Guiliano, chief investment officer at New Jersey-based Resonate Wealth Partners.

World.title: We want to hear your experience with changes to student loan repayment plans
World.content:
President Donald Trump’s “big, beautiful bill” has transformed the sprawling federal student loan system — and student borrowers are feeling the effects of the most consequential changes.

This year, the approximately 7.5 million student borrowers under the Biden-era Saving on a Valuable Education, or SAVE, plan had to select a new one. So far, about 2 million borrowers have done so, after the Education Department warned that the SAVE plan was “illegal” and would be discontinued. The remaining borrowers who did not select a new plan were set to start receiving notices this month informing them that they missed a final deadline and were automatically moved to a new plan.

The Trump administration has said ending the SAVE plan would help streamline repayment programs while ensuring borrowers are paying off what they owe to the federal government. But student advocacy groups fear lower-income borrowers who had benefited from smaller monthly payments — or even qualified to make no payments at all based on their income — will end up with significantly higher bills under the other available plans.

We want to hear from you, whether you’re in this situation or are facing another challenge related to the recent student loan changes. Please share your experience by filling out the form below.

World.title: No one knew why a dad couldn't eat. Then a surgeon took a second look.
World.content:
Richard Satin was sure he was dying.

Things had been fine until the fall of 2025. He had enjoyed the summer with his wife and 8-year-old daughter, including taking a trip to Disney. But in October, he woke up in the middle of the night in agony.

When his wife, Farrah, rushed him to a Long Island hospital, tests showed his blood sugar was spiking. Doctors found he had developed diabetes. They also identified a blood clot in his portal vein, which connects the gastrointestinal tract to the liver. They treated the clot and stabilized his diabetes. He was discharged a week later with the new diagnosis.

But it was the start of a vicious cycle. Within days, Satin was in pain again and returned to the hospital. Doctors had few answers. During one visit, a doctor recommended a high-fiber diet. Another visit came with a recommendation for a liquid diet. Nothing helped.

Soon, Satin lost all appetite. Eating a bowl of Jell-O became an achievement. His daughter became frightened by his appearance. His favorite hobby, golf, was impossible. By mid-December, he had lost 70 pounds. His wife was at the end of her rope.

"Farrah just looked at me and said 'We can't go down this path anymore. We've got to do something,'" Satin recalled.

The couple began reaching out to specialists, but many weren't available for months. Satin, convinced he wouldn't make it that long, made an appointment with a concierge doctor, Dr. William Klein. On Christmas Eve, he had his first appointment with Klein.

"He examined me for a couple of hours, took lots of vials of blood, and said, 'If you don't have surgery immediately, you are in trouble,'" Satin said.

Richard and Becky Satin. Richard Satin

A life-saving surgery

Klein determined that Satin had an issue in his gastrointestinal tract, but was stumped on exactly what was wrong. He referred Satin to a surgeon, Dr. Gary Gecelter, chairman of the Department of Surgery at St. Francis Hospital & Heart Center. Gecelter reviewed Satin's case and repeated all the tests Klein had done.

Gecelter found that Satin had an "unusual inflammatory problem" in his digestive tract. That had led to an inflammatory reaction of the blood supply to the stomach, causing a clot in his liver and a bowel blockage. Previously, doctors had focused on the clotting problem. But Gecelter thought if he removed the part of the small bowel that was getting inflamed, it would help Satin recover.

In early January, Gecelter performed a complex but minimally invasive surgery to remove the inflamed part of the small bowel. Satin "woke up literally saying he felt better," Gecelter said.

"I thought that was more of a placebo effect than reality," Gecelter said. "But the next day, he was tolerating liquids. Within two days, he said he felt his (symptoms) were resolved."

Three days after the operation, Satin was discharged. Less than a week later, he was back to eating his favorite foods. Within three months, he had regained half the weight he lost.

Satin said he was shocked to feel so much better so quickly, especially because it had taken so long to receive a diagnosis.

"It was surreal," Satin said. "There were a lot of moments in October, November, December, that I couldn't always see the light at the end of the tunnel, so many days of not eating, missing Thanksgiving and holidays and birthdays. But I learned a lot in the process."

A "lovely" letter of gratitude

As Satin recovered, his daughter Becky watched with relief. For months, her dad hadn't been able to golf with her or attend her school events. She had worried he would never feel better. To express her gratitude, she wrote a short letter to Gecelter.

"It would have been really bad if he didn't live," Becky said. "I'm happy he did, and I'm so excited to do so many fun things with him. I wrote the letter to say thank-you to the doctors."

Becky Satin's letter to Dr. Gary Gecelter. Richard Satin

A photo shows Satin, Becky and Gecelter all standing together and smiling, with the 8-year-old holding up the note. Gecelter said he keeps the letter in his office.

"I get beautiful letters, especially around the holidays, but this was a stand-out," Gecelter said. "It was written by a child under 10, in her own language. It expressed a sincerity that only a child can convey. It was lovely."

"I don't take any of it for granted"

Six months after his operation, Satin celebrated with a massive party at the country club he and his family belong to. Friends and family were invited. Klein and Gecelter were named the guests of honor.

Satin remains in good health. He has regained much of the weight he lost, though his appetite is smaller than it used to be. He's back on the golf course and attending his daughter's school events. He has made some lifestyle changes to accommodate his diabetes diagnosis, such as watching his blood sugar and avoiding alcohol and fried foods, but his condition is stable.

Richard Satin, left, and Dr. Gary Gecelter, right, with Becky Satin in front. Richard Satin

Gecelter said he has not been able to understand why Satin became sick in the first place, so there's "no saying whether what caused that initial condition could" happen again. But if it does, now doctors will know where to look, Gecelter said.

Satin said he is eager to get back to traveling and to continue spending time with his family. In June, the trio went on a vacation that was initially scheduled for December and had been rescheduled because of his illness.

"I made a promise to my wife 20 years ago that I was going to give her 50 years, so she's holding me to another 30," Satin joked. "I don't take any of it for granted."

World.title: Paraguay's president under house arrested after bank collapse
World.content:
Paraguay's president has been placed on house arrest on Friday after the collapse of a government-linked bank that locked nearly half the country's population out of their accounts.

Paraguay's Senate voted to remove Santiago Peña for misconduct in office, making him the second president ousted by impeachment since the end of Gen. Alfredo Stroessner's 35-year dictatorship in 1989.

Regulators had seized Ueno Bank just three days earlier, sending shock waves through the financial system and setting off the country's worst political crisis in more than a decade.

Santiago Pena, Paraguay's president, during a Bloomberg Television interview in New York, US, on Friday, Sept. 25, 2026. Michael Nagle / Getty Images

Peña was ordered to remain at one of his homes in Asunción until he appears before prosecutors Saturday morning on charges of breach of trust, influence peddling and using public office for personal gain, the most serious of which carry up to 10 years in prison. Lawmakers accuse him of using his political influence to steer hundreds of millions of dollars in public funds into Ueno while regulators overlooked risky insider lending.

The Paraguayan president denied wrongdoing.

When regulators seized the bank, Ueno customers could no longer withdraw cash, access their savings or use their cards to buy anything. The digital lender had aggressively courted the poor and unbanked with generous supermarket rebates, and more than 1 million Paraguayans opened their first bank account there, according to Ueno. Even players on the national soccer team, which Ueno sponsored through its run to a World Cup upset of Germany this year, say they can't reach their money.

People queue outside a branch of the Banco Familiar hoping to be able to withdraw their savings or funds, a day after the intervention of the Ueno bank by Paraguay's Central Bank in Asuncion on November 4, 2026. DANIEL DUARTE /Getty Images

The fallout has spread well beyond savers. A ride-hailing app that relied on Ueno shut down, leaving 3,000 drivers without work. The state power company says $21 million in loans from the Inter-American Development Bank and Taiwan, earmarked for public works, is trapped at the bank. Paraguay's bonds have posted some of the worst losses in emerging markets this week, and the guaraní has slid against the dollar.

Some depositors began recovering their money Thursday, starting with those holding up to 10 million guaraníes (about $1,500). Deposits are insured up to about $35,000, which the central bank says covers 97% of Ueno's customers. It calls the collapse an isolated case and insists the broader financial system is safe.
