When you know how to read that list, you learn things the marketing copy will never tell you.

A casino does not manufacture its own games in most cases. It licenses them from independent studios, and those studios sit under their own testing and compliance obligations. That separation is useful to a cautious player, because a provider has a reputation to protect across hundreds of operators and cannot afford to be caught tampering with outcomes.

Why the provider list matters

The list of provider is one of the few things on a casino site that is hard to fake. Serious studios protect their brands and will not let an unlicensed operator display their logo without a distribution agreement. So when you see recognised names, it usually means the operator passed some form of vetting to get the content.

It also tells you about fairness. Established providers submit their titles to independent laboratories for random number generator testing. The return to player figure you see on a slot comes from the studio, not the casino, and it is checked by third parties, not invented by the marketing team.

What to look for in a provider list

A long list is not automatically a good one. What matters is the mix of names, the type of content they supply, and whether the studios are known for passing independent audits. A handful of categories cover most of what you will encounter.

Established studios

These are the companies whose slots and table games appear across many regulated markets. Their presence suggests the casino has gone through commercial and compliance steps to carry the content. They are also the easiest to research, since their certifications and corporate details are public.

Live dealer specialists

Live casino content comes from a smaller group of studios that run physical or virtual tables streamed in real time. Running these operations requires studio licences and infrastructure, so their inclusion is another signal that the operator works within a structured supply chain.

Provider list feature What it signals Multiple established studios Commercial and compliance vetting passed Named live dealer provider Structured, licensed supply chain Only unknown or unnamed brands Reason to investigate further Published RTP per title Transparency about odds

Most players only need a minute to run through these points. Together, they give a clear picture of the kind of content and studios a casino works with.

Certification and the names behind the games

Provider logos are a starting point, not a verdict. The next step is to confirm that the studios are tested by recognised laboratories and that the casino itself holds a licence that matches the content it advertises. Comparison portals that document licences and testing, such as the editorial work published at mejorescasinos-online.com, exist precisely because this information is scattered and easy to overlook. The useful checks are straightforward once you know what to look for.

- Confirm the studio names link to real, researchable companies.

- Check that the operator names a regulator you can look up, such as the Malta Gaming Authority or Curaçao.

- Look for references to independent testing bodies that audit random number generators.

- Match the advertised return-to-player figures against the studio, not the casino.

Each of these checks takes only a minute or two.

What a thin or hidden list signals

Sometimes the warning is in what is missing. A site that hides its provider list, or fills it with brands that return no results, deserves a closer look before you decide anything. The following patterns tend to repeat.

- No provider names shown anywhere, only generic game thumbnails.

- Logos that do not match the games actually loaded in the lobby.

- Studios with no corporate footprint or testing record you can find.

- Return-to-player values quoted without any source behind them.

- Live tables credited to an unfamiliar studio, rather than recognised names like Evolution, Pragmatic Play Live or Playtech Live.

When a provider list is open and easy to verify, it saves you time and lets you focus on choosing the games you enjoy.

Use the provider list as a quick check

Reading the provider list takes a few minutes and costs nothing. It will not predict any single session, because the house edge is built into the games and losses are a normal part of play, so treat gambling as entertainment with a budget you can afford. What the provider list does give you is a reasonable sense of whether an operator sits inside a tested, licensed supply chain or outside it. That context is worth more than a headline bonus, and it is one of the simplest habits a careful player can learn.

World.title: Why Tuesday’s US midterm results are a historic opportunity for Mexico-US relations: A perspective from our CEO
World.content:
Most of us intently watched Tuesday night’s midterm election results in the United States, regardless of political affiliation. As the MND team is committed to remaining apolitical, I will not weigh in on my personal thoughts on the results. I will, however, comment on what they mean for Mexico and for Mexico-U.S. relations.

It’s important to understand that the hardline approach of the Trump administration over the past two years against both Mexican immigrants and Mexico effectively silenced leaders on both sides of the border. Mexico was constantly on the defensive against the U.S. on tariffs, cartels, deportations, the rights of Mexican citizens abroad and many other topics. Mexican Americans, regardless of status, watched with anxiety as their communities came under threat from aggressive ICE raids. For many people and for Mexico in general, it was a time to keep your head down and stay quiet. The focus became on surviving the storm rather than thriving, leading or growing.

But the midterm election results have dramatically changed that dynamic.

First of all, I am happy for Mexican Americans. They will hopefully no longer have to fear the heavy-handed tactics often deployed by members of ICE. I recently wrote about the death of the 18th Mexican-American in ICE custody here: Yet another Mexican national dies in the custody of ICE: A perspective from our CEO.

People living in the United States — either legally or illegally — shouldn’t have to fear for their lives at the hands of the government. The data shows that the raids have often gone far beyond focusing on criminals, as the administration suggested it would do. Too many good people have been demonized by ICE as the agency has become increasingly extremist.

I am also happy for Mexico. The country has been the brunt of countless threats by the Trump administration on everything from tariffs to immigration to drug policy and cartels — despite historic cooperation from the Sheinbaum administration on many of these issues. Businesses on both sides of the border have had to deal with near-constant tariff threats, which oftentimes defy standard logic and strategic rationale for the North American region. Both Trump and members of his administration have repeatedly claimed that Mexico is run by the cartels, that President Sheinbaum is “afraid of the cartels,” and threatened to take unilateral action in the country. Hopefully, the unprecedented cooperation will continue and the unhelpful threats will diminish.

I am happy for the states of California and Texas, which both elected Mexican American governors. These two states — the largest and most economically prosperous in the United States — now account for more than half of the people of Mexican origin in the United States. Mexican Americans represent 40% of the total population in those states, which, if they were stand-alone counties, would be the fifth- and eighth-largest in the world in terms of GDP. Children of Mexican immigrants to the U.S. now lead both states. The newly elected lieutenant governor of Nevada is also of Mexican heritage.

Mexican Americans stood up, voted, and were heard — loudly and clearly. Their collective action presents a tremendous opportunity for Mexico. Let me give two examples:

1. I recently wrote about the huge, untapped opportunity that the Mexican diaspora in the U.S. represents for Mexico. The engagement of Indian American businesspeople with India stands in stark contrast to the lack of engagement of many Mexican American businesspeople with Mexico. Post-election, the timing is perfect for this to change. The opportunity for Mexican American businesses to further connect with Mexico to find talent, suppliers or customers is massive and could unleash economic growth in both countries.

2. It’s time for Mexico and the U.S. to think BIG on binational projects and initiatives. If not at the national level, most certainly at the state level. Some great examples already exist or are in process. In California, think of the Tijuana airport, which actually straddles the border into California. The airport has experienced phenomenal growth and is a perfect example of how the two countries can work strategically to develop closer ties. In Texas, think of the newly-opened second railway between Laredo and Nuevo Laredo or the proposed expansion of the World Trade Bridge from eight to 18 lanes. Think of the soon-to-be-opened Pharr project adding a four-lane bridge in Reynosa, or the Colombia-Solidarity highway projects to better connect Nuevo León and Laredo. Or even consider the Green Corridors planned project for an autonomous system to transport cargo from Monterrey to Laredo.

It’s a historic time for real leadership — strategic, long-term, big thinking that can foster engagement and economic prosperity between the two countries. Far too much time has been lost dividing, threatening and silencing bilateral collaboration and cooperation. The current circumstances offer an opportunity to take the relationship to a whole new level. Leaders on both sides of the border, stand up! The time is now.

Travis Bembenek is the CEO of Mexico News Daily and has been living, working or playing in Mexico for nearly 30 years.

World.title: Mexico City’s Quintonil named best restaurant in Latin America
World.content:
Quintonil, a contemporary Mexican restaurant in Mexico City, was recognized as the best restaurant in Latin America and the fourth best globally in the 2026 edition of The World’s 50 Best Restaurants, presented Wednesday at the Municipal Theatre of Lima, Perú.

Led by married couple Chef Jorge Vallejo and restaurateur Alejandra Flores, Quintonil was the only Mexican representative among the top 50 in the ranking.

View this post on Instagram A post shared by The 50 Best Restaurants (@theworlds50best)

“With a reputation for weaving fresh, local ingredients and traditional Mexican flavours and techniques into modern preparations, [Quintonil] has cemented its place as a Mexico City classic,” 50 Best said.

Asador Etxebarri, a Basque restaurant in Atxondo, Spain, was ranked best in the world.

Despite securing a place in the top five, Quintonil dropped one spot in the rankings, falling from third to fourth place this year.

Founded in 2012 by Vallejo and Flores, Quintonil has built its concept around Mexican fresh local produce and a contemporary interpretation of traditional flavors and techniques. Many of its ingredients are sourced from an urban garden just 30 meters away from the restaurant.

Located in the high-end neighborhood of Polanco, the restaurant is named after an edible wild plant belonging to the amaranth family, widely used in traditional Mexican cuisine and featured in some of the dishes and drinks served there.

The power duo brings complementary expertise to Quintonil: While Vallejo leads the kitchen, Flores oversees the service experience in the dining room.

“Quintonil is the setting for chef Jorge Vallejo’s boundary-pushing Mexican cuisine and his wife Alejandra Flores’ exceptional hospitality,” 50 Best said.

50 Best highlighted dishes including roasted duck with coconut manchamanteles mole (a fruit and chile sauce) and a beetroot reduction, wild mushroom chileatole soup with cacahuazintle (a traditional corn variety) and beans, and ice cream made with honey from stingless melipona bees, served with papaya and lavender marmalade.

The tasting menu costs around 4,900 pesos (US $233) featuring four pairing options that include wines from around the world, Mexican wines, a selection of terroir-driven wines and rare finds, and a non-alcoholic option.

It also features a cocktail menu incorporating Mexican ingredients.

The recognition from 50 Best adds to Quintonil’s list of accolades, which includes two Michelin stars, a distinction it shares with only one other restaurant in Mexico: Pujol, also located in Mexico City.

With reports from El País

World.title: Mexico City ponders 9-year prison terms for poisoners of animals in publc spaces
World.content:
Mexico City lawmakers are seeking tougher penalties for poisoning animals — including up to nine years in prison under one proposal — after four dogs were recently killed by toxic meat allegedly placed as bait in the Condesa neighborhood.

Labor Party lawmaker Diana Barragán introduced the measure Thursday, seeking to explicitly recognize poisoning as a serious form of animal abuse under the capital’s penal code.

The push follows criminal proceedings against Salvador “N,” who is accused of leaving poisoned pieces of sausage and other meat in and around the capital’s Parque España.

The 58-year-old was arrested near the park around 6:20 a.m. Oct. 30 and formally charged the following day. A judge ordered him held pending trial on animal abuse and cruelty charges.

Barragán’s proposal would allow sentences of up to five years when poisoning injures an animal and three to nine years when it causes death, according to the text posted on the Mexico City Congress website.

The measure would explicitly add poisoning as an aggravating circumstance, increasing existing penalties rather than creating a separate offense. It would cover toxic substances, contaminated food and other chemical or biological agents.

Barragán argued that existing provisions leave legal gaps by not explicitly addressing poisoning. She also warned that toxic bait in parks, gardens and sidewalks endangers children, families and other passersby.

Two other initiatives introduced Wednesday would strengthen penalties and restrict convicted abusers’ access to animals.

Citizens’ Movement (MC) lawmaker Luisa Fernanda Ledesma Alpízar proposed increasing prison terms and fines by up to two-thirds for placing multiple poisoned baits or committing repeated attacks.

In addition, judges could temporarily bar convicted offenders from acquiring, adopting or caring for animals after release. Restrictions would be recorded in an animal abuser registry that shelters and other organizations could consult.

Separately, Institutional Revolutionary Party (PRI) lawmaker Tania Nanette Larios Pérez proposed four to eight years in prison for killing animals or endangering their lives or health through poison, harmful chemicals, concealed sharp objects or adulterated bait.

The local proposals — which now await committee review — follow a separate animal welfare initiative, known as the “Pay de Limón” bill, that activists presented to the Mexican Senate last year.

As for Salvador’s case, the judge gave investigators two months to complete their investigation. He remains at Mexico City’s North Prison and has not been convicted.

Prosecutors allege he left contaminated food in Parque España and nearby streets from Oct. 26 through 28. Pills containing methomyl, a highly toxic insecticide, were allegedly concealed inside meat and sausages.

Police initially detained Salvador for resisting arrest. They had stopped him because he resembled someone shown in images circulated on social media, prosecutors said.

Prosecutors had received seven complaints from owners of affected animals. Four dogs died, while three others remained under treatment, the newspaper El Heraldo de México reported Thursday, citing senior prosecutor Jorge Emilio Iruegas Álvarez.

Authorities previously recovered 14 pieces of suspected poisoned meat in Parque España and surrounding streets.

Prosecutors were also examining whether the bait endangered park visitors, including children, and could warrant additional charges, Iruegas said.

Investigators were still examining Salvador’s reported claim that he had acted in retaliation for an alleged dog attack on his son.

With reports from El Sol de México, El Heraldo de México, El Informador and Excélsior

World.title: Meta launches its Muse AI agent in Mexico, a first for the Latin American market
World.content:
Muse, Meta’s artificial intelligence (AI) agent, has arrived in Mexico, the first country in Latin America to receive it.

In a LinkedIn post, Meta México Country Manager Marco Casarin explained what its AI agent can provide users:

“It doesn’t just answer questions: you tell it what you want to achieve, it figures out how to do it, creates the plan, and moves forward on its own. It takes tasks off your plate, accompanies you, organizes you, and keeps you focused.”

🚨 MUSE LAUNCH ALERT 🚨 muse just touched down in mexico 🇲🇽

órale, ya llegó 🌮 https://t.co/Z1dZMx8yvj — Alexandr Wang (@alexandr_wang) November 5, 2026

And just what is an AI agent?

According to SAS, a global software company, AI agents are “systems powered by AI that perform complex tasks or make informed decisions with varying human involvement.”

AI agents “surpass traditional chatbots and large language models by integrating data and advanced analytics tools to be more adaptable and capable of complex reasoning across industries.”

Casarin said that Muse can connect to your email, calendar, messages and Instagram, describing its ability to connect to other apps and services, always under the user’s control, as one of its standout features.

The first Muse connectors in Mexico will be in the retail, credit and lending categories, as well as in the travel, car rental, entertainment and food delivery industries. Some of the brands mentioned by Casarin are: Cinépolis, Coppel, Despegar, Kavak, Liverpool and Rappi.

Users will be able to access the products and services of these brands, “allowing you to buy movie tickets, find your next car, plan your holiday trip, and find the best deals for everyday purchases,” Casarin wrote. “No more jumping from app to app, no more opening 10 tabs. Decide your goal, ask Muse for it, and enjoy.”

Equally important, according to Casarin, is that the user is always in control. “You decide what it can access,” he said. “You authorize every action before it happens, and you see everything it does and everything it plans to do.”

In Mexico, Muse is already available in Spanish for users over 18 years old through iOS, Android, and muse.ai. it will soon be compatible with AI glasses, and you’ll even be able to interact with Muse via WhatsApp.

Fair warning: The convenience of an AI agent comes with the price of sharing more details about your life and, once AI agents obtain users’ information, there’s no taking back the data shared.

And as Fast Company magazine points out, Meta’s controversial history with user data makes its promises about privacy a hard sell.

With reports from El Universal, Milenio and Infobae

World.title: Detained Mexican judge faces extradition to US over $2 million bribe to free alleged Canadian drug trafficker
World.content:
District Judge Luis Benítez Alcántara, arrested in Colombia on Nov. 1 on charges of accepting a US $2 million bribe from drug traffickers, could face up to 15 years in prison for each of the nine charges the United States seeks to bring against him.

Luis Benítez Alcántara, 49, is accused of taking the bribe to release a suspected drug trafficker who was facing charges in an investigation into a billion-dollar drug trafficking ring, U.S. officials said Thursday.

Benítez is the first Mexican federal judge indicted by the United States, which has already requested his extradition from Colombia to face charges in the U.S.

“Crooked public officials, no matter where they are, who assist drug traffickers operating here at home will face justice in the United States,” U.S. Attorney General Todd Blanche said in a statement.

The bribery case in question involved Andrew Clark, 36, a Canadian drug trafficker and second-in-command to Ryan James Wedding, 44, a former Olympic snowboarder for Canada who led one of the biggest, most notorious and violent transnational criminal organizations.

Clark was arrested in Mexico in October 2024 on U.S. drug trafficking, murder and attempted murder charges in which Wedding was also named. U.S. officials formally requested his extradition in November 2024.

Benítez was presiding over the extradition proceedings when — after accepting the US $2 million bribe payment — he issued rulings that directly facilitated Clark’s release from custody in February 2025, according to U.S. officials.

Clark was re-arrested days later and subsequently extradited to the U.S. where he faces nine charges of distributing and possessing cocaine, methamphetamine, engaging in a continuing criminal enterprise, homicide related to a criminal enterprise, attempted homicide related to a criminal enterprise, and drug trafficking offenses.

Since Benítez accepted money in exchange for releasing Clark, he is considered an accomplice.

As a result, the judge faces a nine-count U.S. grand jury indictment charging him with being an accessory after the fact. The U.S. Department of Justice also accuses him of being an accomplice in drug trafficking and homicide.

If convicted, Benítez would face a maximum penalty of 15 years in prison on each count.

“Mr. Benítez will be held accountable,” Blanche said. “The Department of Justice will continue to identify and dismantle transnational criminal organizations that threaten the security of the American people.”

The judge had a career spanning more than two decades within Mexico’s Federal Judiciary, but his record of decisions is tainted. For example, he released the only defendant in the Pegasus spying case against journalists.

The arrest of Benítez is the latest chapter in the U.S. investigation into the multinational drug trafficking network allegedly run by Wedding, who was apprehended in Mexico earlier this year. He was then flown to California, where he pleaded not guilty to murder and drug charges.

In a related incident, Édgar Aarón Vázquez, the leader of the New Empire Cartel and accused by the U.S. of protecting Wedding in Mexico, was killed on Thursday during a confrontation with police in the State of Mexico.

Vázquez is also believed to have been the intellectual author of the July 2024 murder of Milton Morales, a top Mexico City security official.

With reports by The Associated Press, Reuters, Proceso and Reforma

World.title: El Jalapeño: California high-speed rail project reaches -25% completion as Mexico line hits 25%
World.content:
All stories in El Jalapeño are satire and not real news. Check out the original article here.

MEXICO CITY — Construction on the 102-kilometer Querétaro-Irapuato passenger rail line reached 25% completion this week, just 12 months after breaking ground, creating a stark contrast with California’s Los Angeles-to-San Francisco high-speed rail network, which transit analysts confirmed is currently sitting at -25% complete.

According to data released by Mexico’s Agency for Trains and Integrated Public Transportation (ATTRAPI), crews in the industrial Bajío region have laid physical track, initiated 10 viaducts and begun assembly on railcars in Hidalgo. Meanwhile, across the northern border, project metrics indicate California has managed to regress 25% below its starting line after spending 16 years, US $11 billion and thousands of billable hours untangling lawsuits over land rights that no longer exist.

“When Mexican crews complete 25% of a project, it means a quarter of the actual track is ready for trains,” said Arthur Pendelton, a senior fellow at the Institute for Infrastructure Comparison in Sacramento. “When California logs -25%, it means we have spent enough time in environmental mediation to un-build the preliminary ideas we drafted during the George W. Bush administration.”

The Mexican route forms part of a federal initiative to build 2,500 kilometers of operational track by 2030. Transportation planners in Washington have struggled to interpret the data, noting that under standard U.S. transit models, laying 25% of a line in one year without first commissioning a seven-year feasibility study on environmental noise disruption violates accepted notions of government practice.

“In our system, progress is measured in metric tons of paperwork generated per mile,” Pendelton added, gesturing to a chart showing California’s progress line sloping downward into negative territory. “If you actually pour concrete and build a bridge, you lose the ability to commission a follow-up impact study on the visual aesthetics of the concrete. From a regulatory perspective, Mexico is moving backward by moving forward.”

At press time, California high-speed rail officials announced plans to spend US $2.4 billion to hire an external consulting firm to investigate how Mexico achieved positive momentum on its construction timeline.

World.title: Sheinbaum calls for INE ‘cleanup’ after corruption scandal: Friday’s mañanera recapped
World.content:
Listen to this article

Sheinbaum’s mañanera in 60 seconds

🏛️ Sheinbaum says INE corruption goes beyond Guadalupe Taddei: The president asserted that corruption in the awarding of electoral materials contracts occurred “during the entire period of Lorenzo Córdova,” Taddei’s predecessor as INE president, and “probably before as well.” Taddei resigned as National Electoral Institute president last week amid allegations of corruption.

She said the institute must guarantee clean elections, transparency and republican austerity. 🕊️ Sheinbaum condemns murder of Cuernavaca city councilman: She called the killing of Morena councilman Gabriel Rivas Ríos, an environmental activist, “sad and infuriating,” saying there was “no doubt” it was ordered and carried out specifically against him. Rivas had criticized the Alto Verde residential project proposed for Cuernavaca, and Sheinbaum said she asked the Security Cabinet to support the Morelos Attorney General’s Office’s murder investigation. She said Rivas hadn’t requested federal protection.

She called the killing of Morena councilman Gabriel Rivas Ríos, an environmental activist, “sad and infuriating,” saying there was “no doubt” it was ordered and carried out specifically against him. Rivas had criticized the Alto Verde residential project proposed for Cuernavaca, and Sheinbaum said she asked the Security Cabinet to support the Morelos Attorney General’s Office’s murder investigation. She said Rivas hadn’t requested federal protection. 🇪🇸 Sheinbaum explains absence from Ibero-American Summit: She said she skipped the Madrid gathering because she will travel to China for the APEC leaders’ summit later this month. Sheinbaum noted that Foreign Affairs Minister Roberto Velasco represented her in the Spanish capital. She will seek a call with Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez to discuss the summit’s outcomes.

Why today’s mañanera matters

Alleged corruption in the awarding of National Electoral Institute (INE) contracts to a small group of electoral materials suppliers was a central focus of President Sheinbaum’s Friday morning press conference.

Guadalupe Taddei resigned as president of the INE last week after it came to light that lucrative contracts were awarded to electoral materials companies linked to a businessman with whom she had a close personal relationship. Taddei and that businessman, José Alfredo Hernández Casillas, are reportedly among 25 people who have been added to the Finance Ministry’s Blocked Persons List and who will be investigated by the Federal Attorney General’s Office.

On Friday morning, Sheinbaum asserted that corruption in the INE also occurred when Lorenzo Córdova was president of the institute between 2014 and 2023.

Also of note at today’s mañanera were the president’s remarks about the murder of a Cuernavaca city councilman. Gabriel Rivas Ríos, a Morena party member, was killed on Wednesday in Cuernavaca, capital of the state of Morelos.

Sheinbaum: ‘The INE needs to be cleaned up’

Sheinbaum asserted that corruption in INE’s rewarding of electoral materials contracts predates the 2023-2026 tenure of Taddei as the institute’s president.

Corruption occurred “during the entire period of Lorenzo Córdova,” she said.

“And probably before as well,” Sheinbaum added. “The audit will have to determine that.”

Sheinbaum noted that Córdova and other INE officials participated in various protests against an electoral reform proposal during the presidency of Andrés Manuel López Obrador. She recalled that the slogan of the protests was “El INE no se toca,’ or “Don’t touch the INE.”

“The INE has to be cleaned up. Maybe they said ‘don’t touch the INE’ in order to hang on to this whole electoral mafia that was built with them,” she said.

“The National Electoral Institute is an institute that must guarantee the will of the people, that must guarantee clean elections,” Sheinbaum added.

“In its operation, it must guarantee … transparency and republican austerity,” she said.

Sheinbaum laments murder of Cuernavaca councilman

Asked about the murder of Rivas, Sheinbaum said she knew him and described him as an environmental activist.

She described his murder as “sad and infuriating” and conveyed her condolences to his family and colleagues.

Sheinbaum said that when she heard about the homicide, she requested that the federal Security Cabinet “dedicate time and effort” to supporting the Morelos Attorney General’s Office in its investigation into the crime.

“It was a direct homicide. Some people on a motorbike shot him directly,” she said.

“There is no doubt it was a homicide that was ordered and carried out specifically against him,” Sheinbaum said.

She noted that Rivas had recently been critical of a real estate development in Cuernavaca that could cause “environmental problems.” She was referring to the Alto Verde residential project, whose construction was proposed on a site called La Cazahuatera.

The land where La Cazahuatera is located is “considered one of the last remnants of lowland deciduous forest within the urban area” of Cuernavaca, the news outlet Infobae reported.

In addition to contributing to efforts to solve Rivas’ murder, Sheinbaum said her administration would also work with Morelos Governor Margarita González Saravia “to see what can be done with this [real estate] development that he was fighting against.”

After a reporter noted that many environmental activists have been murdered or attacked in Mexico, Sheinbaum said that a lot of them now have government protection.

“They’ve approached us [to ask for protection],” she said, adding that government protection helps to “avoid” attacks on activists.

Sheinbaum said that Rivas hadn’t requested protection from the federal government.

“That doesn’t mean that we don’t condemn the homicide,” she added.

Sheinbaum explains her absence at Ibero-American Summit in Spain

Sheinbaum told reporters that she decided not to go to this week’s Ibero-American Summit in Madrid as she will travel to China for the Asia Pacific Economic Cooperation leaders’ summit later this month. She said visiting Spain as well as China would mean spending more time outside Mexico than she would like.

Sheinbaum said she advised Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez and King Felipe VI of her decision not to travel to Madrid.

“I wrote a letter to them … because they were the ones that invited me,” she said.

Sheinbaum noted that Foreign Affairs Minister Roberto Velasco represented her at the Ibero-American Summit, a gathering of leaders and officials from Spanish- and Portuguese-speaking countries.

She said she would seek a call with Sánchez to discuss the outcomes of the summit.

Mexico’s Foreign Ministry said in a statement that “the summit’s four agreements match Mexico’s priorities: care systems, academic mobility, disaster protection, and artificial intelligence that serves people.”

By Mexico News Daily chief staff writer Peter Davies (peter.davies@mexiconewsdaily.com)

World.title: Bucking expectations, Banxico lowers the interest rate, despite some inflation concerns
World.content:
Mexico’s central bank (Banxico) lowered its benchmark interest rate 25 basis points to 6.25%, surprising analysts, who as recently as this week expected the rate to remain unchanged.

In a split vote, the three bank governors supporting the reduction argued that there are no perceived demand pressures in the economy and that the degree of monetary restriction implemented is still in effect.

In a statement, Banxico adjudged that the disinflationary process has continued, indicating that, “given the prevailing slack conditions, the pass-through of exchange rate movements to prices would be limited.”

In what is viewed as guidance for future actions, the statement added that “going forward, the Governing Board believes that maintaining the rate for an extended period at the level achieved will support the convergence of inflation to its target and will be appropriate to meet external macroeconomic challenges.”

At the same time that Banxico reduced the interest rate, it raised its headline inflation forecast for the fourth quarter from 3.5% to 3.7%, acknowledging that risks remain tilted to the upside.

“This is mainly due to higher-than-anticipated levels for non-core inflation,” the statement said.

The bank also incorporated an upward adjustment to its estimate of core inflation for the last quarter, from 3.6% predicted in September to the 3.7% they now anticipate.

Although the economy continued to expand in the third-quarter, Banxico believes that “slack conditions are still expected throughout the forecast horizon, and downside risks to economic activity persist.”

Still, Banxico maintains that inflation will reach its target — 3% with a tolerance range of plus or minus 1 percentage point (2% to 4%) — by the fourth quarter of next year.

Banxico’s economic research identified four upside risks to its inflation forecasts: the persistence of core inflation; further depreciation of the peso; disruptions from trade policies or an inflationary impact from geopolitical conflicts; and, climate-related effects and unspecified cost pressures.

Looking ahead, the Governing Board said that maintaining the rate at its current level for an extended period “will support the convergence of inflation to its target and will be appropriate to address external macroeconomic challenges.”

Thursday’s surprise decision — 30 of the 36 institutions consulted by Citi expected the rate to remain unchanged — impacted the currency exchange market immediately.

The reduction pushed the dollar as high as 18.96 pesos during the day, although it later moderated its advance and closed at 18.7499. The peso lost 18.3 centavos, or 0.99%, compared to Wednesday’s close.

With reports from El Economista and El Financiero

World.title: Ueno Bank vs Nubank Differ Beyond the App
World.content:
Asunción, Paraguay’s capital and home of Ueno Bank, seen across the Paraguay River from Chaco’i, a town on the opposite bank, in 2016. Photo: P. S. F. Freitas, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

On Saturday 7 November 2026, Paraguay’s failed Ueno Bank and Brazil’s Nubank, a digital bank listed in New York, look alike on one point only: both won millions of customers fast through a phone app. They differ sharply in size, funding, regulation, ownership links and the safety net for savers.

What Paraguay’s central bank put Ueno, its fifth largest private bank, into a controlled shutdown in early November.

Paraguay’s central bank put Ueno, its fifth largest private bank, into a controlled shutdown in early November. Size Ueno held about US$2.2 billion in deposits at end 2025; Nubank holds US$45.3 billion, roughly 20 times.

Ueno held about US$2.2 billion in deposits at end 2025; Nubank holds US$45.3 billion, roughly 20 times. Reach Ueno’s 2.94 million clients equal about 46% of Paraguay’s people; Nubank’s Brazilian base is about 55%.

Ueno’s 2.94 million clients equal about 46% of Paraguay’s people; Nubank’s Brazilian base is about 55%. Safety net Paraguay’s deposit guarantee fund covers up to 228.3 million guaraníes, Gs (about US$38,200); Brazil’s deposit fund FGC covers R$250,000 (about US$45,000).

Paraguay’s deposit guarantee fund covers up to 228.3 million guaraníes, Gs (about US$38,200); Brazil’s deposit fund FGC covers R$250,000 (about US$45,000). Why Bank supervisors found signs of loans to companies tied to Ueno’s owner, the Paraguayan Grupo Vazquez, in June 2026.

In Plain English

Central bank: the state institution that licenses and supervises banks.

the state institution that licenses and supervises banks. Deposit guarantee fund: an industry fund that repays savers up to a legal limit if a bank fails.

an industry fund that repays savers up to a legal limit if a bank fails. Related party loan: a loan from a bank to companies or people linked to its owners.

a loan from a bank to companies or people linked to its owners. Solvency ratio: a bank’s capital as a share of its risky assets; a low ratio means a thin cushion.

a bank’s capital as a share of its risky assets; a low ratio means a thin cushion. Digital bank: a bank whose customers mainly use a phone app.

Where the Comparison Holds

Both banks built their business on the phone screen rather than on branches. Our Ueno Bank depositors guide explains the shutdown for ordinary account holders.

Ueno reported about 2.94 million clients at June 2026, before the Banco Central del Paraguay (BCP), the country’s central bank, took control. Those are clients, not unique people, because accounts and companies are included.

Start for US$1 Paraguay ranks 10th of 14 with 35.0 points. Strongest pillar: state capacity & security (55); weakest: future resources (13). Alignment group: Closer to Washington. See the full index, the business lens and the data →

Paraguay’s statistics office, INE, projects 6.46 million people for 2026. Ueno’s clients therefore equal about 46% of the population.

Nubank is run from São Paulo by Nu Holdings Ltd. (Nu), a Cayman Islands company listed on the New York Stock Exchange. It reported almost 118 million customers in Brazil, about 55% of the 213.4 million people that IBGE, Brazil’s statistics institute, estimated for 1 July 2025.

That similar share of the home population is the one striking parallel. In both cases a phone app reached a very large slice of the nation.

This also signs you up to our weekday newsletter, The LatAm Brief. Nothing arrives until you click the confirmation link, and you can stop either with one click. Privacy policy

Where Scale and Reach Differ

At December 2025 Ueno was the fifth largest private bank in Paraguay, with 5.9% of loans and 8.9% of deposits. Those figures come from a March 2026 report by FIX SCR, a credit rating agency, using BCP data.

Audited accounts at 31 December 2025 show total assets of Gs 21.096 trillion (US$3.21 billion) and customer deposits of Gs 14.65 trillion (about US$2.23 billion). We convert at Gs 6,575.71 per US$, the BCP rate the rating agency used, and elsewhere at Gs 5,976 per US$ (6 November 2026 close).

Ueno’s loans equalled 77% of its customer deposits, and 47.5% of deposits were term deposits, known as CDAs. It issued a US$350 million international bond in 2026 and announced a US$100 million capital plan in the last week of October.

Nubank’s Brazilian deposits stood at US$36.4 billion in June 2026, roughly 16 times Ueno’s. Its global deposits of US$45.3 billion, up 18% from a year earlier, are about 20 times larger.

Nubank has 139 million customers across Brazil, Mexico and Colombia. It earned US$1.06 billion in the second quarter of 2026, its first quarter above US$1 billion, with a return on equity of 33%.

In Brazil alone, Nubank’s customers outnumber Ueno’s clients about 40 times. The dates differ, with Ueno’s balance sheet at December 2025 and Nubank’s at June 2026, so the ratios are approximate.

Nubank’s credit portfolio of US$39.4 billion sits against deposits of US$45.3 billion. Its group wide cost of deposits was 88% of interbank rates, the rates banks charge each other.

The safety nets differ too. Paraguay’s guarantee fund covers up to 75 monthly minimum wages per depositor per bank, which is Gs 228.3 million (about US$38,200).

The first payout stage covers depositors with balances up to Gs 10 million (about US$1,673). Later stages for larger balances have no published dates.

Brazil’s deposit guarantee fund, FGC, covers up to R$250,000 (about US$45,000 at 5.505 reais per US$, 6 November 2026 close) per depositor per institution group. Under FGC rules as published, the overall cap is R$1 million (about US$182,000) per depositor every four years.

Live Company Intelligence Nu Holdings Ltd — the full investor dossier Company overview and the latest Rio Times coverage.

Why Ownership Links Matter More Than Size

Ueno Bank S.A.E.C.A. is a private bank controlled by Grupo Vazquez, a Paraguayan business group. U Paraguay S.A., a company inside the group, holds 91.21% of its capital. Ueno is unrelated to Brazil’s Banco Original, a separate Brazilian bank.

The BCP board decided unanimously, on 2 or 3 November 2026 depending on the report, to start a resolution, meaning a controlled shutdown, after Ueno’s solvency ratio fell below half the legal minimum. The legal basis is Law 2,334/03 on deposit guarantees and the resolution of financial entities.

The Superintendencia de Bancos is BCP’s bank supervisor. BCP president Carlos Carvallo said the decision followed months of technical work that began in June 2026.

That month the supervisor found signs of loans to companies linked to the group that controls the bank. Audited note 16 lists credit and contingent exposure to related persons and companies of Gs 351.6 billion (about US$53.5 million) at 31 December 2025.

A year earlier the same note showed Gs 334.9 billion (about US$50.9 million at the same rate). Prosecutors cite a larger figure that we cannot confirm.

The irony is sharp, because a rating published in 2026 on Ueno’s own website still described the bank as reasonably capitalised, months before the failure. It put effective capital at 15.8% of risk weighted assets (assets counted by how risky they are) at December 2025, with equity at 10.0% of assets.

That is a fact of the published report, not an allegation. It shows how little a headline capital ratio says about links between a bank and its owners.

Carvallo had led Financiera Ueno, the lender that became Ueno Bank, before he headed BCP. As we reported, Banco Central del Paraguay chief Carlos Carvallo resigned on 3 or 4 November, and he surrendered to police after prosecutors ordered his arrest, on the night of Friday 6 November.

On Friday 6 November the Senate removed President Santiago Peña. Vice President Pedro Alliana was sworn in the same evening.

The Strongest Counter-Argument

Nubank is also young, fast growing and heavy on credit cards, which make up US$26 billion of its US$39.4 billion credit portfolio. Its delinquency rate, the share of loans overdue, was 4.8% for 15 to 90 days and 6.9% for over 90 days.

A sceptic can therefore argue that the lesson is about governance, not the app format. That is fair, and it is why ownership links, supervision and the safety net matter more than the screen the customer sees.

Nubank’s Brazilian structure is also still changing. In its results release of 13 August 2026, Nu said: “in Brazil, we are evolving our structure, adding a full banking license to our operations”.

Nu has also been reported to be buying Banco Porto Real, a small licensed lender, to obtain that licence. The deal needs approval from the Banco Central do Brasil, Brazil’s central bank.

What It Means for You

An investor holding Nubank shares faces a different risk from Ueno’s: credit quality and the pending licence, not ownership links. Our Nubank explained guide describes its products.

For exposure to Paraguay, read our analysis of Paraguay bond risk and the IMF. Ueno’s US$350 million international bond has an unknown fate.

Travellers and expats in Paraguay with Ueno cards should know that the app, cards and ATMs were suspended when we published. Whether and when they reopen is not known, so check the payout rules in our depositors guide.

Nubank customers in Brazil should ask which Nu company holds their money and whether it is covered by FGC. Anyone with more than the covered amount at one institution group holds the excess without that protection.

What Is Not Known

The size of the hole in Ueno’s balance sheet is unknown, and so is the exact solvency ratio, because reports differ. We use no figure.

The exact date of the intervention is contested, either 2 or 3 November. Prosecutors cite a larger total of loans to linked companies than the audited note, and the audited accounts also list a separate, larger related-party item that we cannot match to either figure.

We do not know whether the Banco Central do Brasil has approved Nubank’s full Brazilian bank licence or the Banco Porto Real deal. We also do not know the fate of Ueno’s 2.9 million accounts or of its US$350 million bond.

Payout dates for balances above the first stage have not been published. We use only the 75 monthly minimum wage guarantee.

Sources: Nu Holdings Q2 2026 results release (13 August 2026); Ueno Bank audited financial statements 31 December 2025 and Q1 2026 report; FIX SCR rating report on Ueno Bank (31 March 2026); Banco Central del Paraguay resolution communiqués (as reproduced); FGC published coverage rules; IBGE population estimate 2025; INE Paraguay projection 2026. Read 7 November 2026. BCP and FGC websites blocked automated access, so their figures come from reproductions of their communiqués.

Part of the dossier: Paraguay Crisis, Peña Removal and Ueno Bank. Related: Pedro Alliana, Paraguay’s new president and the first Ueno payouts.

Frequently Asked Questions

Is Ueno Bank the same as Brazil’s Banco Original?

No. Ueno Bank S.A.E.C.A. is a Paraguayan private bank controlled by Grupo Vazquez, and it is not Brazil’s Banco Original.

How much of a deposit does Paraguay’s guarantee cover?

The guarantee fund covers up to 75 monthly minimum wages per depositor per bank, Gs 228.3 million (about US$38,200 at Gs 5,976 per US$).

Is Nubank a bank in Brazil?

Nu said on 13 August 2026 that it is adding a full banking licence in Brazil. We do not know whether the Banco Central do Brasil has approved it.

World.title: Paraguay Bank Crisis Dates to Watch Next
World.content:
PARAGUAY · UENO BANK CASE

Key Facts Why now Paraguay’s Ueno Bank crisis has moved from banking to courts and politics in five days.

Savers Advances start at Gs 10 million (US$1,673); the full guarantee is Gs 228.3 million (US$38,200).

Courts Ueno’s Miguel Vázquez was ordered held pending trial; prosecutors’ final filing is due 4 May 2027.

Power Pedro Alliana has been president since 6 November; ex-president Santiago Peña is in custody.

Power Index Paraguay ranks 10th of 14 in Paraguay ranks 10th of 14 in The Rio Times Latin America Power Index , with 35.0 points (November 2026 edition).

Paraguay has few firm dates in the Ueno Bank crisis: a payout window for savers, a court deadline in May 2027 and several open questions for the Senate and prosecutors.

Paraguay’s Ueno Bank crisis enters its second week on Monday 9 November with most of the next steps still undated. The firm dates are few: payouts to savers by the central bank (the BCP), a court deadline in May 2027, and open decisions on who will lead the BCP.

Ueno was a fast-growing digital bank with about 3 million customers, and the BCP took it over on 2 or 3 November. For US readers the stakes include a US$350 million bond sold to international investors in March, and a new president, Pedro Alliana, who met US Secretary of State Marco Rubio in Washington as vice president on 4 August.

Dates to Watch

Saturday 7 November Peña due to give a statement to prosecutors at 11:00 (reported).

From Monday 9 November Central bank payouts continue; the calendar for later groups is unconfirmed.

Wednesday 11 to Friday 13 November End of the five-business-day payout window, depending on how days are counted (unconfirmed).

Tuesday 17 or Wednesday 18 November Fifteen days after the central bank’s resolution (unconfirmed, see below).

Tuesday 4 May 2027 Prosecutors’ final filing in the Ueno Bank case, set by the court.

No date announced Senate vote on a permanent central bank chief, a judge’s hearing on Peña, Carvallo hearing, bondholder steps.

When Ueno Savers Get Paid

The BCP began paying deposit-guarantee advances this week, starting with savers who hold up to Gs 10 million (about US$1,673), owe Ueno nothing and have an account at another bank. We convert guaraní at Gs 5,976 per US$, the market close of Friday 6 November.

Follow this story Get an email when there’s news on Paraguay central bank Email address Follow Free. One email a day at most, and only when there is news. This also signs you up to our weekday newsletter, The LatAm Brief. Nothing arrives until you click the confirmation link, and you can stop either with one click. Privacy policy

The Paraguayan Banking Association, the industry body, has put the first round at up to five business days, and some reports tie that limit to the new law. Counted from Thursday 5 or Friday 6 November, it ends between Wednesday 11 and Friday 13 November, and we could not confirm the rule at the BCP or in the law’s text.

Congress also approved an emergency advance of up to 40 minimum monthly wages, the legal pay floor, or Gs 121.7 million (about US$20,400), payable within 24 hours of the law taking effect. This is a payment on account: the full guarantee stays at 75 minimum wages, or Gs 228.3 million (about US$38,200), per depositor and per institution.

The central bank says about 97% of depositors fall inside that limit, and it will set a calendar for balances above the first Gs 10 million. Paraguayan business reports say it has 15 days to finish the accounting that shows what is left for larger deposits, and that the board may extend the period.

That points to Tuesday 17 or Wednesday 18 November, depending on the start date. We could not check the deadline against the law’s text, so treat it as unconfirmed.

Our guide to whether your money is safe at Ueno Bank explains the groups and the paperwork. Paraguay Pays First Ueno Bank Savers covers the first day of payments.

Who Is Detained and What the Courts Do Next

At a hearing on Thursday 5 November, Judge Rodrigo Estigarribia ordered pretrial detention for Ueno’s Miguel Vázquez and five other executives, according to Paraguayan court reports. Two women executives were put under house arrest with electronic ankle monitors.

Prosecutors have charged 27 people, among them breach of trust and attempted fraud, and all of them are presumed innocent. The court set Tuesday 4 May 2027 for the prosecutors’ final filing in the case.

Former president Santiago Peña was removed by the Senate on Friday 6 November by 44 votes to 0, with one senator absent, for poor performance of his duties. His lawyers argue the trial was void, and he did not attend.

Prosecutors charged him in case 92/2026, “breach of trust and others”, and detained him that evening; they have asked for pretrial detention. Paraguay Ousts President, Then Detains Him has the full account.

Peña was moved around midnight to the Presidential Escort Regiment, the army unit that guards the presidency, and was due to give prosecutors a statement at 11:00 on Saturday 7 November. A judge must still decide on pretrial detention, and we found no hearing date.

Carlos Carvallo, the central bank president who resigned on 3 November, surrendered on Friday night under a prosecutors’ detention order, and reports say he was charged alongside Peña, as Paraguay’s Ex-Central Bank Chief Surrenders reports. We found no hearing date for him, and he has not been convicted of anything.

Who Leads the Central Bank

Pedro Acosta Bernal, a BCP board member, was named interim central bank president on Wednesday 4 November, after Carvallo and two directors resigned. Raúl Vera Bogado, whom Peña proposed as permanent chief, still needs Senate approval, and the Senate sent that nomination back to committee on 4 November.

With Peña removed, it is unclear whether Alliana will keep the nomination. Alliana has said those hurt by the bank’s closure will be compensated in full.

What It Means for Investors and US Readers

Ueno’s US$350 million of bonds due 2031 were sold in March to international investors. We found no public statement on how bondholders will be treated, so that date stays open.

Paraguay’s government debt is rated investment grade by Moody’s (Baa3) and S&P (BBB-) and one notch below by Fitch (BB+, positive outlook), and we found no rating action since the bank failed. The International Monetary Fund closed its yearly review of the economy on 28 August, and we found no IMF statement on Ueno; Paraguay Bond Risk Climbs After Bank Failure tracks the market reaction.

What Is Not Known

Several core facts are open: the exact date of the central bank’s resolution (2 or 3 November) and the final size of Ueno’s capital hole. How much state money is frozen at the bank is also disputed, and estimates differ widely.

Whether a judge will order Peña held before trial is also open. The payout calendar beyond the first group, the fate of the 2031 bonds and the Senate’s decision on the central bank chief also have no date.

Frequently Asked Questions

When will Ueno Bank savers get their money?

Advances of up to Gs 10 million (US$1,673) started this week. We found no published dates for larger balances, and a five-business-day limit for the first round is unconfirmed.

How much of my Ueno deposit is guaranteed?

The guarantee covers up to 75 minimum monthly wages, Gs 228.3 million (about US$38,200), per depositor and per institution. Congress approved an advance of up to Gs 121.7 million (about US$20,400) on account.

Is Santiago Peña in prison?

He was removed on 6 November, charged and detained that evening in a breach-of-trust case, and is held at a military unit. He has not been convicted, and a judge has yet to rule on pretrial detention.

Who runs Paraguay’s central bank now?

Pedro Acosta Bernal, a BCP board member, has been interim president since 4 November. The Senate has not approved a permanent chief.

Sources: Banco Central del Paraguay (deposit-guarantee communications), Ministerio Público (case 92/2026), the court hearing of 5 November 2026 and the Senate session of 6 November 2026, as relayed by Paraguayan media and cross-checked on 7 November 2026; US Department of State photo of 4 August 2026; market close of 6 November 2026 for the guaraní rate.

World.title: Paraguay’s New President Pedro Alliana
World.content:
Pedro Alliana, then vice president, in Asunción in August 2023. Photo: Shufu Liu / Office of the President of the Republic of China (Taiwan), CC BY 2.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

PARAGUAY · PROFILE

Published Saturday, 7 November, 6:00 a.m. ET · Source: Senate of Paraguay, public statements, market data

Paraguay has a new president, Pedro Alliana, a 52-year-old career politician from the ruling Colorado Party, Paraguay's dominant conservative party. He was sworn in on Friday 6 November 2026, hours after the Senate removed President Santiago Peña over the collapse of Ueno Bank, a private lender.

He inherits a frozen bank with nearly 3 million customers, a party that has split in public and a term that runs to August 2028. For US readers, Paraguay is a soy and beef exporter, so how steady its government is matters to anyone with money or contracts there.

Key Facts Rio Times membership Read everything we publish for US$1 in the first month. Then US$8.99 a month. Cancel anytime. Start for US$1 Prediction markets The prediction platform Polymarket prices Alliana at 11.0% to win the 2028 election, as of 6:04 a.m. ET, 7 November.

Who Hércules Pedro Lorenzo Alliana Rodríguez, 52, born in Pilar; ex-governor, ex-deputy, vice president since August 2023.

What Sworn in as president on Friday 6 November 2026, after the Senate removed Santiago Peña.

Term He serves out the 2023 to 2028 term, which ends in August 2028.

First orders He promised action to compensate Ueno Bank savers and told ministers to travel abroad only when unavoidable.

Open As of Saturday morning, no new central bank head or full cabinet was confirmed.

Who Is Pedro Alliana?

Hércules Pedro Lorenzo Alliana Rodríguez was born on 19 February 1974 in Pilar, a river town in the southern department of Ñeembucú, which is Paraguay's word for a province. He was governor of Ñeembucú from 2008 to 2013.

He then won a seat in the Chamber of Deputies, the lower house of Congress.

A Career Built Inside the Colorado Party

The Colorado Party, formally the National Republican Association (ANR), has been Alliana's political home throughout. He sat in the chamber from 2013 to 2023 and led it until 2022.

Latin America Power Index · November 2026 edition Paraguay ranks 10th of 14 with 35.0 points. Strongest pillar: state capacity & security (55); weakest: future resources (13). Alignment group: Closer to Washington. See the full index, the business lens and the data →

He also served as party president until January 2023. In December 2018 he was diagnosed with leukaemia.

From Running Mate to President

Horacio Cartes, a former president who leads the party, backed the Peña and Alliana ticket in 2023. Alliana became vice president on 15 August 2023.

In October 2026 the party's dominant wing, known as Honor Colorado, split in public, and Alliana and Cartes ended up on opposite sides, according to Paraguayan reports. How deep the rift runs is not clear.

On Thursday 5 November the Chamber of Deputies rejected an impeachment motion against Alliana himself. For the full story of the removal, see our report on the Senate vote and the oath and our earlier piece on the Cartes ticket dispute.

His First Orders

Basilio Núñez, president of the Senate, swore him in before Congress on Friday 6 November. Both chambers then elected Antonio Barrios, a senator, as vice president by a unanimous show of hands, according to the Senate.

Alliana said people hurt by the bank's collapse would not be abandoned and ordered immediate action to compensate savers, with priority for the least well-off. He told ministers to travel abroad only for “unpostponable” reasons, and promised to cut superfluous spending.

Separately, the central bank has announced advances for Ueno depositors, according to reports. Savers can claim up to 10 million guaraníes (Gs 10 million, US$1,673), and an emergency law approved by Congress adds an advance of about Gs 121 million (about US$20,200) from the state deposit guarantee fund, which insures bank deposits; the rate is Gs 5,976 per US$, the market close on 6 November (see our payout explainer).

What Prediction Markets Say

Polymarket, a crypto-based prediction platform, lists the 2028 Paraguayan presidential election. At 6:04 a.m. ET on Saturday 7 November Senate president Basilio Núñez led at 19.5%, followed by another candidate at 18.5%, while Alliana was fifth at 11.0%.

Only US$11,994 has been traded on the market, so these are thin bets rather than polls. Why we show this: prediction markets turn real-money bets into a live probability that moves within minutes of the news, which is why investors, campaigns and newsrooms in the United States now follow them closely.

We show them next to polls and official results, never instead of them.

The Risks He Inherits

Ueno itself is the first test, since its collapse froze the accounts of nearly 3 million customers, including pension funds. The size of the hole in its books is still disputed.

The currency is the second. The dollar gained 5.5% on the guaraní, Paraguay's currency, in the week to Friday, rising from Gs 5,664 to Gs 5,976 per US$, according to market closes (see our currency report).

What It Means for US Readers

If you hold Paraguayan assets or money at Ueno, three signals matter most: who leads the central bank, how fast the guarantee payouts run, and what happens to Peña's case. Exporters and investors will read a quiet first fortnight as a sign the government can govern.

Our guide to who holds power in Paraguay explains the system. Our report on the surrender of the former central bank chief covers the banking side.

What Is Not Known

We could not confirm who will lead the central bank after Carlos Carvallo, the former central bank president, stepped down, or which ministers will stay. Live reports said Alliana was due to sign decrees confirming or naming ministers, but we saw none signed as of Saturday morning.

Reports differ on where Peña is being held, and we could not confirm when he will face a judge. We found no reaction yet from the US government or the International Monetary Fund.

Frequently Asked Questions

Who is Pedro Alliana?

Alliana, 52, is Paraguay's president since 6 November 2026. He was vice president from August 2023, after serving as governor of Ñeembucú and a deputy.

How long will Alliana be president?

He completes the 2023 to 2028 term, which ends in August 2028. The Senate says he was sworn in to complete that period.

Why did Peña lose the presidency?

The Senate found Peña guilty of poor performance of his duties after the Ueno Bank collapse. Forty-four senators voted to remove him on 6 November, and the Senate describes the vote as unanimous among those present.

Will Ueno Bank customers get their money?

Alliana promised action to compensate savers. The central bank has announced advances to depositors, but the full schedule and the size of the hole are not yet known.

Sources: Senate of Paraguay, swearing-in and removal reports, read 7 November 2026; Polymarket market data, read 7 November 2026; market closes for the guaraní, 2 and 6 November 2026.

World.title: Paraguay Bond Risk Climbs After Bank Failure
World.content:
PARAGUAY · UENO BANK CASE

Key Facts RT Ask Rio Times 17 years of Latin America reporting, on demand. Ask Answers are generated from Rio Times reporting only — every claim links to its source article. Open the full Ask Rio Times → RT Ask Rio TimesCost of living, safety, visas across Latin America › RT Ask Rio Times 17 years of Latin America reporting, on demand. × Best for expats Cost of living Safest places Easy visas Tap a question, or type your own — the answer appears right here. Ask Open the full Ask Rio Times → The market After digital lender Ueno Bank failed, Paraguay’s bond spread (extra yield over US Treasuries) touched 1.57 percentage points.

The ratings Rating agency Moody’s affirmed Paraguay’s investment-grade rating with a stable outlook in July.

The IMF The International Monetary Fund called Paraguay’s risks balanced on 28 August; nothing since on Ueno Bank.

The US US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent met President Santiago Peña on 22 October, under two weeks before the takeover.

Brazil and Argentina Brazil’s Lula wished new president Alliana success on 6 November; Argentina’s government made no comment.

Power Index Paraguay ranks 10th of 14 in Paraguay ranks 10th of 14 in The Rio Times Latin America Power Index , with 35.0 points (November 2026 edition).

Prediction markets Prediction market Polymarket gives new President Pedro Alliana 11% to win the next election (7 November, 5:40 a.m. ET).

Paraguay’s bank collapse has lifted the cost of its debt but, so far, drawn no public response from the IMF or the US Treasury that we could find, while Brazil’s Lula has welcomed the new president.

Paraguay’s Ueno Bank failure is so far a national credit shock, not a regional one. Investors now charge Paraguay more to borrow, yet neither the US Treasury nor the International Monetary Fund (IMF), the lender of last resort for countries in trouble, has said anything public that we could find.

That matters to US readers because Paraguay is a Washington partner and the Brazilian neighbour that shares the Itaipú hydroelectric dam. The Senate removed President Peña on Friday 6 November, and Vice President Pedro Alliana took over until 2028, as our report on his removal explains.

Latin America Power Index · November 2026 edition Paraguay ranks 10th of 14 with 35.0 points. Strongest pillar: state capacity & security (55); weakest: future resources (13). Alignment group: Closer to Washington. See the full index, the business lens and the data →

Investors Charged More but Kept Paraguay Investment Grade

The clearest gauge of outside confidence is the spread on Paraguay’s dollar bonds, measured by the EMBI index of emerging-market dollar bonds from US bank JPMorgan. It is the extra yield investors demand over US Treasuries, counted in basis points, where one basis point is a hundredth of a percentage point.

The spread closed at about 143 to 146 basis points on Thursday 5 November, after touching 157 during the day. Reports put the level before the crisis at about 119, so the rise is roughly 25 points.

That is a repricing, not a rout: investors want roughly a quarter of a percentage point more a year to hold Paraguayan debt. Before the crisis, Paraguay had won an investment-grade rating from Moody’s, which affirmed it with a stable outlook in July.

Washington Has Ties to Peña but Treasury Is Silent

The US Treasury’s readout of Bessent’s meeting with Peña on Thursday 22 October described a “growing economic partnership” and welcomed Paraguay’s commitment to secure critical minerals supply chains. The meeting came less than two weeks before the central bank, the Banco Central del Paraguay, took over Ueno Bank.

We found no statement on Ueno Bank, Peña’s removal or Alliana in US Treasury releases through Friday 6 November. Ueno Bank, a fast-growing digital lender with about 2.9 million clients, was the bank the central bank took over this week.

Brazil Welcomes Alliana, Argentina Stays Silent

Brazil’s tie to Paraguay runs through Itaipú, the hydroelectric dam on the Paraná River that the two countries own together, as our explainer on Paraguay’s foreign players shows. Talks to revise the dam’s financial annex, which sets how its power is priced and shared, have run through 2026, and we found no published deal.

Brazil’s President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva congratulated Alliana on Friday 6 November, wished him full success and said he wants to host him in Brasília; his message did not mention Peña. Argentina’s government under President Javier Milei also made no public comment that we found through Friday night, though Paraguay, Brazil and Argentina belong to the same trade bloc, Mercosur.

The IMF Saw Balanced Risks Before the Collapse

The IMF’s Executive Board closed its annual Article IV consultation, a regular health check of a member’s economy, on Friday 28 August. It judged the risks to Paraguay’s outlook “balanced” and put the banking system’s total capital ratio at 17.3%, against a 12% minimum.

That figure covers the whole system, not Ueno, whose own solvency ratio fell below half of its legal minimum before the central bank stepped in. The release does not mention deposit insurance or bank resolution, and we found no IMF statement on the crisis or any Paraguayan request for fund money.

Alliana has promised to compensate affected savers. The cost of that promise to the state budget is not yet public.

The Case Against Calm

Spreads may understate the risk, because the central bank’s governor has resigned and the final bill for Ueno is unknown. If compensation adds to public debt, it could also complicate the IMF’s call to restore the legal deficit limit by 2028.

A larger bill could draw scrutiny from the rating agencies. For now, the outcome rests on how much the state must pay and how fast it moves.

What It Means for You

For holders of Paraguayan dollar bonds, the signals to watch are the size of the depositor bill and any move by a rating agency. For readers with money or plans in Paraguay, the near-term risk is local, in bank access and the guaraní, Paraguay’s currency, which we cover in our report on the currency.

The wider political backdrop is in our report on the former central bank chief. Our guide to who holds power in Paraguay explains the players.

What Prediction Markets Say

Polymarket, an online prediction market, had US$11,954 traded across the whole market as of 5:40 a.m. ET on 7 November on who wins Paraguay’s next presidential election. It prices Alliana, who took office on 6 November, at about 11%; these are bets, not polls.

Why we show this: prediction markets turn real-money bets into a live probability that moves within minutes of the news, which is why investors, campaigns and newsrooms in the United States now follow them closely. We show them next to polls and official results, never instead of them.

What Is Not Known

We could not establish whether the US State Department or the IMF has commented, or whether Argentina’s government will. A US embassy message urging calm on 6 November was reported, but we could not confirm it at a primary source.

Early reports differ widely on how much state money is frozen at Ueno, and we found no final figure. Also open are the cost of resolving Ueno and whether Brazil and Paraguay will settle the Itaipú annex.

The exact date of the takeover is reported as 2 or 3 November.

Frequently Asked Questions

Has the IMF commented on Paraguay’s Ueno Bank crisis?

We found no IMF statement on it. The fund’s board closed its yearly 2026 review of Paraguay on 28 August and called the risks to the outlook balanced.

How much did Paraguay’s bond risk rise?

The JPMorgan EMBI spread closed at about 143 to 146 basis points on 5 November, after touching 157. Reports put it at about 119 before the crisis.

Has Brazil reacted to the change of president?

President Lula congratulated Alliana on 6 November and said he wants to host him in Brasília. His message did not mention Peña.

Has the US government reacted to Peña’s removal?

We found no Treasury or State Department statement through 6 November. The Treasury Secretary had met Peña on 22 October to discuss economic cooperation.

Sources: US Treasury Department readout of 22 October 2026 (home.treasury.gov); IMF Press Release No. 26/280 of 28 August 2026 (imf.org); JPMorgan EMBI spread data for 5 November 2026; Polymarket market data, 7 November 2026 (polymarket.com/event/paraguay-presidential-election-winner).

World.title: Is Your Money Safe at Paraguay’s Ueno Bank?
World.content:
File photo, 2010: the Banco Central del Paraguay building in Asunción, the capital. Photo: FF MM, CC BY-SA 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

PARAGUAY · BANKING GUIDE

Published Saturday, 7 November 2026, 5:40 a.m. ET · Source: Central Bank of Paraguay communiqués, deposit guarantee law

Savers at Paraguay’s failed Ueno Bank are getting their money back in stages, and the guarantee covers balances up to 228.3 million guaraníes (about US$38,200) per person. How soon you are paid depends on your balance and on whether you owe Ueno anything.

By early Saturday 7 November 2026, the Central Bank of Paraguay (BCP) said it had started paying a first group (balances up to 10 million guaraníes, about US$1,670) and a second group (up to 121.76 million guaraníes, about US$20,400). Everyone with more is still waiting for dates the BCP has not published.

Key Facts First group Balances up to 10 million guaraníes (about US$1,670), no Ueno debt, an account at another bank.

Second group Balances above that, up to 121.76 million guaraníes (about US$20,400), same conditions.

Legal cap 228.3 million guaraníes (about US$38,200) per depositor, per institution, however many accounts you hold.

Deadline The BCP says the advance process may not exceed five business days from 5 November.

Power Index Paraguay ranks 10th of 14 in Paraguay ranks 10th of 14 in The Rio Times Latin America Power Index , with 35.0 points (November 2026 edition).

The Central Bank of Paraguay is paying Ueno Bank savers in groups: small balances first, larger ones later, and amounts above the legal cap with no promised date.

What Happened to Ueno Bank

Ueno Bank is a Paraguayan digital lender that the BCP took over in the first days of November 2026, after its solvency ratio (a measure of whether a bank can absorb losses) fell below half the legal minimum. Nearly three million clients lost access to their accounts, cards and app.

Paraguay’s prosecutor’s office has formally accused 27 people, and President Santiago Peña was removed by the Senate on Friday 6 November, as we reported. The payout rules below come from a 2003 deposit-insurance law (Law 2334/03) and a new law approved this week.

Latin America Power Index · November 2026 edition Paraguay ranks 10th of 14 with 35.0 points. Strongest pillar: state capacity & security (55); weakest: future resources (13). Alignment group: Closer to Washington. See the full index, the business lens and the data →

In Plain English BCP The Central Bank of Paraguay, the national regulator that took control of Ueno.

FGD The Deposit Guarantee Fund, an insurance pool that repays savers when a bank fails.

Advance A part-payment now against the full guarantee, so savers do not wait for the whole process.

Guaraní Paraguay’s currency. We use 5,976 per US$, the 6 November 2026 close (RT market data).

Who Gets Paid, How Much and When

The BCP pays through the FGD in groups, and all limits apply per depositor, not per account. A depositor who holds several accounts at Ueno shares one limit across all of them.

Payout Groups Group 1 Total deposits up to 10 million guaraníes (about US$1,670), no debts to Ueno, and an active account at another Paraguayan bank or finance company. Savers under that line get everything back, and payments began on Thursday 5 November.

Group 2 Demand deposits (everyday accounts) above 10 million and up to 121.76 million guaraníes (about US$20,400), no debts to Ueno (loans, cards or other products), and an account at another bank. The BCP said it had started paying this group by early Saturday 7 November.

Later groups No date and no schedule yet. The BCP says the payment method for the next groups will be published “soon” on its official channels.

The 121.76 million figure equals 40 monthly minimum wages, the advance the new law allows. The full guarantee is 75 minimum wages, or 228.3 million guaraníes (about US$38,200), at the minimum wage of 3,044,000 guaraníes (about US$509) in force since 1 July 2026.

The BCP says payments start within 24 hours of the resolution and the process may not exceed five business days from 5 November, which on our count ends on Wednesday 11 November. Under the earlier rule the fund had 15 calendar days, extendable once.

For savers under the cap, the guarantee covers the full balance. For them the question is timing, not loss.

How to Claim Your Money

There is no counter queue and no form to post. The BCP says payment is made automatically into an account, and your job is to find out which bank it names for you.

Check your email and phone. The BCP says it writes to the email address you registered with Ueno. It also contacts the phone numbers registered with Ueno. Look up your status. Enter your ID number at bcp.gov.py/fgd-pagos, which the BCP says is updated gradually. An empty result on day one is not a refusal. Note the bank named for you and download its app. Payment is credited to an account, not paid in cash at a window. Know where the money lands. Savers with no other account are meant to get one opened for them, but groups 1 and 2 require an existing account. No timing has been given for the rest. Pay nobody. The BCP and the paying banks will not ask for passwords, account data or money to open an account or release the fund.

What Happens to Money Above the Limit

The guarantee stops at 228.3 million guaraníes (about US$38,200) per depositor at each institution. The BCP has published no schedule, no amount and no promise for repaying balances above that ceiling.

Debts matter too. The BCP says overdue debts to Ueno are deducted from the advance, yet the first two groups are open only to savers with no debts at all, and the rules do not say how the two statements fit together.

Foreign and Corporate Depositors

Savers who held dollars at Ueno are repaid in guaraníes under the fund’s rules, and the BCP has not said which exchange rate it will use. The guarantee makes no distinction between Paraguayans and foreigners, but groups 1 and 2 require an account at another Paraguayan bank.

Persons and companies linked to Ueno are excluded from the guarantee. The BCP says they must return any money improperly received within 24 hours.

What It Means for You

If you banked at Ueno, the practical order is simple: watch your email, check the BCP page, and move nothing until you know your assigned bank. A US reader with a Paraguayan dollar account should expect a guaraní payout, so the exchange rate on the day matters; the guaraní closed at 5,976 per US$ on Friday 6 November, weaker than 5,875 a day earlier (RT market data).

Background: the first payout announcement, the central bank chief’s resignation, his surrender to prosecutors and the guaraní slide. More from Paraguay.

What Is Not Known

When groups 3 and later will be paid, and what rules apply to balances between 121.76 million and 228.3 million guaraníes (about US$20,400 to US$38,200).

How debts to Ueno are treated: deducted from the advance, or a bar to payment in groups 1 and 2.

How many savers have been paid so far and how much the fund has disbursed.

Whether fixed-term deposit certificates are in group 2, which is described as covering demand deposits.

How foreign residents without a Paraguayan account will be paid, and which exchange rate applies to dollar balances.

What share of balances above the cap can be recovered, and when.

Frequently Asked Questions

Is my money safe at Ueno Bank?

Up to 228.3 million guaraníes (about US$38,200) per depositor, per institution, is guaranteed. Amounts above it have no repayment date.

When will I get my money back from Ueno Bank?

Balances up to 121.76 million guaraníes (about US$20,400) are being paid in two groups, with debt-free savers who hold an account elsewhere first. The BCP says the advance process may not exceed five business days from 5 November.

What if I have more than 228.3 million guaraníes at Ueno?

The guarantee does not cover the excess. The BCP has published no schedule or promise for such balances.

Are foreign depositors and companies covered?

Yes. Nationality makes no difference, the cap applies per depositor and institution, and dollar deposits are repaid in guaraníes. Persons linked to Ueno are excluded.

How do I know a message about my payout is real?

The BCP publishes status at bcp.gov.py/fgd-pagos. It and the paying banks will not ask for passwords, account data or money.

Sources: Central Bank of Paraguay (BCP), deposit guarantee payment communiqués, 4 to 7 November 2026, bcp.gov.py; Law 2334/03 on the Deposit Guarantee Fund; Ministry of Labour (MTESS), minimum wage resolution 670/2026; RT market data, guaraní close of 6 November 2026. Read on 7 November 2026.
